Farah finds the blue bobbin and asks you to watch the edge for a day if you want to learn how the sisters divide the work. Zuleika shifts her seat to make room.
ev.cotan.b.choice.silk: Buy the finished silk bolt for 100 silver
ev.cotan.b.choice.weave: Stay a day to learn the sisters’ loom work
ev.cotan.b.title: The Missing Blue Thread
ev.cotan.c.body:
Beyond a watered field outside Khotan, farmer Rahman is clearing sand from the low wall that holds his channel in place. His mother brings him a painted pottery fragment she found after the last wind. ‘It came from our field,’ she says, ‘and I kept it so the children could see the colour.’ Rahman wants to set a support beside the wall before the next water turn. His mother warns him not to place a heavy stone over a patch of older brick that has begun to crumble.

You ask what stood here before the fields. She has heard neighbours talk of older religious buildings in this part of the oasis, but she knows only the pieces found by their family. The younger child asks whether the painted curve is a hand. She says it might be; the piece is too small to tell. Rahman asks you to help measure the firm ground where a support can stand.

Rahman sets his measuring cord against the firm ground. His mother gives the children a clay cup to carry water and asks them to stay clear of the wet wall.
ev.cotan.c.choice.explore: Spend three days repairing and studying the old wall
ev.cotan.c.choice.fragment: Accept the painted fragment from the family’s basket
ev.cotan.c.choice.listen_elder: Listen to Rahman’s mother speak of the field
ev.cotan.c.title: The Wall Beneath the Field
ev.cotan.entry.body:
At Khotan’s entry yard, clerk Samira is trying to keep a wet cargo register from curling. Her younger brother brings it inside, but a river washer follows him with two pebbles in his palm. ‘You have written my name beside the merchant’s pack,’ he tells her. Samira checks the marks. The merchant owns the sealed jade lot; the washer merely helped carry it from the riverbank. She asks both men to sign the corrected line.

You ask where travellers rest. Samira points to houses near a water channel and says the river washer can show you the safest place to fill a jar today. The merchant opens a corner of his pack and offers a full trading lot of jade for 135 silver. Her brother asks if the stone is all from this river. ‘Different hands have gathered it,’ the merchant answers, ‘and that is why we keep names.’

Samira invites you to stay two days and learn the register. Her brother wants to show you their mother’s collection of old river stones tomorrow. The washer holds out a jar of clear water; Samira’s brother takes a sip, then asks for the path to the channel.
ev.cotan.entry.choice.customs: Stay two days to learn the river register
ev.cotan.entry.choice.lore: Spend a day seeing the family’s river stones
ev.cotan.entry.choice.market: Buy the sealed jade lot for 135 silver
ev.cotan.entry.title: The River Register at Khotan
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.body:
At a well beside the river road, keeper Mahmud has laid out three clay cups. His daughter says travellers keep confusing the cup for rinsing hands with the ones for drinking. ‘Then I should mark the handles,’ he says. She points out that the cups have no handles. He laughs and asks her to find a piece of coloured cord instead. A river washer arrives to fill a jar and waits until they finish.

You ask how much water is left after the washing families draw their share. Mahmud shows you the depth mark inside the well wall and explains who checks it each morning. His daughter says yesterday’s mark was hard to see in the shade, so she has placed a small lamp nearby. Mahmud asks her to move it farther from the rope before someone knocks it in. The washer offers a stone to keep the lamp steady.

Mahmud invites you to stay a day and watch how the well is shared. The daughter has already tied a blue cord around the drinking cup and wants you to tell her whether it is easy to see.
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.choice_1: Ask Mahmud how to plan the next water stop
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.choice_1_result: Mahmud asks how many people and animals travel with you, then points out where you should refill before the next dry stretch. His daughter offers the blue-marked cup while you listen. You know whom to ask if you return to this well.
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.choice_2: Spend a day recording the well’s turns
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.choice_2_result: You stay a day and write down when the washer, the nearby families, and the passing caravans use the well. Mahmud’s daughter checks the depth mark at dusk and finds it easy to see beside the moved lamp. Mahmud asks you to come back for the morning reading if you wish.
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.choice_3_result: You thank Mahmud and continue. His daughter hands the washer the cup with the blue cord, then catches herself and swaps it for the washing cup. ‘Good thing I can see the mark,’ she says, and her father smiles.
ev.cotan.mentor_closure.title: The Well Keeper’s Table
ev.cotan.twoscripts.body:
In a courtyard near the market, an older woman named Dilara is teaching her grandson to copy the names on a crate of cotton cloth. The seller wrote one name in the family’s hand and another in the script the next carrier can read. Her grandson thinks they name two different owners. ‘Look at the pack number,’ Dilara says. He finds the same mark beneath both lines and asks why the names still look so different.

You ask who taught her the second script. Dilara says a former neighbour carried letters east and showed her how to write addresses clearly. The boy wants to send his own note to an aunt who moved away, but he is embarrassed by his uneven letters. Dilara gives him a spare label and tells him to begin with her name. A carrier arrives to collect the cloth and says he can wait while the boy practises one line.

Dilara offers to pay 0.8 silver if you spend the day helping her check other cargo labels. Her grandson also invites you to sit for a short lesson and see how he writes his aunt’s name.
ev.cotan.twoscripts.choice.learn: Sit with Dilara and the boy to compare the two scripts
ev.cotan.twoscripts.choice.work: Stay a day checking the cargo labels
ev.cotan.twoscripts.result.learn: Dilara shows you how the pack number holds the two versions of the name together. The boy copies his aunt’s name again and asks you which line is easier to read. You note their method; the carrier accepts the corrected crate when he is done.
ev.cotan.twoscripts.result.work: You spend the day comparing names and pack marks with Dilara. The carrier takes each crate only after her grandson reads the label aloud. She pays you 0.8 silver, and the boy slips his carefully written note for his aunt into the right bundle.
ev.cotan.twoscripts.title: The Two Names on the Crate
ev.ctesiphon.entry.body:
The old brick arch rises above low walls and open ground. A family has set a shade cloth beside the ruins. A girl sits beneath it with a bowl of mortar, helping her father patch their small shelter.

She says her grandmother used to walk farther than anyone in the family and always stopped here to drink before taking the road to Baghdad. The girl has never made that whole journey. She asks you how far a traveller can go with a full skin of water, then laughs when her father reminds her that everyone drinks at a different pace.

She asks her father where the family will put the second water jar once the shelter wall is finished. ‘Inside the shade, where the clay stays cool,’ he says. You ask whether they sell water to travellers. The girl shakes her head: neighbours share the well, and her father offers a cup when someone stops. He tells her to rinse the cup first; she runs to the jar and returns with it dripping. From the road, a cart driver calls a greeting. She recognises him and asks whether his mother has recovered from her cough. He promises to tell her after he has watered the animals.
ev.ctesiphon.entry.choice.rest: Rest for a day under the shade cloth
ev.ctesiphon.entry.title: At the Great Arch
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.body:
Farid’s daughter has found a brick with her grandmother’s old mark on it. She wants it at the new doorway, where everyone can see it, but the stone step has to be levelled first. Farid can do that after his work tomorrow.

‘She used to stand there and make us wash our feet before coming in,’ the girl says. Farid brings out a length of cord to measure the step. His daughter keeps the marked brick beside her and asks whether he remembers which room Grandmother carried it from.

‘From the little room behind the oven,’ Farid says. ‘She said the mark would help us find it again.’ The girl asks whether the oven still stands. It does, but the room around it has been repaired more than once. You ask how the brick survived. Farid says his mother kept useful pieces under the shade cloth until she had a place for them. The girl rubs dust from the old mark and asks him to leave that side facing the doorway. A neighbour calls from the lane that the mat is ready; Farid tells her to bring it tomorrow, once the mortar has had a night to set.
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.choice.fit: Spend a day helping fit the step
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.choice.listen: Sit and listen to her stories
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.result.fit: You spend the day levelling the step with Farid. His daughter places the marked brick at the edge and walks through the doorway twice to test it. The family thanks you warmly, and your name becomes familiar here.
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.result.listen: She tells you how her grandmother once arrived home with a soaked loaf hidden under her coat, after giving her dry bread to another traveller. Farid laughs and brings out tea. You rest in the shade and recover some strength.
ev.ctesiphon.shelter.title: Grandmother’s Door Brick
ev.damascus.dyework.body:
Two lengths of blue cloth hang at the dyer's door. His apprentice, Layla, begins to roll one up, but a woman stops her. “Wait. My mother stitched a little red thread into the edge.”

Layla searches and cannot find it. Rain sent both customers' cloth indoors last night. In the morning the marks were hidden under the new blue dye. The woman, Samiya, brought a length her mother had kept. She plans to make a new coat for her younger brother when he returns from his travels. As a boy, he wore a robe their mother had sewn, and Samiya wants to keep that little stitch in his new coat.

The master comes over from the dye vat and feels the corner. “The thread is still there. When the cloth dries a little, we'll all look.” Samiya puts her sewing box on a stool and helps Layla work along the hem. Layla looks up at you. “You have good eyes. Will you check the other side? I'd hate to send her home empty handed.”
ev.damascus.dyework.choice.help: Help Layla look for the red thread
ev.damascus.dyework.choice.route: Ask how Samiya's brother travels back from Tyre
ev.damascus.dyework.result.help:
You spread the hem beside the window. In the light you see a red thread tucked into a small repair. Samiya lifts the loose end with her nail and recognizes her mother's stitch.

Layla brings her some water and asks her to return once the cloth is fully dry. The master thanks you for helping. On her way out, Samiya laughs that her brother will probably complain that the sleeves are too long. You leave knowing a few more people in Damascus.
ev.damascus.dyework.result.route:
As she searches the cloth, Samiya tells you her brother travels with a caravan from Tyre. She knows the stretch along the coast and the turn inland toward Damascus. She even describes the green-painted cart he rides beside.

Layla finds the red thread and calls her over. Samiya holds the corner up to the light. “When he comes home, I'll make him try the coat on first.” You thank her and mark Tyre and the road on your map.
ev.damascus.dyework.title: A Piece of Blue Cloth
ev.damascus.entry.body:
As you enter Damascus, Nura is wrapping a narrow-necked bottle in soft cloth. Her nephew stands beside her stall, holding half of a broken stopper and stamping his foot.

“What will we do with the bottle for Mother?” he asks. “She leaves with the caravan tomorrow.”

Nura dries the neck and finds a new stopper. “Hold it for me. Your mother wants a little of home to take to Tripoli. Once I change the stopper, she can carry it.”

Her nephew says his mother lived in Mizza as a child. Every summer she ran to the rosewater workshops to smell the petals. Nura laughs. “She used to put her nose against the door. The maker called her back so she wouldn't burn herself.”

Nura presses in the new stopper and turns the bottle upside down. The cloth stays dry. She sees you beside the stall and asks whether you would like to rest. Her nephew has already picked up the basket to take the bottle to his mother.
ev.damascus.entry.choice.look: Help Nura's nephew deliver the rosewater and ask about the Tripoli road
ev.damascus.entry.choice.pass: Ask Nura which gate to take and continue your journey
ev.damascus.entry.title: Damascus
ev.delli.battuta_a.body:
At a grain courtyard in Delhi, Shirin has laid a damp register beneath a cloth weight. Rain blurred several household marks before the morning distribution. Her daughter Safiya brings an empty sack and asks, ‘Did Uncle Rahim get his share?’ Shirin holds the page toward the light. ‘I can see his name. I cannot tell whether I wrote one measure or two.’ The old clerk at the next table says he still has the wooden tally from yesterday, but his hands are busy weighing the next family’s grain.

You ask why everyone is waiting in the yard. ‘If I guess at a number, somebody will go home short,’ Shirin says. Safiya offers to carry the register to her uncle; her mother stops her because the wet ink may smear again. A trader waiting with the other families says his pack animals leave for Cambay after noon. He has used these grain yards on the westward road and can name the places where travellers find water.

Shirin asks you to hold down the page while she brings the tally over. Safiya points to the mark beside her uncle’s name, and the clerk squints at it before he answers.
ev.delli.battuta_a.choice.ask: Help Shirin explain the corrected shares to the families
ev.delli.battuta_a.choice.court: Spend a day asking the trader about the road to Cambay
ev.delli.battuta_a.choice.pyre: Help compare the tally and the register for a day
ev.delli.battuta_a.title: The Courtyard Register
ev.delli.battuta_b.body:
At a travellers’ house in Delhi, keeper Bibi Hina is sorting two bundles of letters before their carriers leave. Her nephew marked one bundle for the westward caravan and the other for the long eastern road, then set both beneath a leaking roof tile. ‘I know which cloth I used,’ he says, ‘but the ink on the tags has run.’ Hina has him open the outer wraps and read the names aloud before anyone takes a letter away.

You ask who will carry the westward bundle. A driver bound toward Cambay raises his hand from the doorway; his sister lives near a stopping place on that road. The eastern carrier says the route toward Khotan takes many changes of hands, so each address must be clear. Hina asks whether he has enough dry cloth to rewrap it. He shows her a single piece and admits he had saved the rest for his own bedding. She sends her nephew to fetch another piece from the storeroom.

A family has arrived looking for a room, and Hina must settle them before dark. She asks you to hold the letters in order while her nephew brings back the dry wrapping.
ev.delli.battuta_b.choice.embassy: Spend a day preparing the eastern letters and road list
ev.delli.battuta_b.choice.gwalior: Spend a day with the westward driver and learn the Cambay road
ev.delli.battuta_b.choice.house: Stay a day helping Hina settle the guests
ev.delli.battuta_b.title: The Two Road Bundles
ev.delli.entry.body:
At a Delhi water yard, a carrier is marking household jars with a bit of chalk. His younger sister has just returned from a lane where two neighbours share the same doorway. She put the full jar at the wrong threshold and wants to fetch it back before either household starts supper. ‘Read the mark to me,’ her brother says, holding out the empty jar. She does, then notices that rain has blurred the chalk.

You ask whether the two families will mind. ‘They know us,’ she says, ‘but one has a sick child and needs the water first.’ Her brother takes a fresh piece of chalk and draws a wider sign. A caravan scribe waiting nearby asks if they can fill his skin as well. He is copying a long route list toward Khotan, with many stops between Delhi and that far-off city, and needs water before the drivers leave.

The sister carries the corrected jar to the sick child’s home and returns for the other. Her brother asks the scribe to hold the chalk while he fills the skin. The scribe looks at you and says he can show you his route list after the water is delivered.
ev.delli.entry.choice.look: Stay a day and read the long Khotan route list
ev.delli.entry.title: The Water Carrier’s Chalk Mark
ev.delli.jarbands.body:
In the water yard, a young potter is tying a blue thread around a household jar. Her aunt ordered two of the same size, one for drinking water and one for washing, and wants the family to tell them apart at a glance. The potter has only enough thread for one full loop. Her little cousin suggests painting a mark on the other; the potter worries the paint will rub off when the jar is carried.

You ask why the aunt did not choose different shapes. ‘They have to fit the same shelf,’ the girl says. Her cousin fetches a scrap of red cloth and asks whether it will last longer than paint. The aunt arrives with a carrying pole, sets the jars side by side, and has both children lift them. One handle catches on the pole. She asks the potter to smooth it before she takes either home.

The potter can pay you 0.6 silver if you stay the day to help finish and test the jars. If you are leaving soon, she will show you how she tests the handles and marks vessels for the family.
ev.delli.jarbands.choice.finish: Stay a day and help finish the jars
ev.delli.jarbands.choice.learn: Watch how the family marks and tests jars
ev.delli.jarbands.result.finish: You spend the day helping smooth the handle and testing both jars on the pole. The aunt chooses blue thread for drinking water and red cloth for washing. The potter pays you 0.6 silver before they carry the jars home.
ev.delli.jarbands.result.learn: The potter lets you feel the rough spot beneath the handle before she smooths it. Her aunt shows why the pole catches there, and the cousin ties on the red cloth. You record the small craft of keeping the two jars distinct.
ev.delli.jarbands.title: The Blue Thread on the Jar
ev.dongola.entry.body: At Dongola, a caravan has halted near the river while a woman repairs a strap on a water carrier's shoulder. Her son points to the church beyond the houses. “Grandfather said there are pictures older than his father inside.” The woman smiles. “There are. Go and ask the reader which ones he can show you.” A church reader comes out with a bucket and asks the boy to carry it. You ask where the road turns toward the next station. He points past the ferry, then asks whether you have enough water for the dry stretch. The woman feels the weight of your skin and says it should be filled before departure. Inside the church, painted figures remain from earlier generations, but the reader is busy patching a small leak in the roof today. The boy returns with his bucket, proud that he has been trusted with it, and asks whether you will stay to hear the reader's account after the work is done.
ev.dongola.entry.choice.pass: Ask the way onward and continue
ev.dongola.entry.choice.rest: Rest at the station for a day
ev.dongola.entry.title: A Water Carrier at Dongola
ev.dongola.garden.body: A woman tends a small garden above the river landing. Her nephew has brought seeds from a relative upriver but cannot remember which packet holds the beans and which holds the gourds. “Your aunt drew them on the paper,” she says. He opens the bundle; rain has blurred the drawings. She puts a seed from each packet in his palm and asks him to look at their shapes. He recognizes the beans, then admits he has already sown some in the wrong bed. You ask whether they must dig them out. “We can wait until they come up,” she says. “For today, help me keep the fresh water in the bed we know.” The little channel to it has filled with sand. The nephew fetches a wooden scoop, and a ferry passenger offers to carry the remaining seeds into the shade. The woman asks you to stay long enough to see which sprouts appear.
ev.dongola.garden.choice.channel: Clear the water channel with them
ev.dongola.garden.choice.wait: Stay a day and help sort the seed beds
ev.dongola.garden.result.channel: You and the nephew lift sand from the channel while his aunt steadies the little gate. Water reaches the new bed before the heat grows strong. A ferry passenger sees the three of you working and brings another scoop; the garden's neighbours thank you for helping keep their shared water flowing.
ev.dongola.garden.result.wait: You stay for a day, marking the two beds and helping the nephew sort the remaining seeds. At supper his aunt brings beans from the last harvest and tells him that the uncertain bed can wait until it sprouts. You leave rested after sharing their meal.
ev.dongola.garden.title: The Garden beside the Landing
ev.dongola.site_gap.body: At the river ferry, a boatman is replacing the worn end of a reed rope. His daughter holds the coil while he tests each strand. ‘The old part caught under the hull yesterday,’ she says. He asks her to show you the frayed place, then explains why the rope must give a little as the water rises. A traveller arrives with a crate and tries to set it by the rail. The boatman asks him to move it toward the middle of the boat. ‘When everyone stands on one side to see the far bank, I still have to keep her level.’ You ask how to reach the Arabian towns from here. His daughter says the road first follows the Nile north toward Cairo; from there travellers cross Sinai before continuing into Arabia. ‘My aunt went that way,’ she says. ‘She sent word from Cairo before she crossed the desert.’ The boatman points to the marks on his pole, which he uses to read the water. His daughter asks whether today's level changes the loading order. He checks it before answering, then lets her place the traveller's crate at the centre of the boat.
ev.dongola.site_gap.choice.route: Ask about the Nile road toward Cairo
ev.dongola.site_gap.title: The Ferry Rope
ev.dufar.entry.body: In Dufar, a resin collector has brought a basket of frankincense down from the groves. His daughter is sorting the pale pieces from those still carrying bark. “This one came loose before the cut had healed,” she says, holding one up. Her father looks at it and agrees. A trader waiting beside them asks whether the better grade will be ready for his coastal boat. “After she finishes,” the collector answers. The girl asks him why he promises the cargo before they have counted it. “Because I know you count more carefully than I do,” he says. You ask which road leads through the town. The trader points between the storehouses and offers to introduce you to the resin sellers if you stay. At the far end of the street, horses are being led toward another vessel. The collector tells his daughter to keep the incense away from the wet harnesses while they finish the basket.
ev.dufar.entry.choice.look: Spend a day among the incense sellers
ev.dufar.entry.choice.pass: Ask the road through town and continue
ev.dufar.entry.title: The Frankincense Basket
ev.dufar.sail.body: A sailmaker near Dufar's shore is patching a long tear in a small boat's sail. Her brother brought it in before dawn and promised to collect it after he helped unload another vessel. “He said that yesterday too,” her son tells you. She smiles, draws the torn edges together and asks him to bring more thread. The boy has wound it around the wrong spindle, so he sits down to sort the tangles. You ask whether the sail can still catch wind after the repair. “It will if the patch lies flat,” she says, showing where the old cloth has stretched. Her brother arrives carrying a basket of dates for their lunch. He sees the work is nearly done and offers to pay someone to help finish the seam before the tide changes. The son wants to carry the sail to the boat himself. His mother tells him to finish untangling the thread first; then they can go together. The boy asks whether they can eat the dates after the sail is hung; his uncle says he will save the best for him.
ev.dufar.sail.choice.sew: Help finish the seam for a fee
ev.dufar.sail.choice.tide: Ask her brother about the tide and coastal route
ev.dufar.sail.result.sew: You hold the cloth flat while the sailmaker and her son finish the seam. Her brother tests the patch against the light and pays you the share he promised. The boy carries the folded sail to the boat with his mother and returns the spindle before he leaves.
ev.dufar.sail.result.tide: Her brother draws the route toward Aden on a board and shows where his boat waits for the tide. The boy asks why he never points out that turn when they sail together. “You were busy watching the birds,” he says. You leave with the coastal passage clearer in mind.
ev.dufar.sail.title: A Sail to Bring Home
ev.dufar.site_gap.body: An incense seller is wrapping resin in thick paper while his nephew tests the seals on two clay jars. “This one smells of dried fish,” the boy says, pushing a jar away. His uncle laughs. “Then it can carry water, not incense.” He gives you a pale piece to smell and asks what you notice. The scent comes through before you crush it. He shows the boy how to keep the paper dry and how to tie the bundle without breaking the resin. A customer asks whether the shop will send a parcel toward Esher. “If the carrier still has room,” the seller answers, “but tell her which door to find before she leaves.” The nephew offers to walk to the corner with you and point out that road. His uncle calls him back for a moment: the last jar still needs a clean lining, and the boy is the only one with small enough hands to set it neatly. The customer says she will bring the receiving name tomorrow, when she knows which cousin is at home.
ev.dufar.site_gap.choice.interact: Help line the clean incense jar
ev.dufar.site_gap.choice.route: Ask about the road to Esher
ev.dufar.site_gap.title: The Incense Seller’s Wrapping
ev.edessa.clayletter.body:
At a potter's yard, Safa holds a letter flat against a board with a lump of clay. Her father sent it from Tarsus, where he took a load of bowls to sell. A corner got wet on the journey home. She can still read the part where he asks if her little brother has stopped hiding his shoes, but the directions for his return are fading.

Her brother says he hid the shoes because their father always set them beside the door as though the boy were about to leave too. Safa reads that line aloud again, and both of them laugh. Their father promises to bring back a pair that fits.

Several bowls must also be moved into the shade before they dry too quickly. Safa has put off that work to save the letter. She asks you to help copy the remaining directions, or stay and move the bowls while she writes. She has money set aside for a day's help.

‘Does Father know you hide my shoes?’ Safa asks her brother. ‘He found them last time,’ he says, ‘and put them back by the door.’ She smooths the damp corner of the letter without rubbing the ink. You ask whether another carrier might remember the road their father named. Safa says the pottery buyer knows the same route and will come for the bowls before sunset. Her brother takes the wooden board at the dry end so she can lift the letter carefully. ‘Ask him about the shoes too,’ he says. Safa laughs, then notices the shade moving across the clay pieces and calls him to help shift them.
ev.edessa.clayletter.choice.copy: Copy the surviving route in the letter
ev.edessa.clayletter.choice.work: Stay a day and move the bowls into shade
ev.edessa.clayletter.result.copy: You hold the board steady while Safa copies the legible names and turns onto a clean sheet. Her brother reads them back, slowly enough for her to catch a missed stop. She adds a line of her own, asking their father to bring shoes with room to grow. You copy the road toward Tarsus into your map as she speaks, and mark the city at its far end.
ev.edessa.clayletter.result.work: You spend the day carrying unfired bowls beneath the awning. Safa finishes copying the letter while her brother counts the bowls, losing his place whenever he finds a pair that matches. When the light fades, she pays you the agreed wage. Her brother shows you where he has hidden his shoes this time; he intends to leave them there until their father comes home. You leave the next morning.
ev.edessa.clayletter.title: A Letter at the Potter's Yard
ev.edessa.entry.body:
The road into Edessa passes a water trough. Miran is filling a leather bag from a jar, while his niece Derya sits nearby with a pile of flat stones. She has arranged them into a winding line and says it is the road her uncle took when he went away to buy wool.

“That road had more turns than this,” Miran says. Derya adds two stones. He went away long enough for her to outgrow the shoes she was wearing when he left, and she has made him tell the story of his return three times.

Miran asks where you are headed and shifts his bag so you can fill yours. Derya wants to know if your road has a river. When you show her the map, she finds Edessa before Miran does. He tells you where travellers stop for water beyond the town; she puts another stone beside the trough to mark the place where you met.
ev.edessa.entry.choice.pass: Thank Miran and continue through Edessa
ev.edessa.entry.choice.rest: Stay with Miran's family for a day
ev.edessa.entry.title: Arriving at Edessa
ev.egrigaia.entry.body:
In Egrigaia, a weaver named Saran is hanging a length of pale camel-wool cloth while her mother checks it for dust. Her younger brother has carried it across the yard, brushing past a charcoal basket. He insists he did not touch it. His mother points to a grey mark at the edge and asks him to fetch clean water. Saran says she can wash that corner without wetting the whole bolt.

You ask who will take the cloth when it dries. Saran says a trader from a nearby route has promised to collect it, and her mother will decide whether the marked edge meets his order. The brother returns with water and asks whether the trader will be angry. ‘He will ask what happened,’ their mother says. ‘We can show him the clean edge when it is ready.’

The trader arrives early. Saran asks him to wait in the shade while she finishes. She can tell you which households weave the white wool, and her brother knows a place to rest if you stay a day.
ev.egrigaia.entry.choice.look: Stay a day and see the family finish the cloth
ev.egrigaia.entry.choice.pass: Ask where the road leaves town and continue
ev.egrigaia.entry.title: White Wool at Egrigaia
ev.egrigaia.site_gap.body:
At a pasture tent, keeper Orin is loosening the roof cord so smoke from the cooking fire can leave. His wife says the opening is still too narrow. He adjusts it, then the wind shifts and smoke comes back toward her pots. Their daughter lifts the door flap a little; clean air moves in below and the smoke rises. Orin thanks her for seeing what he missed.

You ask whether the patched felt around the opening will hold. Orin’s wife points to new stitching she made after the last snowfall. Their daughter says one seam still needs another stitch, and brings the needle. The family has a guest expected for supper, so the pots must be back over the fire soon. Orin offers to hold the felt while his wife works.

A herder stopping for water knows the road toward Tenduc and can name the camps. Orin leaves the cord loose enough for you to try adjusting it while his daughter watches the smoke.
ev.egrigaia.site_gap.choice.interact: Help Orin adjust the smoke opening
ev.egrigaia.site_gap.choice.route: Ask the herder about the Tenduc camps
ev.egrigaia.site_gap.title: The Felt Tent’s Smoke Opening
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.body:
At a smaller weaving tent, two sisters are deciding which border to put on a white camel-wool shawl for their grandmother. The younger one wants a bright red thread; the older says Grandmother asked for a narrow blue line. ‘She may still like red,’ the younger says. Their father, who twisted the warp, asks whether either of them remembers what Grandmother wears when she visits. Both answer at once: the old blue scarf.

You ask when they will give her the shawl. The family is meeting her at a nearby camp tomorrow. The younger sister has already woven a little red tassel and does not want to waste it. Her older sister suggests tying it to the wrapping instead. Their father asks them to hold the shawl in daylight before deciding. They find that the white wool makes both colours vivid.

A neighbour with a cart can carry the finished shawl to Grandmother’s camp today and offers 0.8 silver to anyone who helps with the delivery. The sisters can also spend the following day showing you how the border is woven. The younger one lays her red tassel beside the blue thread and smiles.
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.choice.deliver: Help deliver the finished shawl today
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.choice.weave: Stay another day and learn the border weave
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.result.deliver: You ride with the neighbour and deliver the shawl. Grandmother spots the red tassel on the wrapping before she sees the blue border and knows both sisters worked on it. The neighbour pays you 0.8 silver as promised.
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.result.weave: You stay the next day and watch the sisters finish the narrow blue line. The younger one ties her red tassel to the parcel. Their father thanks you for taking an interest in the family’s work.
ev.egrigaia.whiteedge.title: A Border for Grandmother
ev.ephesus.entry.body:
The road climbs toward the houses on Ayasuluk Hill. Below, the older stones of Ephesus spread across the ground where streets once led to the sea. Leyla and her daughter Nisa are gathering fallen twigs beside the path. Nisa has found a smooth piece of marble and is trying to carry it with the firewood.

“That one will not burn,” Leyla says. Nisa knows. She wants to show it to her grandfather, who tells stories about the old town whenever he sees a stone with a carved edge. Leyla agrees to take the marble if Nisa carries the smaller bundle of wood.

They ask where you have travelled from. Leyla points out the path to the houses and the place where travellers can draw water. Nisa asks whether the stones in your own town are as white as this one. She holds it up beside your map, leaving a pale dust mark on her thumb.
ev.ephesus.entry.choice.pass: Thank Leyla and continue past the old stones
ev.ephesus.entry.choice.rest: Stay a day with Leyla's family
ev.ephesus.entry.title: The Houses Above Old Ephesus
ev.ephesus.olivejar.body:
At the foot of the hill, Marika and her son Petros are sealing jars of olive oil. Petros's older sister has gone to Smyrna to learn a trade. Her last letter said she missed the oil their mother pours on warm bread. Marika has saved a small jar for her, wrapped in cloth so the stopper will stay firm.

Petros wants to carry it himself. Marika points to the larger jars ready for sale and reminds him he has promised to help finish them first. He says he can do both, then gets oil on his sleeve while testing a lid. Marika hands him a rag and asks him to slow down.

One sealed jar is available for travellers to buy. Marika also asks if you will accompany Petros to the caravan stop the next day. He knows the stops toward Smyrna from his sister's letters and would be glad of company on the first stretch.

You ask whether the sister knows a parcel is coming. ‘She asked for a taste, not a whole jar,’ Marika says. Petros answers, ‘Then she can share it with the family who lets her work there.’ His mother checks the stopper and tells him to write her name on the cloth before the oil goes into anyone else’s load. He reaches for charcoal, then remembers his sleeve is still oily and asks you to hold the jar steady. Outside, a driver calls that he can wait until morning if the road is wet. Petros looks to his mother; she says to finish the labels tonight and decide about departure after they hear the weather.
ev.ephesus.olivejar.choice.buy: Buy a sealed jar of olive oil for 120 silver
ev.ephesus.olivejar.choice.walk: Walk with Petros to the caravan stop
ev.ephesus.olivejar.result.buy: You pay Marika and take a sealed jar of olive oil. She checks the stopper once more before handing it over. Petros wraps his sister's smaller jar in fresh cloth and tells you she will put the oil on bread before reading the rest of his letter. You carry your purchase onward.
ev.ephesus.olivejar.result.walk: You spend the next day walking with Petros. He tells you about the sister who taught him to read and the stopping places she named on the road toward Smyrna. At the caravan stop he finds a traveller going that way and gives her the small jar and his letter. You add Ephesus, Smyrna, and the route between them to your map. Petros heads home to help his mother with the larger jars.
ev.ephesus.olivejar.title: The Oil Jar for Smyrna
ev.esher.a.body: At Esher's harbour, a groom is giving a horse water before it boards a ship. The animal watches men carry crates across a gangplank and refuses to come near it. “He heard the wood move under the last crate,” the groom tells his daughter. She asks the crew to secure the plank and walks over it herself. “Now let him see me come back,” she says. The horse follows her as far as the shade. A customs clerk meanwhile checks the horse's tag against the ship's list. You ask where the arriving vessels came from; he names the coast toward Aden and the boats that call at Dufar. The groom asks whether you are looking for passage or a horse of your own. His daughter says the horse will be ready to move when the loading noises settle. The clerk invites you to stay and watch how he marks both incoming cargo and the animals going out.
ev.esher.a.choice.buy_horse: Buy a horse from the groom
ev.esher.a.choice.walk_harbour: Spend a day with the harbour clerk
ev.esher.a.choice.watch_ships: Ask the pilots which boats call at Dufar
ev.esher.a.title: A Horse Waiting for the Gangplank
ev.esher.b.body: In a shaded store at Esher, an incense seller is dividing a large lot of frankincense. His sister has written the buyer's mark on every sack, but one tag is upside down. “That is yours,” she says, handing it to him. He turns the sack and recognizes his own crooked letters. A customer asks why the resin is kept in a dry room while dates are sold outside. The sister breaks a pale piece and lets him smell it. “If the sacks grow damp, you won't want to pay for this scent.” Their niece brings in a tray of dates from the neighbouring stall and asks whether they may take a short break before weighing the last sack. The seller agrees, then asks you whether you want a full trade sack, a little food for the road, or directions to the ships toward Aden and across to Axuma. He waits for his sister to finish the account before anyone carries a sack away.
ev.esher.b.choice.ask_axuma: Ask about Aden and the Axuma crossing
ev.esher.b.choice.buy_dates: Buy a small serving of dates to eat
ev.esher.b.choice.buy_frankincense: Buy a full trade sack of frankincense
ev.esher.b.title: A Frankincense Seller’s Ledger
ev.esher.cat.body: A harbour scribe is looking for his mother's grey cat among the date baskets outside her house. His little sister insists the cat came back from the quay before lunch. “I fed him,” she says. “Then you must know where he went,” he answers. She crouches beside the baskets and finds only a strip of torn awning cloth. Their mother opens the door and asks why both children are under her stall. The scribe shows her the strip; wind has pulled the awning loose, leaving a gap that the cat likes to climb through. She says he will come home when the yard grows quiet, but the awning needs fixing before the next rain. The sister hears a scrape behind a basket and points. You can help her bring the cat out carefully, or take the tools her mother offers and mend the shade while the children look for him. Her mother puts the ladder by the door, where it will not block the neighbours.
ev.esher.cat.choice.awning: Repair the awning for the mother
ev.esher.cat.choice.cat: Help the children bring out the cat
ev.esher.cat.result.awning: You fasten the torn awning while the mother holds the ladder. The children coax the cat from behind the baskets before you finish. She tests the shade, pays you for the repair, and tells them to give the cat a place inside before the wind rises again.
ev.esher.cat.result.cat: You move the basket slowly while the sister holds out a bit of food. The cat emerges and lets the scribe carry him indoors. Their mother thanks you for taking care around the stall, and the neighbouring sellers call to see whether the cat is home.
ev.esher.cat.title: The Cat under the Date Baskets
ev.esher.entry.body: At Esher, a date seller has left a basket beside the harbour clerk's table. Her younger brother has used the basket lid as a tray for his lunch. “When I need that lid, you are always eating,” she tells him. He puts it back and asks which ship she is waiting for. “The one carrying our uncle's letter,” she says. The clerk finds the ship on his list and promises to call when its cargo is counted. You ask how the road out of town runs. The date seller points past the incense sheds and offers to walk you there after she has read the letter. Her brother says he can show you now, but he first has to return the neighbour's water jar. Nearby, merchants are taking frankincense from the storehouse and carrying food toward the boats. At the mosque door a visitor finishes washing and makes room for another traveller. The date seller shades her eyes, looking for the incoming sail.
ev.esher.entry.choice.market: Spend a day among the harbour sellers
ev.esher.entry.choice.pass: Ask for the road out and continue
ev.esher.entry.title: The Basket beside the Clerk’s Table
ev.etzina.entry.body: When you leave the city of Campichu you ride for twelve days, and then reach a city called ETZINA, which is towards the north on the verge of the Sandy Desert; it belongs to the Province of Tangut. The people are Idolaters, and possess plenty of camels and cattle, and the country produces a number of good falcons, both Sakers and Lanners. The inhabitants live by their cultivation and their cattle, for they have no trade.
ev.etzina.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.etzina.entry.title: Of the City of Etzina
ev.ev_accon_battuta_a.choice_1_result:
You spend a day with Hamid at the resting places along the shore, helping him find a companion who knows the hill roads. At Kark Nuh, he says, travellers can drink at the lodge, and someone will show them where the tomb stands. It lies inland, and he hopes to go with someone who knows the way.

Back beneath the shade cloth, Safa has cut open the pomegranate. She offers Hamid a piece. He tastes it and laughs that she chose a good one. Adil gives you a piece too and thanks you for helping Hamid find a companion. The travellers who rest at Acre come to know you.
ev.ev_accon_battuta_a.choice_2_result:
You walk with Hamid along the old harbour steps. He points north along the coast and describes the road towards Tyre. He once watched people mending boat nets there and borrowed a small knife from one of them.

You spend the day asking people along the shore. At dusk a netmender lends you a small knife. When Safa hears, she brings out the pomegranate at once. You mark the direction of Tyre on your map.
ev.ev_accon_battuta_a.choice_3_result:
Hamid sets the mat aside. Travellers, he says, tell another story about Abu Yaakub Yusuf: that he once turned the copper vessels of a young woman's dowry into gold. Safa stares and asks whether Hamid saw it himself.

“I saw the lodge and his tomb,” Hamid says. He tells you how he lost the road inland until a man with a donkey led him to the door. You listen through the day and record the marvel as a story alongside the road Hamid actually travelled. At dusk, Adil borrows a knife and Safa cuts the pomegranate for everyone. Then he invites you to tell the story to newly arrived travellers, who are glad to listen.
ev.ev_accon_entry.choice_1_result: You ask Safa where the main road begins. She sets down the water jug and points to an earthen track beside the old harbour steps. “Follow it to the fork and ask whoever is travelling there.” Yusuf has already run off with the basket. You follow her directions and mark Acre on your map.
ev.ev_accon_entry.choice_2_result:
You walk along the road with Safa and Yusuf. The driver is still loading a sack of beans. Their uncle is crouched beside him, holding a rope taut. Yusuf hands him the basket and lifts the bread. The letter is still underneath. Their uncle tucks it into his clothes and asks Yusuf to tell his grandmother that he'll have someone write back from Jerusalem.

You spend the night at a resting place by the shore. The next morning their uncle meets you beside the road and points out the direction his party will take to Jerusalem. You add the city and road to your map.
ev.ev_aden_a.choice_1_result: You spend the day beside the handover. The niece asks you to hold each repaired bag while she compares the two lists, and by dusk she has corrected the duplicate mark. The seller explains how the pepper will pass from ship to caravan; later he asks you to stay for a second conversation with the carriers.
ev.ev_aden_a.choice_2_result: You pay for a bag of pepper. The niece checks its seam in front of you and ties on a clean label bearing your mark. “Keep it above the wet baggage,” she says. The seller points out the carriers who handle the spice after it leaves Aden and invites you back to hear their plans.
ev.ev_aden_a.choice_3_result: The seller names the road toward Dufar and the sea passage toward Cambaet. He asks his niece to show you how the two carriers mark their loads, and she makes you repeat the turns before she closes the map. You leave with a firmer idea of the next stages of travel.
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.body: The pepper seller calls you back to the awning before the next load leaves. His niece has repaired the torn bag and is waiting beside a caravan master and a sailor. “Tell our visitor where you take the cargo,” the seller says. The sailor names the next coastal landing; the caravan master points to the inland road and asks what you plan to carry. You say you have not decided. “Then look at the load while it is still here,” the niece says. She opens one bag to show how tightly it must be packed and closes it again. The caravan master offers you a bag at his own price. The sailor spreads a route sheet on an empty crate, but the wind catches its edge. All three hold it down and begin arguing cheerfully about which departure will happen first. The niece asks which carrier will write the next cargo mark. Both men answer at once, and the seller hands her the pen.
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the caravan master’s bag of pepper
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay the caravan master for his bag of pepper. The niece turns the seam toward you so you can inspect her repair, then ties your mark beside it. He loads the bag with your goods and explains how the spice is kept dry on the next stage.
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_2: Ask them to mark the two routes
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_2_result: The sailor marks Cambaet on the sea passage, and the caravan master points out Dufar along the coast. The niece adds the water stops each knows firsthand. You follow their marks with a finger and leave better prepared to choose a departure.
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_3: Spend another day with the lighter crews
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day seeing cargo pass from the large ship to smaller boats. The niece calls out each bag's mark, and the sailor answers when it is safely aboard. By evening you have heard the stages by which pepper leaves the harbour and why each handover needs a fresh count.
ev.ev_aden_a_followup.title: Aden: The Carrier’s Turn
ev.ev_aden_b.choice_1_result: You stay for a day at the customs desk. The officer lets her daughter read the next cargo form aloud, then checks the goods against it. The girl corrects her own mistake before the merchant takes his stamped paper. By evening the officer knows you waited patiently and showed respect for the harbour's work.
ev.ev_aden_b.choice_2_result: You pay the harbour fee and buy a full trade bundle of frankincense from the merchant. He ties it shut and tells you about the road to Esher, where his brother receives shipments. The customs officer gives him his paper, and you leave with the incense safely packed.
ev.ev_aden_b.choice_3_result: You stand quietly outside the mosque during prayer. Afterwards the officer's daughter joins you in the shade and asks whether she read the merchant's name correctly. Her mother confirms it. You spend a little time talking with them before returning to the harbour, on easier terms with the people there.
ev.ev_aden_entry.choice_1_result: The boy walks his cart to the corner and points you toward the road out of Aden. His mother calls him back before he can follow you farther: the next ship's crew has come for water. You continue, able to find your way through the harbour lanes.
ev.ev_aden_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day in the market. The spice seller shows you where pepper is weighed, and the water seller introduces the carriers who take food to the boats. When her customer returns, the boy reminds him about the jar he owes. By evening you know the streets and the talk of Aden's merchants.
ev.ev_aden_entry.choice_3_result: You leave your shoes at the mosque door and wait until the gathering has room for a visitor. An attendant shows you where to stand and thanks you for treating the place with care. Outside, the water seller points out the lane back to the harbour; you leave with the town's ways and turns in mind.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_a.choice_1_resu: You stay through the next day, helping the gatekeeper sort bundles while the student returns with her corrected slip. She recognizes the water seller’s cloth and keeps her paper in a safer pocket. The gatekeeper thanks you by name in front of the porters who come through his gate.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_a.choice_2_resu: You spend the next day with the carrier the gatekeeper named. He shows you where travellers join the road to Cairo and points out the first place to find water. The student copies the directions beside the clean borrowing slip so her relative can use them later.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_a.choice_3_resu: You carry the student’s books through the gate and stay the following day while she brings a clean slip to the school. The keeper checks it against the borrowed volume. She thanks you before the teachers and offers to show you the reading room next time you come.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_b.choice_1_resu: You spend the next day checking the three addresses with the daughter. A harbour traveller supplies the new Indian trading house, and the father seals that letter only after she writes it clearly. He thanks you in front of the courier and promises to send word when a reply arrives.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_b.choice_2_resu: You stay another day to speak with the courier. He points out the road to Cairo and the merchant who receives letters there. The daughter writes his directions on a spare sheet; her father is relieved to know whom to ask if the first letter is delayed.
ev.ev_alexandria_battuta_b.choice_3_resu: You take the sealed letter to the gate while the family finishes the other two. The courier checks the merchant’s name and tucks the letter safely into his bag. The daughter sees you return with his receipt and thanks you before going back to the address she is copying.
ev.ev_alexandria_entry.choice_1_result: You ask the porter how to leave the city. He shifts the crate to his other shoulder. "Follow the wall to the water seller's shelter. He watches the caravans pass every day; ask him there." He steadies the swaying crate and heads back towards the quay.
ev.ev_alexandria_entry.choice_2_result:
Hasan arrives at last. He scolds his escort for leaving the tally behind, then apologises to the clerk. The clerk checks tally against ledger and finally lowers the sack onto the scale.

The porter points towards the merchants waiting under the arcade. "If you carry someone else's goods, bring the tally. Otherwise the pepper may hang there until dark." You spend a day at the quay and talk with merchants about the roads out of town. One is leaving for Bethlehem in the morning. He draws the caravan's gate on a sheet of paper and tells you where to find them.
ev.ev_alexandria_mentor_geomancy.choice_: You pay and learn geomancy. You pay 8000 coins. You spend 10 days learning the art. You can now read it on any road. A mark is set on this affair.
You ask what Populus means for a voyage. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_antiochia_entry.choice_1_result: The keeper pins the board with his foot until the last mule crosses. He points towards the city gate. "Eastwards? Go out that way. More carts are coming; don't stand on the bridge looking for signs." You cross with the queue while the river moves beneath your feet.
ev.ev_antiochia_entry.choice_2_result:
A carpenter arrives with his tools and prises up the loose board. A nail has broken underneath it; each wheel has pushed the end a little higher. The driver who had shouted the loudest now holds the new board steady for him.

By the time the carpenter drives in the last nail, it is growing dark. You stay in town that night and return to the bridge in the morning. The keeper recognises you and points east. "For Edessa, go out that way. There are guarded roads in the hills. Follow the one the other travellers use." Carts are crossing the bridge again.
ev.ev_axuma_entry.choice_1_result: The church reader walks with you as far as the fig tree and points to the road onward. His daughter calls after him to remember the empty jar he promised to return. He goes back for it, waving you on. You know where the station lies when you need water again.
ev.ev_axuma_entry.choice_2_result: You stay for a day and help move the jars under the roof. The daughter brings bread and a bowl of lentils when the work is done. “You saved me two trips in the sun,” she says. After a full night's rest you leave with your strength restored and with the station's turn fixed in mind.
ev.ev_axuma_site_gap.choice_1_result: The niece takes you to the fork and points out the stones that mark the Dongola road. “The spring path ends among the trees; this one keeps going,” she says. You trace the turn for yourself before returning her tile.
ev.ev_axuma_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the jar while she presses clay into the crack and winds a strip of cloth around the rim. Her uncle waits until the patch has dried before pouring in a little water. It holds. He explains how he checks a jar before trusting it with a day's supply.
ev.ev_babylonia_cairus_entry.choice_1_re:
The carrier entrusts the basket to the boatman and takes up his jars for the next house. He shows you the way to the city gate. "Follow the stalls with awnings. Don't turn into the grain yard."

The girl waves from the boat. It has not left yet, but she is already checking whether the bread in the basket has been crushed.
ev.ev_babylonia_cairus_entry.choice_2_re:
You help the carrier deliver his water and stay by the river that night. The boatman carries the first basket across for the girl. In the morning she prepares another basket of bread, and her father takes her to the island. Her uncle eats the bread she brought and shows you the marked column inside the measuring well. He records where the water reaches each day. People who tend the canals and fields come to ask him.

On the way back, the carrier points out the yard where caravans for Petra gather. He says his daughter has won this time: she will set the hour for future lunch deliveries.
ev.ev_badashan_a.choice_1_result: You spend the day beside their felt rug. Farid’s sister shows you how she checks each wrapping; their mother corrects the porter’s tally. You record the stone trade and are invited to return when the next ledger is opened.
ev.ev_badashan_a.choice_2_result: You pay 135 silver for the full lapis lot. Farid and his sister count the parcels with you; their mother names the way carriers travel toward Balkh. You mark that city on your map and keep the receipt with the goods.
ev.ev_badashan_a.choice_3_result: Farid’s mother explains which approaches lead toward Taican and Kashmir and which valleys become difficult after rain. You mark both places and remember to ask about local conditions before travelling.
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.body:
Farid opens a second ledger when the porter returns from the lower road. His sister notices one parcel has been marked twice: once for the buyer who changed his mind and once for the new offer. ‘If we leave both names, someone will come back for a stone we no longer have,’ she says. Farid crosses out the old entry and asks his mother to check the carrier’s route.

She finds a water stop omitted from the margin. You ask whether that matters to the price. ‘It matters to the people carrying it,’ she replies. The porter points to Balkh on a rough map and explains where he pays for animal feed. Farid has a second merchant lot available for 135 silver if you want the whole shipment.

His sister dries the corrected ink while you decide. You can buy the lot, ask them to trace the road toward Balkh, or stay the day until the broker’s report is complete and study how the family settles a disputed entry.
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the lapis lot for 135 silver
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_1_resul: You pay 135 silver for the full lapis lot after Farid corrects the entry. His sister checks the count a final time, and you record both the purchase and what their ledger taught you.
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_2: Ask them to draw the road toward Balkh
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_2_resul: The porter describes the lower road toward Balkh, including a stop where he feeds his animals. Farid’s mother checks his directions, and you mark Balkh on your map with notes on the tolls.
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day for the completed report
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You stay the day while the family matches parcels to names. Farid shows you the completed report, with old offers crossed out and the carrier’s costs added. You leave better able to judge another stone bargain.
ev.ev_badashan_a_followup.title: Farid’s Second Ledger
ev.ev_badashan_b.choice_1_result: You spend the day listening to the clerk compare names in the old books. His niece repeats the parts she can remember, and you record the family’s claim as a claim, alongside the valley names. They ask you to return if another traveller brings a new spelling.
ev.ev_badashan_b.choice_2_result: You pay 2 silver. The clerk teaches you greetings and a question about a stone’s origin; his niece makes you say each phrase to the messenger before he leaves. People at the market answer you more warmly afterward.
ev.ev_badashan_b.choice_3_result: You pay 135 silver for the uncut balas ruby. The broker and clerk check the broker’s receipt together, then wrap the stone for travel. You record where they came from and keep the receipt.
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.body:
The clerk’s niece brings you a note with three words she heard from stone carriers. She has written each as it sounded to her, then left room for the clerk’s correction. A messenger from the next valley is waiting; he can speak the words aloud before he takes his letter.

The first word names a pass. The clerk asks the messenger whether it is the approach toward Taican or the one travellers use for Kashmir. The messenger draws two lines on a scrap and says the roads divide after the pasture. You repeat his words, and he grins at your careful accent. The niece asks him to say them more slowly for both of you.

The clerk can give you a short lesson for 2 silver, with a chance to practise among the local traders. You can instead ask the messenger to show the two mountain directions, or buy one uncut balas ruby for 135 silver while the broker is still in the yard.
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_1: Pay 2 silver for a short lesson
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_1_resul: You pay 2 silver and practise with the clerk and messenger. At the market you manage a short exchange with a stone carrier; he remembers your effort and introduces you to another trader.
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the messenger to draw the two mountain approaches
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_2_resul: The messenger draws the routes toward Taican and Kashmir and names the pasture where they divide. You mark both places on your map and note the local names beside them.
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_3: Buy the uncut balas ruby for 135 silver
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.choice_3_resul: You pay 135 silver for the uncut balas ruby. The broker and clerk check the licence and receipt together; the niece writes you a clean copy. You record the trade and keep the stone wrapped for travel.
ev.ev_badashan_b_followup.title: The Clerk’s Mountain Words
ev.ev_badashan_entry.choice_1_result: The boy waves his ledger at you as you leave. You mark Badakhshan on your map and follow the road beyond the market.
ev.ev_badashan_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day hearing the traders compare stones, origins, and transport costs. By evening the boy can read the corrected figures without help. You record what you learned and mark Badakhshan on your map.
ev.ev_badashan_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the caretakers and listen to the people who gather there. They guide you back toward the market, remember your courtesy, and give you a small token of the visit. You mark Badakhshan on your map.
ev.ev_balc_a.choice_1_result: You help Farid measure and set the doorway over two days. The caravan woman comes back with details of the road to Samarkand, which you add to your map. Mina insists on keeping one carved flower visible from the street; the neighbour agrees when she sees it in the afternoon light.
ev.ev_balc_a.choice_2_result: Farid gives you the thin carved fragment once the sound stones are set aside. Mina wraps it in a scrap of cloth and tells you which flower on the wall resembles it. You keep the fragment and make a note about the repaired lane.
ev.ev_balc_a.choice_3_result: Farid tells you how his father showed him the first stones he was allowed to set. Mina interrupts to ask whether he dropped one. ‘Two,’ he says, making her laugh. You record the family’s account of the old wall. A little later Mina comes to ask about another piece she found.
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.body:
Mina returns to the doorway with another carved piece. Her uncle Farid turns it over and finds a line of old lettering under the dust. ‘That is why we measure before we build,’ he tells her. ‘If the writing goes into the wall, no one can read it again.’ She asks him to set it where neighbours can see it. He agrees to ask the owner of the house.

You ask where the stone came from. Mina shows you a heap beside the lane; it had been saved after earlier repairs, but nobody had recorded who moved it. A trader from Badakhshan stops to look and says he knows a stone worker in his home valley who reads old marks. Farid does not know whether that will help, though he will let Mina draw the letters.

The householder comes out and approves a place above the doorway for the larger piece. Farid sets a small loose fragment aside for you. Mina brings a bit of charcoal. The trader steadies the paper while she tests the first letter, and Farid calls her back before the mortar sets.
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.choice_1_result: Farid gives you the loose fragment after Mina has copied its pattern. She folds the drawing into her uncle’s tool bag, and you put the stone into yours. You add the doorway and the family’s account to your notes.
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the Badakhshan trader where to find the stone worker
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.choice_2_result: The trader tells you the name of his valley in Badakhshan and how caravans reach it. Mina writes the place beside her drawing in case the family sends a message. You add Badakhshan and the old stone to your travel notes.
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.choice_3: Help Mina draw the letters for the neighbours
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.choice_3_result: You hold the paper while Mina rubs charcoal across the letters. The householder carries the drawing indoors for her children to see, then thanks you for staying with the work. Farid points out the flower that will face the street once the mortar dries.
ev.ev_balc_a_followup.title: Mina’s Second Stone
ev.ev_balc_b.choice_1_result: After the woman signs the corrected ledger, you pay 135 silver for the full lot of lapis. Yunus writes your pack number carefully this time, and his mother checks the seal before the chest is closed. You take the stone cargo with you.
ev.ev_balc_b.choice_2_result: You inspect the single uncut balas ruby in the innkeeper’s daylight and pay 135 silver. The trader wraps it separately, and Yunus writes only one stone against your name. The woman with the cloth reminds him to dry the new page before closing the book.
ev.ev_balc_b.choice_3_result: The lapis trader names Badakhshan’s mountain markets, and the cloth trader traces the Samarkand road past the wells she trusts. You mark both destinations. Yunus asks whether you can come back after supper to check a newer entry in the ledger.
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.body:
After supper at the inn, Yunus brings the ledger you were asked to check. A newly arrived driver has written the number of his lapis packs in the column for nights of lodging. ‘My mother will charge him for twenty beds,’ Yunus says, embarrassed. The driver, who is standing nearby, laughs and points out the mark he meant to make. Yunus asks him to wait until his mother can witness the correction.

You ask whether the driver is bound for Samarkand. He says his sister lives on that road and wants a letter carried before he turns back to Badakhshan. He can describe the stops, but first he needs Yunus to copy her address without losing a character. The lapis trader from earlier has another sealed lot for 135 silver and sets it on the table while he waits for his own account.

Yunus’s mother arrives, sees the wrong column and hands him a fresh pen. He looks at you for help with the letter. The driver sits down, ready to repeat the address as many times as needed.
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the other lapis lot for 135 silver
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_1_result: You check the separate sealed lot and pay 135 silver. Yunus’s mother records the sale in the right column while her son corrects the driver’s lodging. The second lapis cargo leaves the inn with you.
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_2: Copy the Samarkand address and learn the road
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_2_result: You copy the sister’s address and ask the driver to trace each stop toward Samarkand. He checks the spelling twice before taking the letter. You note the city and the family’s route; Yunus’s mother thanks you for keeping the ledgers apart.
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to help Yunus sort the records
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.choice_3_result: You stay through the next day, helping Yunus move each pack mark to its proper column. By evening he can explain the book without asking his mother at every line. She sets aside a dry shelf for his papers and sends you out with a bowl of supper.
ev.ev_balc_b_followup.title: Yunus Checks the Night Ledger
ev.ev_balc_c.choice_1_result: You contribute 2 silver for oil and incense. The visiting woman adds it to the keeper’s small box, and the grandson promises to bring the right wick next time. You spend a while hearing the family’s account of the shrine before returning to the road.
ev.ev_balc_c.choice_2_result: You sleep behind the shrine wall and rise after a full night. In the morning the grandson is waiting to tell you about the dream he had, though his grandfather first makes him eat breakfast. You record the family’s stories and remember this night on the hill.
ev.ev_balc_c.choice_3_result: At dawn the keeper recites a short verse his mother taught him, then tells his grandson what its old words mean to him. You listen beside the newly lit lamp and add the hill shrine to your notes before the day’s visitors arrive.
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.body:
After the night at the hill shrine, the keeper’s grandson tells you he dreamed that the oil jar rolled downhill. His grandfather asks whether he checked the shelf before telling everyone. The boy runs inside and returns with the jar steady in both arms. ‘It was only a dream,’ he says. ‘Still, I should move it farther from the edge.’ The visiting woman from yesterday helps him clear a space.

You ask the keeper how he remembers the stories his mother taught him. He points to a little carved scrap kept in a niche. It came from a wall his family once repaired; he uses it to remind the boy which parts he knows from his mother and which he heard from travellers. The woman notices the lamp shelf has come loose. The boy brings a wedge of wood, but needs someone to hold the shelf while he fits it.

The woman stays to refill the lamp. The keeper offers to spend the day talking with you, while the boy waits to see whether you will tell him about a place you have visited.
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_1: Hold the lamp shelf while the boy repairs it
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_1_result: You hold the shelf while the boy drives in the wedge. The woman sets the lamp back and thanks you for making room for it. The keeper tells the next visitors that you helped his grandson finish the repair.
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_2: Stay a day and exchange stories with the keeper
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_2_result: You spend the day at the shrine. The keeper tells you what he remembers of his mother, and you answer the boy’s questions about another road. The woman tends the lamp while you write down what the family told you.
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_3: Hear the boy’s account and go on
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.choice_3_result: The boy tells his dream again, this time including the jar he checked in the morning. His grandfather laughs and sends him to fetch breakfast. You remember their lamp and shelter as you take the road down from the hill.
ev.ev_balc_c_followup.title: The Grandson’s Morning Dream
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.body:
The clerk’s son Umar finds you at the inn with the damp register folded under his arm. ‘Father wants me to check a name before the western caravan leaves,’ he says. His sister Laila copied it from a driver’s wooden tally, but the driver’s mark looks like another family’s. Umar knows both households and does not want either charged for the other’s pack.

You ask whether he can ask the driver directly. ‘He is loading at the next yard,’ Umar says, ‘and will be gone before I fetch Father.’ The innkeeper offers to send her boy across the lane. Laila arrives a moment later with the old list you used at the toll station. She says the second family’s pack was a jar, while this one is a chest; the shapes beside the names differ.

Umar writes the correction, then asks whether you would carry a note to the next record keeper if your roads meet. Laila reminds him to put the family name on the outside so nobody opens the note merely to learn who it is for.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.choice_1: Carry Umar’s note and ask who will receive it
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.choice_1_result: Umar names the keeper at the next station and Laila copies the name onto the outside of the note. You keep it dry beneath your own papers. The family asks you to come back before you leave so they can check the final wording together.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.choice_2: Leave the correction with the clerk’s family
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.choice_2_result: You thank Umar and leave the delivery to his family. Laila folds the corrected list into a fresh cloth, and the innkeeper’s boy returns with news that the driver is still loading. They have time to speak to him before he goes.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a.title: The Clerk’s Second List
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a_resolution.body:
Before you leave Balkh, Umar and Laila bring the finished note. Their father has signed beneath the corrected pack number. ‘I thought he would tell us to begin again,’ Umar says, ‘but he only asked why we had left so much space around the name.’ Laila says the space makes the mark easier to read. The clerk, standing behind them, admits that she is right.

You ask whether the next keeper will recognise the family. The father says yes, but he wants the letter delivered by hand so the correction is entered once, in the proper book. Umar shows you where the fold is sealed. Laila has written the recipient’s name large enough to read without unfolding it.

The inn’s breakfast is being cleared away. Umar turns the signed note so the name faces you. Laila lifts the breakfast bowls before the ink can touch them.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_a_resolution.choi: Carry the signed note to the next keeper
You take the sealed note with its clear name. Umar watches you slip it beneath your dry papers; Laila nods when she sees it will stay flat. The family’s correction is now in your care.
Spend a day copying the corrected record

You spend the day copying the pack number and both family names. Umar compares each line with the signed note, and Laila corrects one letter before you close the book. You keep the record even if the next road never takes you past that station.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.body:
Laila’s younger brother Karim catches up with you near the market. He is carrying a chipped bowl from the family’s shelf of old objects. ‘Laila said you would look at it before I ask the potter,’ he says. A former owner scratched two names beneath the rim, and Karim cannot tell whether the second is a person or a place. His sister arrives to warn him that the bowl still holds water; it should not be carried by its thin handle.

You ask why the names matter to him. Karim says their grandfather used to set the bowl at supper and tell a different story each time. ‘Did he ever say who scratched it?’ Laila asks. Karim shakes his head. A potter at the next stall calls over that he can repair the chip, but the writing may become harder to see if the glaze runs across it.

Karim wants to make a copy of the letters first. He has brought paper and charcoal, though the bowl is slippery in his hands. Laila steadies it and asks whether you want to see the marks with them.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.choice_1: Help Karim copy the letters and keep his account
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.choice_1_result: You hold the bowl while Karim rubs charcoal across the paper. Laila adds the story their grandfather told most often. Karim asks the potter to leave the names visible, then promises to bring you the finished copy before you travel on.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the drawing with Karim and Laila
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.choice_2_result: You tell Karim the drawing belongs with the bowl. He folds it carefully, and Laila finds a clean cloth to wrap both pieces before they go to the potter. The siblings thank you and continue their search together.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b.title: Laila’s Brother Brings the Bowl
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b_resolution.body:
Karim finds you again after the potter has repaired the bowl. The chip is smooth, and the two scratched names are still legible. He has copied them twice: one sheet for home, one for you. Laila reads the second name aloud, then says she has heard it used for a settlement on the road toward the mountains. ‘Grandfather may have known someone there,’ she says. Karim wishes he had asked him when he could.

You ask whether the family wants the spare copy back. Karim says they made it for you, though he would like to know if another traveller recognises the name. Laila tells him to write his own address on the back so a reply can find them. He does, taking a moment to spell the street properly.

The potter calls them to collect a small cup he repaired as well. Karim hands you the paper, then runs back when the potter calls his name again.
ev.ev_balc_consequence_b_resolution.choi: You fold Karim’s copy into your travel book and promise to look out for the name. Laila sees that the paper will stay dry. Karim runs to collect the cup, leaving you with a way to write back.
Spend a day asking around about the name

You spend the day showing the copied name to traders and potters. Two remember hearing it, though they disagree about the exact turning. Karim writes their answers beside his own copy and thanks you for taking the question seriously.
ev.ev_balc_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days checking names and marks with the clerk. Laila discovers that the third caravan’s record was filed beneath a different driver’s name. You note Balkh on your map and in your travel book. The clerk’s son later comes looking for you with a question about the list.
ev.ev_balc_entry.choice_2_result: Laila takes you to a shelf of stones her family has kept from old buildings. She tells you which ones her grandfather found and which came from travellers. You spend the day with her and record what you learned of Balkh. Before you leave, her younger brother asks whether you can look at another object.
ev.ev_balc_entry.choice_3_result: The merchant opens the sealed package and lets you check the jade against his tally. You pay 135 silver for the whole trading lot, spend the day settling the purchase, and load it with your goods. Laila makes sure the merchant’s name is legible in the register before she ties it shut.
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.body:
When you return, Nadir has set aside the page he promised. The driver’s sister has added a note: a well on the Badakhshan road has a broken lip, so a loaded animal needs help at the edge. Her brother says he would have called it a small matter. She asks him to imagine lifting their heaviest pack there alone. He takes the pen and adds a mark beside the warning.

You ask whether Nadir pays people for such details. ‘I return their pages with the names spelled correctly,’ he says. The sister answers that this is payment enough when a letter must find her. She shows you the route as far as she knows it and lets Nadir fill the gaps from drivers who came through yesterday.

The copyist offers you a clean copy of their account. He also has a spare seat if you want to spend the day copying the places for yourself. The sister checks the ink before either of you touches the page.
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.choice_1_resu: Nadir hands you the clean page, and the sister points out her note about the damaged well. You fold it only after she shows you where the ink will not smear. Their road account travels with you.
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask the sister to trace the Badakhshan road
