ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.choice_2_resu: The sister traces the Badakhshan road to the point she knows, and Nadir adds the stops he checked with other drivers. You mark Badakhshan on your map. Her brother asks her to say the well warning once more so he will remember it too.
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.choice_3: Spend a day copying the account yourself
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.choice_3_resu: You spend the day copying the road account. Nadir has you read each place back to the sister; she catches one mistaken letter and tells you why a carrier might take it to the wrong village. You leave with the pages in your own hand.
ev.ev_balc_mentor_followup.title: A Second Page from Nadir
ev.ev_baldacum_a.choice_1_result: You spend two days walking the channels and listening to Yusuf and the river workers. His granddaughter draws the last bend for you; you mark Basra downstream on your map and record how water reaches the courtyard. Yusuf asks you to come back when he opens an old service passage.
ev.ev_baldacum_a.choice_2_result: You pay 146 silver for the full Damascus steel bundle. The merchant opens the wrapping and checks every piece with you on the dry stones; Yusuf’s granddaughter carries the old tile safely away from the loading path. You record the purchase.
ev.ev_baldacum_a.choice_3_result: You stay a day while Yusuf clears the channel. He shows you which walls were rebuilt and where older work remains; his granddaughter finds a tile with a familiar mark. You write down their account and keep a reminder of the courtyard.
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.body:
Yusuf has cleared the old service door beside the water channel. His granddaughter insists on sweeping the step before anyone enters; loose grit made her slip there yesterday. Behind the door is a narrow storeroom where workers once kept spare tiles and tools. A neighbour who collects old coins is waiting with one he says came from this quarter. He offers it for 3 silver.

‘Did it really come from here?’ the girl asks. The collector says he bought it from a river porter and cannot prove the exact room. Yusuf tells her to write down what the man knows and leave the rest blank. You ask whether the channel continues beyond the wall. Yusuf takes a stick and traces its way to the river, then farther south toward Basra where the cargo boats go.

His granddaughter has put the blue tile safely on a shelf. She wants to walk the rooms once more before dark, and Yusuf invites you to come. The coin collector waits at the door, holding the piece flat in his palm.
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the old coin for 3 silver
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_1_resul: You pay 3 silver and take the coin. Yusuf’s granddaughter writes down the collector’s account of where he bought it, leaving its earlier history open. You keep the coin with that note.
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_2: Ask Yusuf how the river reaches Basra
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_2_resul: Yusuf traces the water from the yard into the Tigris, then names the downstream stops toward Basra. His granddaughter adds the landing where she watched the boats load; you mark Basra on your map and record their directions.
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day walking the old rooms with them
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You spend the day with Yusuf and his granddaughter, checking which doors still open and where the water enters. She puts the blue tile back in its place; you leave with a lasting reminder of the old courtyard.
ev.ev_baldacum_a_followup.title: Yusuf’s Service Door
ev.ev_baldacum_b.choice_1_result: You pay 135 silver for Mariam’s full brocade length. She and her apprentice fold it with the repaired edge inside, and she asks you to return when the next piece is finished. You keep a reminder of her workshop.
ev.ev_baldacum_b.choice_2_result: The pepper seller names Hormuz, and the river porter names Basra. The money changer adds what each route costs him; you record their account and mark both places on your map.
ev.ev_baldacum_b.choice_3_result: You spend the day talking with the money changer and Mariam over fruit syrup. The apprentice finishes his repair before the cup warms; by closing time the stallholders know your name and you have pages of notes on their trade.
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.body:
Mariam’s apprentice has finished mending the first brocade length. Today he is setting up the next one, counting the warp threads aloud. Mariam stops him at the fourth group: he has counted a strand twice. He looks embarrassed, but she makes him find the mistake himself before the loom begins to move.

A pearl seller waits outside with news of ships from Hormuz. He asks whether Mariam can make a border like the one on a cloth a buyer showed him. ‘Bring the cloth tomorrow,’ she says. ‘I will not guess from your fingers in the air.’ You ask the seller where the pearls came from. He points toward the Gulf, then admits he bought them from a broker and knows the port better than the diver.

Mariam has a full new length of brocade for 135 silver. The apprentice finishes his count and asks her to check it. She offers to let you watch the loom through a full day, and the pearl seller waits to show you his route.
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the new brocade length for 135 silver
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_1_resul: You pay 135 silver for Mariam’s new length. Her apprentice folds it and checks the repaired edge on the other cloth before you leave; she gives him a nod that makes him grin.
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the pearl seller about Hormuz
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_2_resul: The pearl seller tells you which river landing he uses before travelling toward Hormuz and where he meets sea traders. You mark the port on your map and record what he knows of the pearl trade.
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to watch Mariam weave
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.choice_3_resul: You stay the day beside the loom. Mariam lets the apprentice make the first full row while she watches; by evening you can recognise the border she planned. You keep a reminder of the visit.
ev.ev_baldacum_b_followup.title: The Next Length on Mariam’s Loom
ev.ev_baldacum_c.choice_1_result: You listen as the daughter reads each family’s account, including where the tellers disagree. The storyteller lets you keep a copy for your notes and invites you back when another relative speaks.
ev.ev_baldacum_c.choice_2_result: You pay 2 silver for the old coin. The dealer lets you examine both sides before wrapping it; the storyteller tells you which part of its history he can actually trace. You keep the coin and write down its known origin.
ev.ev_baldacum_c.choice_3_result: Over two days you speak with three families and copy their names beside their memories. One points to the riverbank, another to a gate, and the third remembers only carrying her brother through smoke. You write each account clearly and leave the storyteller a copy.
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.body:
The storyteller’s daughter has brought back a page from a family near the river gate. It names an aunt who kept an old coin in her sewing box, though no one remembers who first gave it to her. The daughter lays the page beside the storyteller’s coin. ‘She should have her name written down,’ she says. ‘It was her box for years.’

His daughter asks a visiting boatman whether his family ever used that gate. The boatman says his uncle took the river route south, toward Basra, after the siege, but the family does not agree on which night. You ask whether they have written down the uncle’s name. The daughter finds it on the back of the page and smiles; they have at least that much right.

She offers to copy the family’s names for your travel book. Her father asks you to stay a day if you want to help copy the remaining account. The boatman reaches for his tea and waits for her next question.
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_1: Ask the daughter to copy the family names
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_1_resul: The daughter copies the family’s names into your book, including the aunt who kept the coin. You thank her for checking each spelling with the boatman. Their neighbours greet you warmly when you take the completed page.
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_2: Ask the boatman about the route toward Basra
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_2_resul: The boatman names the southbound landings his family used and tells you where a traveller can change boats. You mark Basra on your map and add his account to your notes.
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and help copy the family account
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.choice_3_resul: You spend the day copying names and letting each visitor check the line about their family. By evening the daughter has a clean page to keep; the people at the tea house thank you for the care you took.
ev.ev_baldacum_c_followup.title: The Coin and the Family Name
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.body:
The customs clerk catches up with you near the river gate, carrying the second paper he promised to show you. It lists two crates under the same boatman’s mark. He has checked the crates, and only one belongs to that family. ‘If I copy this as it stands, his sister will be asked to pay for a stranger’s goods,’ he says.

The boatman arrives with his sister. She takes one look at the mark and points to a small stroke that should not be there. ‘That is the other driver’s sign,’ she tells the clerk. He asks her to name someone at the gate who can confirm it. She knows two guards, but neither is on this shift. You ask whether the paper can wait. The clerk says he must finish the register before dusk.

He writes down the two guards’ names on a scrap for you and says they may help if you want to take it over. His pen hovers above the list while the sister checks the last crate herself.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the guards’ names and ask who can confirm the mark
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.choice_1_re: You take the scrap and ask at the river gate. A porter knows the two guards and tells you when one will return. The clerk keeps the disputed crate off the family’s bill until you can check.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the clerk and leave the matter with the family
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.choice_2_re: You thank the clerk and leave the paper with the boatman’s sister. She says she will bring the right driver back before the register closes. The clerk nods and returns to his desk.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_a.title: The Clerk’s Second List
One of the river gate guards comes off duty with the porter you met. He knows the other driver’s mark because he helped unload the same crates that morning. The clerk asks him to point to the stroke that distinguishes it from the boatman’s mark. The guard does, then asks the sister whether she has eaten since the first boat arrived.

‘Not yet,’ she says, keeping a hand on the disputed crate. Her brother offers to bring bread while the clerk corrects the list. You ask whether the guard is willing to put his name beneath the correction. ‘I am,’ he replies, ‘after I see both crates once more.’ They walk together down the line, and the clerk carries the wet original beside a clean sheet.

The boatman returns with bread. His sister takes it, finally letting go of the crate. The guard is ready to confirm the mark before dusk; if you stay another day, the clerk can introduce you to the other people who use this landing.
Ask the guard to confirm the mark now

You walk the line with the guard. He confirms the mark, the clerk corrects the bill, and the boatman’s sister thanks you with her mouth full of bread. You carry the corrected note as proof of what was settled.
Stay a day and meet the landing workers

You stay a day while the clerk introduces you to the porters and boatmen. By evening the list is corrected, the crates have gone to their owners, and you know whom to ask if another cargo mark puzzles you.
The Guard Who Knew the Crate
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.body:
Near sunset, the boatman who brought you news draws a line in the dust with the end of his oar. His younger brother was due to come upriver today, but the boat has not arrived. ‘It may be waiting where the channel shallows,’ he says. His wife brings a lamp and asks whether he has heard any word from the next landing.

You ask how far south the river carries cargo. He names the places he knows, including Basra, then marks the bend where heavy boats sometimes wait for water. His wife leans over the drawing. ‘You have put the old sandbar back,’ she says. ‘The last flood moved it.’ He rubs out the line and asks her where she saw the new one.

A boy from the landing comes with a message: the missing boat stopped to mend a rope, and everyone aboard is safe. The boatman laughs at himself, then offers to draw the route clearly for you before the lamp burns low.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.choice_1: Ask him to draw the river route
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.choice_1_re: The boatman draws the main channel and his wife adds the new sandbar. You copy their marks before the lamp burns out; the boy carries the message on to the next family.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.choice_2: Thank them and decide on the river later
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.choice_2_re: You thank the family and leave them to welcome the younger brother when his boat arrives. The boatman folds his rough drawing; he says to ask again when you have a sailing date, because the water will keep changing.
ev.ev_baldacum_consequence_b.title: The Boatman’s Water Line
While you are finishing the sketch, the boatman’s younger brother reaches the landing with the rope he stopped to mend. His sister-in-law asks him whether the new sandbar is where she drew it. ‘Closer to the southern bank,’ he says, and lays the damp rope beside their sketch. He wants to sleep before unloading but agrees to check your copy first.

You show him the route. He points out a place where light boats can stop and heavy ones should keep moving. His older brother asks whether this is the same advice he gave last year. ‘Last year there was more water,’ the younger man says. His wife offers him breakfast and reminds both brothers that travellers need the date of the observation, not just the shape of the river.

You write the date beside the bend. One brother will let you carry a copy for the next boatman; the other will stay a day to compare the older notes with today’s water.
Carry the updated river note onward
You carry the dated note to the next boatman. He compares it with the level at his landing and keeps the changed sandbar in mind. Back at the family’s boat, the brothers finally sit down to eat.
Stay a day and compare the older notes
You spend a day comparing the old drawings with the brothers’ fresh observations. Their sister-in-law adds dates to the pages; you leave knowing which marks belong to this season’s water.
ev.ev_baldacum_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days at the desk while the clerk checks the cargo marks and copies your name. The boatman’s sister helps you identify the river landings, and you mark Baghdad on your map. Before you leave, the clerk asks you to look at a second paper.
ev.ev_baldacum_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day with the river workers and the old keeper, writing down what each remembers of the channels and former palace wing. The keeper shows you a surviving tile; you keep the visit in your travel notes. Near evening a boatman comes with fresh news of the water.
ev.ev_baldacum_entry.choice_3_result: You spend the day checking the merchant bundle, then pay 146 silver for the Damascus steel. The merchant and clerk count it together; the boatman’s sister shows you where to record the lot in your travel book.
ev.ev_baldacum_geomancy_court.choice_1_r: You lay out the figures with the sand-reader at the courtyard gate. His daughter watches your hand, then asks what question you had in mind. You finish the reading together.
ev.ev_baldacum_geomancy_court.choice_2_r: You thank the reader and continue along the lane. His daughter smooths the sand for the next visitor while he answers her question about a crooked line.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_bazi.choice_1_resu: You pay 100 silver and study with the traveller for twenty-one days. His niece makes you copy the four pillars yourself; the boatman sometimes comes by with fresh river news for your practice. When the course ends, the teacher promises to show you his own calendar before you leave.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_bazi.choice_2_resu: You pay 80 silver and spend ten days learning the sand figures from his colleague. The teacher of calendars introduces you to the other table; when you can set out the figures yourself, the sand-reader asks you to return for one more exercise.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_bazi.choice_3_resu: The traveller shows you how he writes the boat’s possible departure days beside the four pillars, then points to the latest message from the pilot. You record his explanation and leave the niece to correct the calendar.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.body:
The calendar teacher is preparing to move his books to another room before the river air dampens them. His niece has laid the pages in sunlight and asks which one he promised to show you. He finds a sheet covered with notes from boatmen, including the pilot who changed his loading time during your lessons.

‘This mark is not a prediction,’ the niece says, pointing to a stain. ‘That is where you spilled tea.’ Her uncle laughs and gives you a cleaner page with the four pillars drawn in the margin. You ask when boats normally travel south toward Basra. He asks the returning boatman instead of guessing; the man names the landings he used last season and where he stopped for fresh water.

The teacher offers you a copy of the calendar page. His niece is also sorting a stack of older notes and would welcome help for a day. The boatman waits by the door in case you need the southern route explained again.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.choice_1: Accept a copy of the calendar page
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.choice_1_: The niece makes you a clean copy. The teacher checks the four pillars in the margin and hands it over; you keep the page with your notes from the course.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.choice_2_: The boatman names the downstream landings toward Basra while the teacher’s niece marks them beside the dates. You add Basra to your map and write down both the route and what you learned at the table.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.choice_3: Spend a day helping sort the older notes
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.choice_3_: You spend the day sorting river notes by date. The niece finally finds the boatman’s missing sheet, and the teacher thanks you before the books are carried indoors. The family speaks well of your help.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_followup.title: A Date in the Traveller’s Calendar
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_geomancy.choice_1_: You pay 80 silver and study the sand figures for ten days. The reader has you practise while his daughter checks that you have copied each figure correctly. On the last day he asks you to bring one question of your own.
ev.ev_baldacum_mentor_geomancy.choice_2_: The sand-reader makes one set of marks and asks you to count before he names the figure. His daughter points out where you missed a line. You record the example in your notes.
The sand-reader’s daughter is carrying a covered tray to the courtyard gate. The wind lifted yesterday’s marks before her father could copy them, so she has asked him to work under a cloth today. He raises one corner and shows you four carefully drawn lines. ‘They are easier to check when the dust stays put,’ she says.

You ask what question he set for your last exercise. He points toward the river and asks how one would plan a journey south toward Basra when the water level changes. His daughter says the boatmen know that part; she went to ask one before you arrived. The man is coming back after unloading, and her father leaves an empty space beside the figures for his answer.

He can give you a copy of the finished figures. You may also wait for the boatman’s route, or stay the day and help his daughter protect and copy each new pattern before the wind reaches the tray.
Take a copy of the finished figures
The reader copies the figures onto a small sheet while his daughter holds the cloth against the wind. You keep the page with your lessons and note what question he used.
Wait for the boatman and ask about Basra

The boatman names the river landings toward Basra and explains where the current is strongest. You mark Basra on your map; the reader’s daughter adds the boatman’s observations beside the sand figures.
Stay a day to copy the covered figures

You spend the day copying figures as the reader draws them. His daughter checks each sheet before lifting the cloth; when the wind rises again, the pages are already safely inside. They thank you for keeping pace.
ev.ev_basora_entry.choice_1_result: Nura’s son points out the path between the warehouses. You thank him, mark Basra on your map, and follow it into town.
ev.ev_basora_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day in the shade while boats come and go. By evening your strength has returned. Nura’s son draws the canal bend in the dust for you, and you add Basra to your map.
ev.ev_berrhoea_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Safiya and continue through the streets. Her father calls after her to make sure she has written the new price on every sheet. You mark Aleppo on your map as you leave.
ev.ev_berrhoea_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Safiya. She takes you past the water place, the bread ovens, and the sellers whose letters go farthest. One of them has a brother near Trebizond; Safiya asks him to repeat the stopping places on the northward road. By evening you have marked Aleppo, Trebizond, and the route between them on your map. Safiya goes back to her stall with the revised price list, and you depart the next morning.
ev.ev_bethleem_entry.choice_1_result: You ask Yona to show you the road. He sets down the peel and walks you to the edge of the path so you can see the next fork. Lina calls him back to taste a loaf, and he answers her. You continue on your way and mark Bethlehem on your map.
ev.ev_bethleem_entry.choice_2_result:
You spend the day by the oven. That afternoon Lina remembers to turn the tray. Every loaf comes out evenly coloured. She offers one to her father. Yona breaks it open and tastes it. “Done right through. These are ready for the travellers.”

At dusk they invite you and a few passersby to share warm bread, olives, and soup. Lina breaks her burnt loaf from the morning and finishes it with the soup. You sleep on one of the pallets they lend to travellers and leave the next morning with your strength restored. You mark Bethlehem on your map.
ev.ev_bochara_battuta_a.choice_1_result: The seller takes you along the surviving wall and shows you which rooms people remember as part of the school. You spend the day listening to her family and neighbours; they remember that you took an interest in their quarter.
ev.ev_bochara_battuta_a.choice_2_result: The neighbour tells the blacksmith story as a tale he cannot verify. He then spends the day describing the caravan stops toward Samarkand, where he once sent melons. You mark that city and its road on your map.
ev.ev_bochara_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You pay 0.4 silver for a fresh piece of melon and eat it beneath the shade. The seller fixes the last corner of the cloth while her father cuts another slice for himself. You leave with more strength for the road.
ev.ev_bochara_entry.choice_1_result: The dyer’s daughter steps aside to let you pass and calls after you to check your water before the next stretch. You mark Bukhara on your map and carry on.
ev.ev_bochara_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day resting near the yard. By supper, the daughter has retied all six rolls, and the neighbour’s son has brought his family’s bundle. You regain your strength and mark Bukhara on your map.
ev.ev_cabul_entry.choice_1_result: The cobbler’s daughter shows you the road out of the yard before returning to her stitching. You mark Kabul on your map and continue.
ev.ev_cabul_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day resting in the yard and regain your strength. At supper the driver is wearing his repaired boots and offers you a place beside the fire. You mark Kabul on your map.
ev.ev_cabul_site_gap.choice_1_result: She draws the branch she trusts and names its water stop. You mark the route toward Taican on your map while the driver checks the straps on his boots again.
ev.ev_cabul_site_gap.choice_2_result: You watch him roll damp wool and stitch it above the leather sole. His daughter tests the driver’s fit once more; you record the craft and understand why each layer has its place.
ev.ev_cacanfu_entry.choice_1_result: The daughter finishes moving the silk to the shelf while her father sends the broker to the grain owner. She points out the street beyond the quay. You follow it across town, knowing where to return if you need the canal landing.
ev.ev_cacanfu_entry.choice_2_result: You stay another day. The daughter brings you through the market, asks two sellers to show how they store silk clear of damp sacks, and takes you back by a different lane. Her father shows you the canal branch on his route board before you leave.
ev.ev_cachanfu_entry.choice_1_result: The sister points out the lane through town while her brother finishes a sound knot in the bamboo rope. The ginger trader waits for the ferryman rather than stepping onto a full boat. You follow the lane and remember where the river landing lies.
ev.ev_cachanfu_entry.choice_2_result: You stay another day. The sister takes the finished rope to the river and introduces you to the ferryman, who shows where people wait while cargo is loaded. She then walks you past the ginger stalls and back through the town gate.
ev.ev_caffa_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Arslan and move on. Sada calls after you to say there are seven and a half apples now, because she has eaten her half. You mark Caffa and the shore road on your map.
ev.ev_caffa_entry.choice_2_result: You stay at Arslan's shelter for the day. He shows you where the carts gather, while Sada makes you count the apples twice to prove she has not hidden any. They share supper and give you a place to sleep. You leave the next morning stronger and mark Caffa on your map.
ev.ev_caffa_mentor_runes.choice_1_result: You pay and learn the runes. You pay 5000 coins. You spend 7 days learning the art. You can now read it on any road. A mark is set on this affair.
ev.ev_caffa_mentor_runes.choice_2_result: You ask what Raidho names on this quay. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_caiju_entry.choice_1_result: The daughter reads the corrected count back to the clerk. The porters lift the last sacks off the embankment, giving the waiting cart room to pass. The boat owner points out the street beyond the landing, and you continue through Caiju.
ev.ev_caiju_entry.choice_2_result: You stay another day. The daughter walks you past the warehouses and along the high road above the water, then introduces you to a boatman who knows the onward channel. She keeps the corrected cargo sheet dry beneath her arm.
ev.ev_cail_a.choice_1_result: You spend a day at the landing. The groom asks you to keep a clear space while each horse comes down, then shows you how he checks its legs on dry ground. He names the road toward Melibar when he hears where you may travel next. As the last horse settles, the broker invites you to the stable for another talk.
ev.ev_cail_a.choice_2_result: You pay the western merchant for a horse after the groom has walked it in front of you. He checks the tag and hands you the lead rope. The broker explains why horses arriving from across the sea command such a price and offers to introduce you to the stablekeeper.
ev.ev_cail_a.choice_3_result: The boatman points out the coast toward Coilum and the longer passage toward Samara. He asks which ship you came on, then shows how departure depends on wind and cargo. You leave with a better idea of the harbours named by sailors here.
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.body: The broker calls you to the stable after the landed horses have had water. A groom is showing a younger animal how to walk between the stalls. “He needs a little space,” the groom says when a buyer crowds its shoulder. The broker asks you to move the folded cloth that blocks the passage. Once the path is clear, he turns to a younger horse, recently landed and not yet trained for a long road and lets you inspect its lead rope and hooves. Another merchant is waiting with a route sheet. “If you're leaving without a horse,” he says, “I can still show you the roads toward Melibar and Coilum.” A sailor at the door joins in, naming Samara as a port farther across the water. The groom asks them all to lower their voices until the young animal finishes its turn; only then does the broker resume his offers. The sailor points to a worn place on the route sheet where many hands have traced the same crossing.
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay the broker for the horse after the groom walks it before you. The groom checks the lead rope and asks you to let the animal drink once more before travel. The broker hands you its tag and explains how to care for it on the next stretch.
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.choice_2_result: The merchant marks Melibar and Coilum on the route sheet and tells you which road the land carriers use. The groom looks over his shoulder and confirms the first turn outside town. You leave with the coast and both ports clearer in mind.
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day helping at the stable
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day carrying water and keeping the passage clear while the horses settle. A sailor waiting for his cargo tells the groom about Samara beyond the sea. The groom repeats the name to you and shows how he judges whether a newly landed horse is ready for a longer road.
ev.ev_cail_a_followup.title: Cail: At the Stable after Landing
ev.ev_cail_b.choice_1_result: You wait two days while the steward finishes his rounds. When he comes, the niece demonstrates that the cloth's colour holds in water. He signs the seller's receipt and thanks the people who kept the order ready. The seller introduces you, and the steward remembers your patience.
ev.ev_cail_b.choice_2_result: The seller tells you how people in the market speak of brothers of a royal household and the harbours associated with their family. The broker adds the roads toward Melibar and Coilum, correcting a turn in the older man's account. You leave with the story as the merchants tell it, and with both ports in mind.
ev.ev_cail_b.choice_3_result: You pay for a full bolt of fine cotton cloth. The niece folds it with the finished side inside and ties it for travel. Her uncle introduces you to the next buyer in line, who thanks you for leaving the display clear, and the market's cloth sellers remember the exchange.
ev.ev_cail_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You spend the three days before the boat is ready helping the family sort food, water and bedding. The daughter marks each skin so her mother can find it without lifting the packs. When the boat is ready, the older pilgrim thanks you in front of the harbour families and invites you to hear their account if you meet again.
ev.ev_cail_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You stay for a day at the landing. A boatman who has made the crossing from Maabar shows the daughter where the water is loaded and traces the route for you on a board. Her mother checks the pole once more; this time she can reach her skin without shifting the bedding.
ev.ev_cail_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You pay the gem trader for the ruby. He shows you its weight and wraps it while the pilgrims finish loading. The daughter asks whether you bought it for a traveller; you say you will decide where to take it later. She wishes you a safe journey before joining her mother on the boat.
ev.ev_cail_entry.choice_1_result: The cotton seller points you past the horse yard to the road onward. The groom thanks her for the leaves and leads the animal away from the crowded stall. You leave with the turns through Cail clear in mind.
ev.ev_cail_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at the market. The groom shows you where newly landed horses are watered; the cotton seller introduces a buyer who brings cloth down to the ships. Their talk gives you a feel for the goods and streets of Cail before you leave.
ev.ev_cail_entry.choice_3_result: You leave your shoes at the shrine entrance and follow the attendant's directions around a family carrying offerings. Afterwards she points out the lane back toward the horse market. She thanks you for giving the family room and remembers you when you pass again.
ev.ev_cail_entry.choice_4_result: A traveller who came this way tells of the mountain of Serendib, of chains and iron pins and the eleven-span foot-mark; his tale sets you on the pilgrims' road, and he promises the rest at the harbour.
ev.ev_calatu_a.choice_1_result: You spend a day on the wall while ships enter the harbour. The assistant erases his mistaken arrival mark and writes each vessel in the order it ties up. The watchman shows you the turn across the gulf toward Ormus, and later asks you to join him for a closer look at the shipping records.
ev.ev_calatu_a.choice_2_result: You pay the merchant for a bag of pepper after the clerk checks its mark. She has the porter sew a loose corner before handing it over. The watchman tells you why ships bring spices here on their way inland and invites you to look over his harbour list.
ev.ev_calatu_a.choice_3_result: The assistant points to the vessels preparing for the Dufar coast, correcting himself when one turns toward another berth. The watchman explains how to distinguish a ship still waiting outside from one ready to depart. You leave with a better sense of the harbour's movements.
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.body: The watchman calls you to the wall again when the next ship ties up. His assistant has made a fresh harbour list, and the pepper merchant is waiting to see whether her cargo has arrived. “Read the mark first,” the watchman tells him. The boy squints at the painted boards on the quay and finds the right one. The merchant gives him a smile and asks whether the road toward Camadi is busy this week. “Ask the caravan master below,” the watchman says. “I can tell you which boats have come in; he knows the inland wells.” The caravan master joins them with a packet of pepper for sale. As he and the merchant talk, the watchman traces Ormus across the gulf and Dufar along the coast for you. The assistant puts a pebble on each name so the wind will not fold the map.
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay the caravan master for a sealed bag of pepper. The merchant checks the seam with you and makes him replace a worn tag. The watchman tells you which ship brought this cargo before it passed to the inland buyer.
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the caravan master about Camadi
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.choice_2_result: The caravan master names the stopping places toward Camadi and marks the point where the road leaves the coast. The assistant copies the turn beside his harbour list. You compare the two and leave with a clearer picture of the inland route.
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day following the harbour list
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day with the assistant, matching the ships on the water to the names on his list. A sailor explains which one will sail toward Ormus and which must first call at Dufar. By evening the assistant no longer confuses the high stern with a ship that has already docked.
ev.ev_calatu_a_followup.title: Calatu: The Watchman’s Second List
ev.ev_calatu_b.choice_1_result: The guard shows you the grain tallies kept for the wall and names Ormus across the gulf. He tells you how the harbour could shelter people arriving from there, then asks the young porter to read today's reserve aloud. The porter gets it right, and the guard sends him to help his sister at the quay.
ev.ev_calatu_b.choice_2_result: You buy a small serving of dates from the seller's boat and eat them beside the quay. She puts the rest of her stock beneath the storehouse awning. The guard explains why arriving food goes first into the town's count; after the meal you feel ready to continue.
ev.ev_calatu_b.choice_3_result: The guard opens the storehouse map. He shows where caravans turn toward Camadi and where the coastal road continues toward Dufar. The porter copies both names onto a scrap for you, then asks his sister to check the spelling before you leave.
ev.ev_calatu_entry.choice_1_result: The grain seller points you through the street behind her stall. Her son is still reading names from the board as she hands out the sacks. You continue with Calatu's harbour and town lanes fixed in mind.
ev.ev_calatu_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the stalls. The fisherman collects his household's grain, and the grain seller introduces you to the date seller and the porters who keep the town supplied. By evening you know which lane reaches the wall and where the food boats unload.
ev.ev_calatu_entry.choice_3_result: You leave your shoes at the mosque door and wait until the attendant shows you where visitors may sit. Afterwards he walks you back to the wall. The grain seller recognizes you from the harbour and thanks you for treating the gathering with care.
ev.ev_camadi_a.choice_1_result: You spend the day with Banu among the old walls. She names the families who once lived there and points toward Kerman beyond the plain. You mark it on your map and write her account in your travel book. She asks you to return if you want to hear more.
ev.ev_camadi_a.choice_2_result: You pay 1.2 silver for a small bag of dates. Banu’s grandson ties it shut while she tells you which grove produced the fruit. You eat some on the road and feel refreshed. You note the grove in your travel book, and Banu invites you back to hear more about the old street.
ev.ev_camadi_a.choice_3_result: The caravan people show you where the road reaches Cobinan. You mark the town on your map and write down how the old conflicts changed their stopping places. Their practical advice makes you more confident about the next journey.
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.body:
Banu spreads a worn cloth under her palm and draws the old quarter as she remembers it. Her grandson adds the well and the house they live in now. ‘That part is your map,’ she tells him.

She has a caravan lot of dates ready to sell to traders at a fixed price. You can buy the lot, ask her how travellers reach Hormuz and take ship toward Calatu, or stay a day and help the boy put the family’s names in the right places on the cloth.

The boy puts his finger on a blank space in the cloth. ‘Who lived here?’ Banu names a baker and then remembers his daughter has a stall by the present market. You ask whether she will show the daughter this drawing. ‘When it is finished,’ she says. ‘She may remember where her father kept the oven.’ Another trader arrives to ask about the date lot but has not agreed to buy it. Banu looks up at you and asks whether you want to discuss the price first.
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the caravan lot of dates for 108 silver
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 108 silver for the caravan lot of dates. Banu’s grandson checks the bundles in front of you and ties them firmly. You record the exchange and her family’s story in your travel book.
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_2: Ask Banu about the road to Calatu
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_2_result: Banu names the wells on the inland road to Hormuz and says sailors there can take you onward to Calatu. You mark the town on your map and write down what she remembers of the route.
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to finish the family map
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day listening and writing names beside the boy’s drawing. Banu’s family thanks you for helping preserve it, and people in Camadi come to know you through them.
ev.ev_camadi_a_followup.title: A Map under Banu’s Palm
ev.ev_camadi_b.choice_1_result: You spend the day in the shade, sharing water and stories with the travellers. You write down what you learned about the heat of this plain. They remember you kindly when the party moves on.
ev.ev_camadi_b.choice_2_result: Banu shows you the inland road toward Hormuz, where ships continue across the gulf toward Calatu, and the road back to Kerman. You mark both towns on your map and record her directions in your travel book.
ev.ev_camadi_b.choice_3_result: You pay 108 silver for the merchant bale of cotton cloth. Banu’s neighbour wraps it against the dust, and the other stallholders greet you as a familiar trader.
ev.ev_camadi_entry.choice_1_result: Banu’s grandson points you toward the road out. You mark Camadi on your map and continue.
ev.ev_camadi_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day tasting fruit and talking with the stallholders. You write down what you learned in your travel book and mark Camadi on your map.
ev.ev_camadi_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the mosque courtyard and speak with people resting there. One offers you a small keepsake from the town. They greet you warmly when you leave, and you mark Camadi on your map.
ev.ev_cambaet_entry.choice_1_result: The apprentice steps aside so you can pass beneath the cloth. At the far end of the lane he points out the road beyond the market. “Come back when the cloth is dry,” he says, returning to his line. You continue with the town's turns clear in mind.
ev.ev_cambaet_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day walking the stalls with the dyer. She introduces the cotton seller who buys her offcuts and the porter who carries finished cloth to the water. When the merchant returns, he recognizes his sister's two blue threads on the bundle. You leave with the neighbourhood's trades and paths in mind.
ev.ev_cambaet_site_gap.choice_1_result: The dyer takes you to the corner where carts leave for Semenat and points out the road marker she uses for deliveries. “Ask at the next water stop before taking a side track,” she says. You trace the turn on your map while the apprentice carries his basin back to the yard.
ev.ev_cambaet_site_gap.choice_2_result: You help rinse and spread the cloth. The streaks remain near the old fold, so the apprentice opens the whole length before his aunt returns it to the vat. She shows you how to judge the dried edge and gives him the task of checking the next batch himself.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a.choice_1_result: You present yourself at the Kaan's court with your gifts, and the chamberlain receives them with practiced courtesy. He measures you as he speaks, and when the audience ends he makes you a small sign to stay.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a.choice_2_result: You stand before the great hall and measure its size with your eyes until it overwhelms you. The palace of the Kaan is now marked in your book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a.choice_3_result: The Kaan's guards speak of the empire's breadth: a road runs from this gate to the city of Kinsay, where the Kaan's granaries never empty. Its name is now on your map.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.body: A chamberlain of the Kaan's household finds you as you leave the shadow of the great hall. He has served at three feasts beneath those painted beams and can read a guest's worth by the way he stands. He does not ask what you saw; he asks what you mean to carry away from the hall. The court, he says, keeps tokens for travellers it intends to remember.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_1: Take the cord of the hall's own silk the chamberlain offers
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_1_resul: The chamberlain knots a cord of vermilion silk about your wrist, the same silk that hangs in the great hall. In Cambaluc the knot is known; those who see it will know you stood where the Kaan holds his feasts.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which road the envoys take when they leave for the south
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_2_resul: The chamberlain draws the road the envoys ride southward, past Kinsay, marking the post-stations where horses are changed. The way to Kinsay is now clear on your map, and you know how the Kaan's word travels.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_3: Promise to speak well of the great hall in the cities ahead
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.choice_3_resul: The chamberlain accepts your promise and asks nothing else. In Cambaluc your word now carries weight among those who heard you give it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_a_followup.title: Cambaluc: The Chamberlain's Token
ev.ev_cambaluc_b.choice_1_result: You buy silk in the suburb at the Cambaluc price, and the counting-house keeper watches the transaction with sharp eyes. When the bolt is wrapped, he motions you inside to a quieter chamber.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b.choice_2_result: You spend a day counting the cart-loads of silk that enter the city. By evening the tally is beyond counting, and the city's hunger for silk is in your book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b.choice_3_result: You visit the public granaries and find them full in a year when no one goes hungry. The men who keep them remember your interest.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.body: The keeper of a counting-house in the suburbs calls you over from his abacus, where the day's carts are being tallied. He has seen your face among the thousand cart-loads of silk, and he knows which travellers understand the city's measure. He does not sell you his silence; he offers what the suburbs sell to those who ask the right questions.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_1: Buy a bolt of silk at the price written in his ledger
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_1_resul: The keeper sells you a bolt of silk at his own list price, no bargaining and no tricks. The cloth is real, the price fair, and the suburb lets you leave with it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_2: Ask him to draw the road the northern carts come by
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_2_resul: The keeper draws the road the northern carts take to the twelve suburbs, marking the watering places and the toll-houses. The way to Chandu is now on your map, and you know what the north sends south.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and count cart-loads with the tally-men
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.choice_3_resul: You spend a day at the counting-house, learning how the suburbs are numbered in silk and pepper and grain. It costs you time, but the measure of Cambaluc stays with you when you go.
ev.ev_cambaluc_b_followup.title: Cambaluc: The Counting-House Keeper
ev.ev_cambaluc_c.choice_1_result: You walk among the transplanted trees of the green hill, where cedars brought from the south shade the jade terraces. A gardener tending the roots looks up at your footsteps and sets down his spade.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c.choice_2_result: You climb the hill at sunset and see the whole city at once — the palace, the market, the relay stations, all below one roof of light. The sight settles in you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c.choice_3_result: The gardeners who water the trees by hand speak of the summer palace at Chandu, a day's ride north. Its name is now on your map, and their craft is in your book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.body: On the lower slope of the mountain of green jade, the oldest of the thousand gardeners sets down his buckets and waves you over. He watered these trees when they were carried in on the backs of elephants, and he has climbed this hill every day since. He does not forbid you the mountain; he asks only that you understand what it cost to raise it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_1: Ask him how a tree can be moved without knowing it
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_1_resul: The gardener shows you the wet earth bound in silk about the roots, and the way the diggers take a tree whole in winter. The art of the green hill is now written in your travel book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_2: Ask him to draw the road the trees came by from the north
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_2_resul: The gardener draws the road the trees came by from the forests of the north, past Chandu, marking the passes and the places where the elephants rested. The way to Chandu is now on your map, and you know what a mountain is made of.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_3: Take up a bucket and help water the trees for a day
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.choice_3_resul: You climb the hill with a shoulder-pole and buckets, learning the gardeners' pace and their water. The gardeners of Cambaluc remember that you helped, and the hill keeps a part of you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_c_followup.title: Cambaluc: The Gardener of the Green Hill
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.body: The first answer does not end at the gate. A clerk of the relay stations draws you aside and asks what you intend to carry away from Cambaluc. Beyond the question lies the palace gate and the relay stations; he offers to set a name to your name, the name of a courier who reads the roads of the empire. Choose what you will make of the sign.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the name and ask the relay clerk who can vouch for it
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.choice_1_re: You take the name the clerk offers and ask who can vouch for it. He names two relay masters, and the matter opens again.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the relay clerk and keep your own counsel
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.choice_2_re: You thank the clerk and keep your own counsel. The matter closes at the relay station, and nothing more is asked of you in Cambaluc.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_a.title: Cambaluc: The Mark at the Gate
You have agreed to carry the relay's seal with you — the name of a courier who reads the roads of the empire. It will not decide the whole journey, but at the next relay station his name may win you a fresh horse.
Send the seal on before nightfall
You send the seal on before nightfall. The courier's word now travels with your name, and the relay stations have a reason to receive you.
Keep the seal in your travel book
You keep the seal in your travel book and spend a day setting it down plainly. The record is made; the favour waits for a road that may never call on it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_b.body: The answer sends a rumour along the road. Before the day is out, a guard of the granaries finds you at the gate with a second account of the palace gate and the relay stations — how the couriers count their days, and who reads the road ahead. It is less grand than a traveller's tale, and more useful.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_b.choice_1_re: You follow the guard's practical advice and ask him to set it down. He writes the account out for you, and the road's true measures come into your hand.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the account with the guard
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_b.choice_2_re: You leave the account with the guard and keep your own counsel. It goes back to the granary gate, and Cambaluc asks nothing more of you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_consequence_b.title: Cambaluc: The Road Behind the Answer
You have chosen to carry the guard's account with you — how the couriers count their days, and who reads the road. It will not decide the whole journey, but it will keep you on the swift road among the slow ones.
Pass the couriers' count before nightfall
You pass the couriers' count to the next rider before nightfall. The road's measures now travel ahead of you, and where they land, your name follows.
Keep the couriers' schedule in your travel book
You spend a day copying the couriers' schedule into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_1_result: The clerks of the shìbó sī write your cargo into the great register and hand you the tally. As you turn from the table, a clerk of the relay stations rises to ask a word with you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_2_result: The men of Cambaluc answer you freely, for the city is proud of its size and its roads. Their answers are many and different, and one of them follows you out of the gate to give you the truer account.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day walking the great market of Cambaluc and carry away a load of goods. The market of the Great Kaan's city is now written in your book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.body: The chronologer of the Astronomical Bureau does not let you leave with only his lessons. He draws the yarrow-stalks once more, this time for the road ahead of you, and reads what season it will be open and where a man must stand when he chooses it. Then he sets the reading down between you and leaves the rest to your choosing.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take his parting notes on reading a road by time and position
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_1_: The notes are plain and exact, like the man himself. What you learned at the Bureau is now written where you can consult it on the road.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask which road the hexagrams show to be open in the season ahead
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_2_: The chronologer reads the hexagrams and names the road south, the road by which the Kaan's envoys ride to Kinsay. The way is now clear in your mind, and you know the season in which to take it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_3: Linger a day at the Bureau to learn the reading of the seasons
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_3_: You spend a day among the Bureau's instruments, learning how the year is read and the roads ordered. It costs you time, but the hexagrams now have a reader who knows where he stands.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.title: Cambaluc: The Chronologer's Parting Hexagram
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_iching.choice_1_re: The chronologer of the Astronomical Bureau takes your fee and opens his hand. The fourteen days' teaching begins with the first cast, and before you leave he has a parting hexagram to lay before you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_iching.choice_2_re: The chronologer shows how each hexagram names a turn in the road. The six-and-forty signs are now written in your book, though their reading stays with him.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_1_result: You watch the governor's clerks at their tally. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Caracoron opens on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_2_result: You bargain with desert caravans for tea. You pay 6000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_3_result: You pass through the government quarter without delay. The road to Etzina opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.body: In the capital of Tangut a clerk of the governor's court who has sealed caravan papers for twenty years draws you from the market into a side room. He says Caracoron and Etzina are not merely names on a map — they are the measure of how far a Tangut passport will carry you before the desert takes over.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_1: Ask him to seal a note naming the road to Caracoron
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_1_resul: Caracoron is marked on your map with the clerk's seal beside it. The northern road is no longer a rumour.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_2: Buy a chest of tea at the court caravan price
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_2_resul: You leave with tea at a price the desert caravans accept. The chest is sealed for the next march.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_3: Wait a day for the passport office to open again
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You wait a day for the office. The waiting costs time, but Etzina is named before you go.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.title: Campichu: The Tangut Seat's Second Counsel
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_1_result: You enter one of the three Christian churches. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_2_result: You walk the idol abbeys and note their gilded figures. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Egrigaia opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_3_result: You leave a small offering at an abbey gate. You pay 500 coins. Your name carries a little more weight here now. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. The road to Campichu opens on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Campichu on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_3_result: You enter the sì and bow before the painted scrolls. The monks remember your courtesy, and the scent of incense lingers in your sleeves. You set the road to Campichu on your map.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_1_result: You walk the gardens with Nuri’s brother. By evening both families have agreed on a shorter turn and he moves the gate as promised. You write down how the channels are shared and spend the day in Hami.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_2_result: You pay 0.6 silver for a slice, eat it beside the baskets, and feel refreshed. Nuri wraps the remaining pieces for the children while the two families settle their water turn.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_3_result: The drivers point out the roads toward Lop and Suzhou, then show where each party usually fills its water skins. You mark the two places on your map.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.body:
At Nuri’s stall, she and her brother are tying a full merchant load of melons for the next caravan. The neighbours have finished their water turn, and the child who carried the cut melon is drawing small marks on each basket so her mother can identify her family’s share. Nuri checks each knot before the driver loads it.

‘You used to mix these baskets up,’ Nuri tells the child. ‘I can read the marks now,’ the girl replies. You ask where the caravan will go. The driver names Lop and Suzhou and shows a worn list of wells; another party is waiting for news from Etzina. Nuri says the full load is available for 108 silver. The driver warns that this is trade cargo, not a snack for the road.

The child hands her mother’s basket over first. You can buy Nuri’s merchant lot, ask her and the driver to go through the wells with you, or stay a day for the eastbound party to arrive and ask them about Etzina.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the full merchant load for 108 silver
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 108 silver for the full load. Nuri’s brother counts the baskets with you and the driver makes room for them. You write down the water turns and packing method you learned, ready for the next desert stretch.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_2: Ask them to name the wells toward Lop and Suzhou
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_2_result: Nuri holds the paper while the driver names the usable wells toward Lop and Suzhou. You mark both destinations and record where a party can refill before crossing the dry ground.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_3: Wait a day for the eastbound party
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_3_result: You wait through the next day. The arriving driver tells you what he saw toward Etzina, and Nuri shares tea while you draw that place on your map. The girl asks him whether he noticed her basket marks on the road.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.title: Nuri’s Packed Melons
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_1_result: You stay through the day. The keeper explains where he learned the old story and how his family looks after travellers now. His nephew finishes mending the mat and invites you to sit; you record their account.
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_2_result: You watch the gathering without interrupting. The woman brings her father another cup of tea and thanks you for moving his stool; the keepers remember your courtesy. You note what you saw in the courtyard.
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_3_result: The keeper spends the day asking a returning driver about water and shelter toward Etzina. He then tells you what the driver knows, and you mark Etzina on your map.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_1_result: The girl shows you the newly marked water skin before you leave. You mark Hami on your map and continue with your own water checked.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at the market. The seller tells you how water reaches the gardens; drivers tell you where they stop between the oasis and the desert. You record what you learn and mark Hami on your map.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the place of worship and speak with the people who sweep its courtyard. One of them guides you back to the main lane; you mark Hami on your map, and the family remembers that you came respectfully.
ev.ev_caracoron_entry.choice_1_result: The carpenter’s sister names the road beyond the wagon yard. Her son points out the gate his grandmother still calls by its old name. You mark Caracoron on your map and go on.
ev.ev_caracoron_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day while the family repairs wagons and compares old and new street names. The boy takes the finished cart to his grandmother, then returns to show you the market gate. You add the city and their accounts to your book.
ev.ev_caracoron_site_gap.choice_1_result: Altan names the stopping places toward Camul and the ground where the herds find pasture. His daughter checks two names from her uncle’s last trip. You mark the route before they close the saddlebag.
ev.ev_caracoron_site_gap.choice_2_result: Altan shows you how to twist two strands so they hold one another. His daughter gives you the peg to keep the tension even. You learn the family’s repair method while his brother tries the mended bag.
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_1_result: You pay 0.5 silver for the melon. Rima’s daughter wraps it with leaves so it will not bruise, then asks her mother to check the channel one last time. You carry the fruit as a small provision.
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_2_result: You spend the day watching the water pass from the neighbour’s branch to Rima’s younger vines. Her daughter marks the hour with a shadow on the wall. You record what the family showed you; Rima asks you to return when the next parcel of seeds is ready.
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_3_result: You pay 1 silver for the dried grapes. The daughter checks that the cloth parcel is tied tightly, then gives you the small provision. Rima reminds her to put the next basket back in the shade.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.body:
Rima calls you back to the orchard when her daughter is sorting melon seeds for the next planting. The girl has mixed two dried batches in one bowl. ‘I marked the cloths, not the seeds,’ she admits. Rima asks her to look at their size before giving up. The neighbour who shares the water channel brings a handful from his own crop so they have something to compare.

You ask whether the varieties come from the same valley. Rima says one was brought by a driver from farther west, though she knows it now by the taste of its fruit. The neighbour talks about the mountain road to Badakhshan where his brother once carried grafts. The daughter asks him which trees survived the trip. ‘The ones he wrapped well,’ he says, showing her a folded leaf.

Rima cuts a melon she had saved for the family and offers you a piece. Her daughter spreads the seeds in two lines on clean cloth, ready to hear your guess before she checks the old labels.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_1: Accept the melon and hear how Rima kept its seed
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_1_result: Rima gives you a generous piece of melon, and her daughter compares its fresh seeds with the two dried lines. She can now separate the batches by herself. You carry away a small fruit provision and note the family’s method.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the neighbour about the Badakhshan road
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_2_result: The neighbour names the places where his brother watered the grafts on the road toward Badakhshan. Rima’s daughter writes them on the old seed label so the story stays with the batch. You mark Badakhshan on your map.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_3: Help the daughter sort seed for the neighbours
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_3_result: You help divide the seeds into labelled cloth packets. The neighbour takes his share, and Rima’s daughter keeps the remaining two rows apart this time. The family thanks you for staying until the work is done.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.title: Rima’s Seed Packet
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_1_result: You pay 116 silver for Saliha’s finished carpet. Her brother rolls it carefully, making sure the narrow corner faces out so she can check it once more. The full trading carpet joins your cargo.
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_2_result: You spend the day at Saliha’s bench. She has you try the corner on a scrap while her brother counts the turns aloud. By evening you know why their family keeps that small change in the border, and you put the lesson in your notes.
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_3_result: You pay 1.5 silver for the packet of dye samples. The aunt labels each small portion before handing it over, and Saliha warns you to keep the indigo wrapped separately. You leave with a portable sample of the family’s work.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.body:
Saliha’s aunt invites you into the dye yard, where her nephew is holding three sample threads against the light. He says the blue has dried darker than he expected. His aunt asks whether he compared it before or after washing. ‘Before,’ he says. She hands him a clean bowl and tells him to wet the thread, then wait. Saliha calls from the loom that a buyer wants another finished carpet, and the aunt has one prepared for 116 silver.

You ask how they decide which colour belongs in the narrow border. The aunt says Saliha decides after seeing the whole field of the carpet. A trader from Yarcan has brought a mineral pigment she wants to examine, though he cannot stay past tomorrow. The nephew asks whether he may try it on a scrap. His aunt agrees if he marks the source first, so nobody later mistakes it for their usual dye.

Saliha brings the carpet into the courtyard. The wet blue sample dries beside the new mineral colour, and her aunt asks what difference you see.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the finished carpet for 116 silver
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 116 silver for the other finished carpet. Saliha rolls the full trading piece and ties on a tag naming the colours she used. Her brother carries it to your load while the aunt checks the next dye bath.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the pigment trader about Yarcan
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_2_result: The pigment trader describes Yarcan, its market, and the road on which he brought the mineral. The nephew writes the place on his sample cloth; you mark Yarcan in your map. Saliha asks him to keep the wet and dry tests side by side until morning.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_3: Spend a day testing the border colours
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day at the dye yard. The aunt has you compare each thread after washing and drying; Saliha chooses the colour once the whole border is in view. You record the lesson, and the nephew keeps his labelled sample for the next order.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.title: The Aunt’s Dye Samples
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_1_result: You sit with the neighbour while he tells the story he learned at home. Mariam’s son asks which names belong to which telling, and the neighbour patiently repeats them. The people at the cave remember that you listened with respect.
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_2_result: The traveller tells you the version her father passed on, including the old coin carried to a baker after the long sleep. Mariam’s son wants to know what the coin looked like; the traveller says her father never told her. She thanks you for asking and hopes you will carry the account onward.
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_3_result: You stay a full night by the cave and help Mariam sweep in the morning. The two visitors talk until their lamps burn low, and her son finally falls asleep against the wall. At dawn he asks you which part you remember best; you answer while he gathers the last wicks.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.body:
The morning after your night at the cave, Mariam’s son has two scraps of paper on his knee. The Muslim neighbour wrote one set of names, and the Christian traveller wrote another. ‘Which one should go on the wall?’ the boy asks. Mariam tells him to ask whether either guest wants their paper displayed. Both would rather keep the sheets for visitors to read at the table, where they can answer questions.

You ask the traveller where she learned the story. Her father heard it on the eastward road, she says, and she can name the oasis of Khotan where they once stopped. The neighbour asks whether that was before or after a hard winter; the traveller cannot remember, but she recalls his hands around a warm cup as he told it. Mariam puts the papers in a small box so the lamps cannot singe them.

The boy wants to copy both lists neatly. The traveller also offers to show you the road she knows. Mariam says anyone who stays another day can help make a safe shelf for the box.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_1: Help the boy copy both lists
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_1_result: You help the boy copy both lists. He puts the names on separate sheets and leaves space below each for the visitors’ own explanations. Mariam places them in the box, and you note how the two accounts were told.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_2_result: The traveller tells you about Khotan and the resting places her family used on that road. The boy adds the city’s name to the back of her paper, and you mark Khotan on your map. Mariam closes the box before the first visitors arrive.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and make a shelf for the papers
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay a day helping Mariam fix a shelf away from the lamps. Her son tests it with the box before putting both stories inside. The two visitors thank you, and the cave’s papers will be easier for others to read safely.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.title: Names Told at the Cave
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.body:
Tariq catches up with you after your days at the relay. He has tied a fresh cord for a driver who has never taken the northern stage. ‘The last knot is where his cousin will meet him,’ he says, ‘but I only heard the place from my father.’ The driver asks whether that is enough to trust. Tariq says it is enough to ask another person, and takes the cord back rather than send him out with a guess.

You ask who keeps the next station. The yard clerk comes over with a name and shows the driver a mark that the keeper uses on receipts. Tariq repeats it aloud. A fruit seller nearby says she saw the cousin last month, repairing a harness by the water trough. The driver wants to write a short note so the cousin knows when to expect him.

Tariq asks whether you will carry a copy of the cord’s marks. The clerk puts paper on the table; she can help check every knot against the names before anyone leaves.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_1: Take a checked copy of the relay cord
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You take a copy of the knots and ask Tariq who will recognise each mark. He and the clerk name the station keepers in order. The driver writes his note to the cousin, and Tariq says he will come back when the names are set out clearly.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_2: Leave the cord with Tariq and the driver
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank Tariq and let him finish the cord with the driver. The clerk checks the last mark before they tie it off. When you leave, the driver is already repeating his cousin’s name without looking at the paper.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.title: Tariq’s Last Knot
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a_resolution.bo:
Tariq returns with the checked cord and a narrow strip of paper. His father has written the station names beside each knot. ‘He corrected my count,’ Tariq admits, showing you where one short stage was missing. The driver asked him not to erase the old mark; it will remind them both why the route had to be checked.

You ask whether the cord will survive rain. Tariq dips one end in a bowl, then lays it in the sun. The knots stay firm, while his paper curls. The clerk says to keep the names inside a dry book and use the cord outside. The driver sends word that his cousin will indeed be at the last station.

Tariq offers you the spare copy. If you leave soon, he can pass your name ahead. If you have a day, he will teach you to make the same knots and write the station names in your own hand.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a_resolution.ch: Let Tariq send your name ahead
Tariq hands the checked cord to the outgoing rider with your name attached. The clerk reads it once more before the rider leaves. Your introduction now travels ahead to the next relay.
Stay a day and copy the station names

You spend the day making knots and writing the station names. Tariq checks the short stage that he once missed; you have it in the right place. The clerk gives you a dry sleeve for the paper when the lesson is done.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.body:
After your day in Tariq’s garden, a dyer named Amina comes looking for you. She heard that his father blamed a late water turn for a pale patch on the vines. ‘My sister says the channel was clear that day,’ Amina tells you. ‘If the water arrived late, the gate farther up must have been held closed.’ She asks Tariq to bring his father’s note so they can put the days in order.

You ask why the timing matters to her dye work. Amina uses the same channel for rinsing wool after the orchards have taken their share. If the turn changes, she must keep the wet bundles another night. Tariq arrives with his father’s note: he had mixed the day of the pale patch with the day the neighbour repaired the stone. Amina laughs at herself for nearly doing the same.

She sketches the water turns on a piece of cloth and asks whether you want to carry the corrected account. Her sister can still add the precise hour when she returns from the washing yard.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_1: Wait for Amina’s sister and take the corrected account
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You ask Amina to wait for her sister’s account. The sister returns with the hour she marked on a jar, and the two women correct the cloth drawing together. Amina promises to give you a clean copy after the wool is rinsed.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the water-turn account with the dyers
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You tell Amina the account will be most useful beside her washing yard. She agrees and pins the cloth where her sister can see it. Tariq takes the corrected date back to his father before the next water turn begins.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.title: The Dyer’s Question
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b_resolution.bo:
Amina brings you a clean list after the wool has dried. Her sister has checked the hours against the jar marks, and Tariq’s father has added the orchard’s next turn. ‘I used to keep all this in my head,’ Amina says. ‘Then my nephew began helping at the dye vats, and I had to explain it so he would know when to draw water.’ The nephew is behind her, reading the list aloud to prove he understands.

You ask whether the water schedule changes in winter. It does, she says, and she has left a blank line for that. Tariq’s father will write again when the season turns. Her nephew points out a smudge on the lower edge; Amina dries it with a cloth rather than rub it away.

She slides a copy toward you. Her nephew keeps his finger on the first line and asks whether he should read it aloud once more.

The sister arrives with a rinsed bundle under one arm and checks the copied hour against the mark on her jar. She points out one line where the nephew has written the time too small; he makes the letters larger before handing you the page.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Carry the corrected water list to other travellers
You take Amina’s clean copy. Her nephew reads the first line once more, and she lets him write the family name beneath it. The corrected schedule is now in your care for the road.
Spend a day checking the channel turns

You spend the day following the channel between orchard and washing yard. Amina’s nephew marks each turn as it arrives; by evening he can tell his aunt when the next rinse will begin. You copy the list into your travel book.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days comparing cords and pack marks with the clerk. Tariq finds the slipped knot and keeps his father’s cloth out of the animal tally. You add Kashgar to your notes and map. He comes to find you again when the next relay hands in its cord.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_2_result: Tariq takes you into his family’s garden for the day. His father explains which water turn keeps the vines alive, and Tariq shows you how they mark the baskets for market. You record the visit; by evening a dyer from the weaving quarter asks whether you heard the same story she did.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_3_result: You inspect the merchant’s sealed jade lot and pay 135 silver. He waits a day to have the transfer entered properly, then loads the goods with yours. Tariq moves the melon crate aside so your pack animal can pass.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.body:
On your return, Habib has spread his cloth map across the bench. The young carrier has come back from the first station and says the repaired trough held water. ‘Did you drink there?’ Habib asks. ‘We filled the skins and let the animals rest,’ the carrier replies. Tariq marks the report on his cord, careful to distinguish what the carrier saw from what another driver told him.

You ask about the western road to Samarkand. Habib traces it with a finger, stopping where several wells are close together. He says caravan leaders sometimes argue over which one to use, but the decision depends on the season and the loads. The carrier admits he would have chosen the nearest without looking at the animals.

Habib takes a spare knotted cord from the bench. Tariq brings a clean cup and moves it away from the map before the tea is poured.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: Habib ties the spare cord to your wrist and has you name the first two stations. The young carrier supplies the third from his new memory. You carry their introduction to the relay with you.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask Habib to trace the Samarkand road
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: Habib traces the westward road toward Samarkand, marking the wells he has checked this season. Tariq copies the names onto your paper. You add Samarkand to your map, and the carrier asks for a copy as well.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day comparing the drivers’ reports
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You spend a day sorting reports by who saw each stop and when. Habib has you ask the carrier again about the repaired trough, and his answer stays the same. Tariq marks the account cleanly; you leave with a clearer way to compare road news.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.title: Habib’s Cloth Map
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_1_result: The clerk takes the old ledger into the shade and lets his assistant read the entries aloud. She asks why the destination changes from year to year; he shows her the pilots’ notes attached to each shipment.
