You learn what the port once sent and hear the name of Zayton from the men who made the northern crossing. The pilot comes over while they are still talking.
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_2_result: For another day you work beside the assistant, calling out each bundle before the porters lift it. The elephant keeper gets his feed, and a pilot tells you which southbound ships stop near Pentam. When the clerk closes the list, he asks the same pilot to speak with you about the sea roads.
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_3_result: A timber seller opens one sandalwood pack so you can see the wood before it is tied shut again. You pay for the full load, and the clerk adds your name beside the porter who will bring it to your ship. The seller stays until you have checked that the pack is dry.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.body: The pilot finds you by the storehouse as the clerk closes the harbour list. He has a chalked board under one arm and a rope still looped around the other. ‘The assistant says you asked where our ships go,’ he says. He sets the board down and marks Zayton to the north and Pentam farther south. A porter interrupts to ask whether the sandalwood now belongs on your load or the next ship’s. The pilot waits while the clerk checks the name. ‘This is why I keep my own list,’ he tells you. ‘At sea I cannot run back to the storehouse for a missing pack.’ His younger deckhand asks whether a ship for Pentam can use the same pilot all the way. ‘Only until the next crew knows the shallows better than I do,’ the pilot answers. He invites you to inspect the sealed sandalwood, mark the northern route, or stay for the next day’s departure preparations.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_1_result: The seller brings out the packed sandalwood and opens a corner for inspection. You pay for it and watch the clerk move your name to the correct load list. The pilot has his deckhand carry the marked pack beneath a dry awning.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_2: Have the pilot mark the sea road to Zayton
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_2_result: The pilot marks Zayton on your chart and talks through the water stops with his deckhand present. The younger man repeats the order back to him, then corrects one cramped mark at the edge of the board. You leave with a usable route and the story behind the port’s old elephant entries.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_3: Spend another day watching the departure
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_3_result: You return for another day as the deckhand checks ropes and counts water jars. He points out the craft bound near Pentam and asks you to test his list against the loads already aboard. When he finds his own missing jar, the pilot lets him call the final count.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.title: The Pilot after the Loading List
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_1_result: You spend two days following the broker between the harbour and the town office. The niece brings each corrected bag number to the clerk, who explains why the office keeps one copy of the load list ashore. By the second day she can check it herself. The broker introduces you to another pilot before you leave.
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_2_result: You pay for a dry load of pepper. The niece opens the top bag at your request, lets you smell the grain, and seals it again in front of you. Her uncle writes your name on the load list. The broker asks you to wait a moment while he finishes the sailing notice.
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_3_result: Two sailors compare their next ports with you on a board laid across the mooring posts. One names Zayton; the other describes the onward connection to Fuju and where to ask for water. The niece listens, then moves the dry bags beneath the roof before the evening rain.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.body: The broker brings a new sailing notice to the pepper merchant’s stall. His niece looks first for the name of the ship that will take their dry bags. ‘It is there,’ he says, ‘but the crew has asked for fresh water before they take another load.’ The merchant sends her to a waterseller with two jars. You help her hold the notice flat while she compares the bag numbers. She finds one that has been copied twice and takes the page back to the broker. He strikes out the extra line in front of the merchant. A sailor arrives from the northbound ship and asks if the pepper is ready. ‘Ready once you carry the water,’ the niece tells him. He laughs and takes one jar. The broker now has a moment to show you Fuju on his route sheet. He asks whether you want to purchase a separate pepper load, take down the route, or spend a day learning how the harbour office checks departing cargo.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_1: Buy a separate load of pepper
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_1_result: The merchant sells you a sealed load of pepper. His niece checks its number against the corrected notice before the sailor carries it away. You pay the agreed cargo price and receive a copy of the entry for your own records.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the broker to mark the route to Fuju
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_2_result: The broker marks Fuju on the route sheet and has the sailor name the harbours where a ship can take on water. The niece holds the notice away from the wet jars while you copy the ports, then gives the sailor his own dry copy.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_3: Spend a day with the harbour office
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_3_result: For another day you help the niece carry corrected numbers between the merchant and the office. A clerk checks each against the bags in the storehouse and learns your name in the process. By evening the niece catches a new copying error before a sailor takes the notice aboard.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.title: The Broker’s Sailing Notice
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_1_result: The boy gets the fresh grass to the yard before the animal has shaken its gate loose. His aunt points you down the street past the rice cook. You follow her directions across town and learn where the quay, market, and inland gate meet.
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_2_result: You stay through the next day’s market. The aunt introduces you to a sailmaker whose mother sells rice by the mosque, and he walks you through the alleys instead of waving from his stall. By evening you can find the waterside stores and the town gate without asking again.
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_3_result: At the mosque, a caretaker is carrying water to the entrance. You help move the jars clear of the steps before greeting the elders inside. One of them introduces you to his nephew, who knows the path back to the quay. He thanks you by name when you leave.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_1_result: You pay Batar 5 silver, and he takes you through the working yard. His daughter shows how the lashing can be loosened, then retied without losing the panel’s shape. He invites you back to see the next frame.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_2_result: You watch the family raise the light reed wall from the meadow. The grandfather tells you who taught Batar the binding, and the daughter comes out to show the blue border she has finished.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day drawing the frame and its knots. Batar checks your sketch, and his daughter adds the part hidden behind the panel. You take away a careful record of their work.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.body:
Batar has begun a second frame, and his daughter has copied his demonstration onto scrap wood. She asks whether the drawing shows the knot from the front or the back. You turn the board around for her; she sees why the first lashing twisted. Her grandfather says he made the same mistake when he was learning. ‘You said you never did,’ she reminds him. ‘I was hoping you had forgotten,’ he says.

You ask where the reeds come from. Batar names households farther along the road toward Cacanfu that cut and dry them, and his daughter adds which bundles bend best. She has kept one loose knot for you to try. The grandfather is going to stay all day to help raise the frame and offers you a place at the workbench. Batar hands his daughter the cord and waits for her to choose the next knot.

The daughter asks her grandfather to hold the board steady; he complains about her fussy lines but does exactly as she asks.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_1_result: You and the daughter retie the loose loop. Her grandfather tests the panel with his hand, and Batar shows you how it can be taken apart for another journey. You keep the method in your notes.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask about the reed-cutters toward Cacanfu
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_2_result: Batar draws the road toward Cacanfu and marks the households that dry reeds beside it. His daughter adds the stream where the bundles are soaked. You can now find the city they were speaking of.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day helping raise the frame
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day lifting and binding the frame. At dusk the daughter sets her blue-edged panel in place. Her grandfather has her check the knot herself before anyone hangs a roof cloth.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.title: The Next Reed Frame
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_1_result: You spend a day walking the outer path. Hulan points out where her mares cross the stream and the falconer shows you the safe place to watch his bird. You record what you saw of the meadow.
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_2_result: You watch the white mares drink. Hulan’s son finally finds the foal tucked beside its mother and stops worrying over his count. You remember the family’s herd at the stream.
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_3_result: You pay the falconer 8 silver. He lets you handle the lure, then asks you to watch how the bird responds before he releases it. He invites you to his bird yard for a longer account.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.body:
At the bird yard, the falconer lets his niece feed a trained hawk while he repairs a perch. She asks why the bird refuses the first piece. He says the meat is too cold and tells her to warm it in her hand. You ask whether he taught her the same way he learned. ‘My uncle shouted more,’ she says before he can answer. He laughs and admits that his own teacher shouted still louder.

A messenger from the road to Cambaluc comes for directions. The falconer asks his niece to describe the first river crossing; she remembers the bridge but forgets the fork beyond it. He corrects her and lets her finish. A younger bird is ready for a short feeding exercise, and she asks whether you would watch. He puts down his tools so both of you can see the bird clearly.

The niece asks whether he is listening to her directions. The messenger repeats the fork correctly, and she smiles.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_1: Ask how the niece learned to feed the hawk
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_1_result: She shows you how she tests the meat and how the bird signals it has had enough. Her uncle listens, then asks her to explain the perch too. You record what they taught you.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the messenger about the road to Cambaluc
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_2_result: The messenger and the niece compare their accounts of the river crossing. You mark Cambaluc on your map; the falconer adds the fork beyond the bridge so you can ask the next household for help.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_3: Spend a day watching the young bird train
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_3_result: You stay the day. The niece calls the bird back after each short flight while her uncle tends the perch. By evening she can read its movements without him prompting her.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.title: At the Bird Yard
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_1_result: You watch Hulan’s family milk the mares. The granddaughter carefully carries the first small bowl to her aunt, then asks the neighbour to repeat her words. You remember the morning they shared.
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_2_result: You give 1 silver toward the gathering. Hulan’s aunt thanks you and asks the granddaughter to bring you a clean cup. You sit with them as the family shares its morning milk.
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_3_result: The aunt tells you how her mother taught her to set the small bowl aside, and the neighbour adds her family’s version. The granddaughter asks more questions than either expected, so they invite you to listen again.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.body:
Hulan’s aunt has dried the small bowl and is showing her granddaughter how to mend a loose rim with a narrow strip of wood. The girl asks why they keep using the old bowl when her mother has made two new ones. ‘Your grandmother shaped this one,’ the aunt says. A neighbour comes by with fresh grass for the mares and adds that her own family keeps an older bowl for a different morning custom. The women compare what each remembers, and neither expects the girl to take notes. She does, on the back of a feed tally.

You ask how the bowl became part of the family gathering. The aunt recalls a winter when her mother shared milk with a stranded household. Hulan’s son arrives, sees the feed tally covered in writing, and asks whether the horses have somehow learned to read. The granddaughter laughs and sets the repaired bowl where he cannot kick it.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_1: Ask the aunt about that winter visitor
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_1_result: The aunt tells you what her mother cooked for the stranded family and how they later returned with hay. Her granddaughter adds the story to the feed tally. You remember the family through the bowl they still use.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_2_result: You join the family as they give thanks for grass, water and the people who returned home. The aunt offers you milk afterward; the granddaughter checks that the repaired rim holds. You carry the morning with you.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_3: Spend a day helping mend the family bowls
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay the day, smoothing two old bowls and cutting a strip for a third. At dusk Hulan’s son brings the mares back; the granddaughter makes him wash his hands before he touches her work.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.title: The Small Wooden Bowl
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.body:
After your goods are checked, the groom at Orina’s yard asks you to look at a mare whose pack keeps sliding left. ‘My brother tied it,’ he says, ‘and now he insists the mare walks crooked.’ The brother comes over carrying a strap and hears him. ‘She does walk crooked when you put all the pots on one side,’ he replies. You help them unload two pots, and the mare stands comfortably.

The groom asks how far you intend to travel. You tell him, and he names a horse keeper across the meadow who knows which animals can take a long road. His brother asks whether that keeper will remember a traveller sent over without a note. The groom tears a corner from the clean tally sheet, writes his own name, and asks the brother to witness it. ‘There,’ he says, ‘now he’ll know why you came.’ He lets you decide whether to take the introduction.

The brother keeps rubbing the same strap between his fingers, testing whether it will slip again.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You take the note and ask both brothers where the keeper works. The younger one points to a low paddock beside the stream. The groom says you may mention the mare and the lopsided pots when you arrive; the keeper knows the family.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the brothers and leave the note
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank them for the offer and leave the note on the tally board. The brothers return to loading the mare, this time dividing the pots between both sides.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.title: A Groom’s Introduction
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a_resolution.bo:
The horse keeper reads the groom’s note, then looks up when you mention the lopsided pots. ‘That brother will put a whole kitchen on one flank if you let him,’ she laughs. A mare beside her has a rubbed patch under the saddle, and she is waiting for a new pad before letting anyone ride her.

You ask whether she keeps another animal for a longer journey. She shows you a quieter horse and explains what it eats during a march. A young helper interrupts to say the saddle pad is ready. The keeper asks him to bring it over and lets you watch how she checks the fit. When the helper pulls too hard, she loosens the strap and makes him try again. She gives you a choice: carry the groom’s introduction onward to a rider who needs it, or stay a day to help finish fitting the horses.

The helper asks which saddle you would choose, and the keeper waits until you have looked at both.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a_resolution.ch: Carry the introduction to the waiting rider
You pass the note to the waiting rider and explain who sent you. The keeper nods as he reads it; the helper takes him to the quiet horse. Your name is remembered among the people at the paddock.
Stay a day and help fit the saddles
You stay for the day and help check each saddle pad. By evening the rubbed mare can take a short walk without flinching. The keeper thanks you and keeps the groom’s paper with her other notes.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.body:
The falconer who asked Orina about the meadow families is putting fresh padding on a bird’s perch. His niece holds the roll of cloth, but a gust sends it across the grass. The bird shifts, and the falconer asks everyone to stand still until it settles. His niece retrieves the cloth and apologizes. ‘The wind has tried to take that roll three times,’ he says, and she answers that he might finally tie it down.

You ask where a traveller can watch birds without troubling the herd. He draws the edge of the meadow in dust with a stick, marking the stream and the low rise where the bird returns. His niece adds the place where Hulan takes the foal to water. She says the drawing would help a visiting rider who keeps asking the wrong family for directions. The falconer offers to send the drawing along with you, or to keep it here for the next visitor.

His niece rubs the edge of the drawing flat, pleased that the stream and slope now fit on one sheet.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_1: Take the drawing to the visiting rider
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You copy the falconer’s drawing, including his niece’s mark for the foal’s watering place. She runs after you to add one last bend in the path. The rider is still waiting at the far yard.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the drawing with the family
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You leave the drawing with the family. The niece puts a stone on each corner so the wind cannot lift it; the falconer finally ties down the loose cloth roll.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.title: The Falconer’s Ground
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b_resolution.bo:
The rider at the far yard has been sent to collect a bird perch, but the path he was given takes him straight through Hulan’s herd. He studies your drawing and asks which mark is the low rise. You point it out; the falconer’s niece has drawn a tiny horse beside the watering place, and he laughs when he recognizes why.

His own horse is thirsty. You walk with him to the stream and show the outer path that keeps the mares undisturbed. Hulan’s son is there counting the foals again. He tells the rider to wait until the smallest one has crossed, then waves him through. The rider says another person is expected later with a second perch. He asks whether you can pass on the directions, or whether you would rather stay and make a clearer copy with him.

The boy turns back to the herd, calling the foals one by one so his count will be right this time.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Tell the next rider how to cross the meadow

You meet the next rider and explain the stream crossing and Hulan’s herd. He follows the outer path and reaches the bird yard without scattering the foals. The first rider thanks you as he carries off the perch.
Stay a day to make a clearer route drawing
You spend a day walking the turns with the rider and drawing them again. Hulan’s son checks the crossing mark. The finished sheet stays at the yard for travellers who come after you.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b_resolution.ti: The Rider at the Far Yard
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days matching your loads to the clerk’s marks. Orina shows you the yard where travellers can rest their animals, and a groom offers to help you check your pack straps afterward.
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day among the meadow families. Orina’s sister tells the story of their father’s lost sandals, and several neighbours add where the old camp paths ran. You record their accounts; a falconer later asks what you heard.
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_3_result: You spend the day checking the bale and pay 146 silver. Orina’s sister records its weight and helps you tie it for the road. You leave the cloth yard with the trade added to your book.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.body:
When you return, the horse keeper has set out two saddles and a strip of leather she uses to record hoof measurements. Her helper has drawn a map of the road south toward Chinangli. He asks you to check the water stop he marked; he has never taken that road himself. The keeper says her cousin did and reads a line from his letter aloud. They move the mark nearer the stream.

You ask why the quiet mare is standing apart. The keeper says she has recovered from the rubbed saddle but needs one last walk before carrying a traveller. The helper brings her out and lets you watch the first few steps. He wants to keep the corrected map for the next visitor. The keeper offers you a copy of her notes, a closer account of the southern road, or a whole day helping the helper check the horses.

The keeper asks the helper to hold the mare still while she checks the strap. This time he remembers to loosen it first.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: You copy her notes on hoof wear, saddle fit and rest. The helper reads them back and catches a word you missed. She thanks you for taking the work seriously.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask about the road south to Chinangli
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: The keeper and her helper use the cousin’s letter to correct the route toward Chinangli. You mark the city and its water stops on your map. The helper keeps his first drawing so he can see what he learned.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_3: Spend a day checking the yard horses
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You spend the day checking saddles and watching each horse walk. The quiet mare completes her circuit without favouring her back. The keeper tells her helper he may now prepare her for a traveller.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.title: One More Morning at the Horse Yard
ev.ev_charchan_entry.choice_1_result: The boy waves a clean stone as you leave. His aunt reminds you to ask before filling your water skin at the next well. You mark Charchan on your map.
ev.ev_charchan_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day, watch the aunt sort the stones, and learn which nearby wells carry sweet water. The boy eventually finds one uncracked piece; you write down what they taught you and mark Charchan on your map.
ev.ev_charchan_site_gap.choice_1_result: Aysa names the road to Pein and the wells she trusts along it. You mark both the route and Pein on your map while her brother fills the waiting woman’s jar.
ev.ev_charchan_site_gap.choice_2_result: You try the knot while Aysa holds the bucket. Her brother checks it against the rim; it passes without catching. You record what you learned about the well and its ropes.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_1_result: You walk the quay and count the upstream boats. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Cambaluc on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_2_result: You buy a bolt of river-traded silk. You pay 10000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The road to Cacanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_3_result: You ask which spices the downstream boats carry. You set what you saw into your travel book. A small turn of fortune favours you. You set the way to Chandu on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.body: On the quay of the great river a broker who prices silk and spice for boats bound to Cambaluc opens his ledger beside the water. He says the river is a road that remembers every toll — and that a traveller who buys silk without hearing the days to Cacanfu and Chandu rides half-blind upstream.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_1: Buy a bolt of silk at the river ledger price
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_1_resu: He sells you silk at a price the upstream markets will recognize. The bolt is sealed for the boat.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_2: Ask him to name the water road toward Cambaluc
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_2_resu: Cambaluc and Cacanfu are marked on your map. The river road north is clear.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day counting spice chests with the clerks
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_3_resu: You spend a day among the chests. Chandu is named in the talk, and a small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.title: Chinangli: The River Brokers' Ledger
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_1_result: You watch the paper-money exchange at a stall. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The clerk gives you one sample paper note as a record of what you saw.
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_2_result: You buy a small porcelain bowl with paper-money. You pay 4000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_3_result: You ask the exchange clerks how the notes are renewed. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_chinangli_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. You set the way to Chinangli on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Chinangli opens on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the sì (Buddhist monastery). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Chinangli on your map.
ev.ev_chinghianfu_entry.choice_1_result: The binder’s daughter points out the street to the landing before taking the boatman through the market. The reader carries the rest of his books back to the meeting house. You follow the same turn across town and know where to find the waterside path.
ev.ev_chinghianfu_entry.choice_2_result: You stay another day. The page dries flat, and the binder shows his daughter how to stitch it in without pulling the edge. The reader returns, checks that the children can turn it safely, and introduces you to the families who use the book.
ev.ev_chinginju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Chinginju on your map.
ev.ev_chinginju_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Chinginju opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_cobinan_entry.choice_1_result: The apprentice points out the street beyond the smiths. You mark Cobinan on your map and continue.
ev.ev_cobinan_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the workshops, writing down what the metalworkers tell you. Before leaving, you mark Cobinan on your map.
ev.ev_coigangiu_entry.choice_1_result: You ride on without delay. The road to Coigangiu opens on your map.
ev.ev_coigangiu_entry.choice_2_result: You rest half a day by the road. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set the way to Coigangiu on your map.
ev.ev_coiganju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Coiganju opens on your map.
ev.ev_coiganju_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Coiganju on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_coilum_entry.choice_1_result: The porter sets his cup down and walks you to the lane that carries travellers through Coilum. He calls back to the cook to leave the basket where its owner can see it. You continue with the harbour's turns in mind.
ev.ev_coilum_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day near the warehouses. The basket's owner arrives, recognizes her knot and asks the cook to write the new label in front of her. Later the porter shows you the separate sheds where pepper and galangal are kept. You leave knowing the people and the paths behind the harbour bustle.
ev.ev_coilum_site_gap.choice_1_result: The weigher walks to the door and shows you the road that follows the coast toward Maabar. “The boats use the landing behind us; you want the carts' road,” she says. Her son points out the first turn as you leave, proud that he has learned it too.
ev.ev_coilum_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the scale steady while she sets the dry sack on it. Her son writes down the weight and leaves the damp sack on boards for later. She shows you the empty sack's weight, then lets him make the next calculation without her hand over his shoulder.
ev.ev_constantinopolis_entry.choice_1_re: Anna calls out the turn toward the market before hurrying after her brother. You mark Constantinople on your map and continue.
ev.ev_constantinopolis_entry.choice_2_re: You spend the day along the harbour and the lodging streets. Anna introduces you to a cloth merchant who crosses into Anatolia and takes the overland road toward Smyrna. You mark Constantinople, Smyrna, and that road on your map.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_1_result: You pay 135 silver for the sealed trading lot. Amina wraps its corners again and Yusuf signs the ownership mark before the merchant steps aside. The jade cargo goes with you; the cracked pebble stays on the tray as a lesson for his daughter.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_2_result: You spend the day walking the safe shallows with Yusuf and Amina. They show you how a change in current alters the gravel bed; Amina finds the cracked pebble’s matching mark on another stone. You record the river work in your travel book before your feet finally warm.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_3_result: The older washer sits beside you and turns each sample toward the light. He does not offer a price until Yusuf has signed off the lot; instead he tells you what he looks for at this river bend. A little later he asks you to come back and help him check a different tray.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.body:
The older washer calls you back to the river when Amina brings a second tray of stones. She has marked where each came from with a little strip of reed. Her father Yusuf says the reeds will dry and curl, so she should copy the places before the marks fall off. ‘I can remember them,’ she says. Then she pauses over one pale stone and admits she is no longer sure which bend it came from. The older washer gives her a clean board to write on.

You ask what happens after they sort the river haul. Yusuf says a merchant checks the stone and buys a sealed trading lot if the quality agrees with his order. Another river worker carries goods west toward Yarcan and can tell you where the loads change hands. Amina asks him whether his cart has room for a note to her aunt; he says there is, if she writes the address clearly.

The older washer sits with you while Amina copies her reed marks. He is willing to spend a day showing you the shallows after the next water change, and the carrier waits to explain his westward road.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the other sealed jade lot for 135 silver
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_1_result: The merchant opens a second sealed lot while Amina reads the reed marks on its tag. You inspect the jade and pay 135 silver for the whole trading pack. Yusuf signs the transfer, and the carrier helps you stow it before he takes Amina’s letter west.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the carrier about the road to Yarcan
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_2_result: The carrier names the stops where the river goods change hands on the way to Yarcan. Amina adds her aunt’s address to his letter bundle and checks it with Yusuf. You mark Yarcan on your map before the cart leaves.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day learning how the washers mark the shallows
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day with the older washer and Amina, comparing her reed marks with the changing riverbank. She corrects the one pale stone’s place on her board. Yusuf thanks you for staying, and the family remembers you at the water’s edge.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.title: Amina’s Second Tray
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_1_result: You pay 100 silver for the completed silk bolt. The aunt checks the roll and ties on a label with your name. Farah keeps working on the unfinished edge while Zuleika helps load the purchased cloth with your goods.
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_2_result: You spend a day beside the sisters. Farah shows you the edge pattern; Zuleika has you count the shuttle’s passes aloud until you can see where the blue belongs. Their aunt says she will show you the dye yard if you return.
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_3_result: You pay 1.2 silver for the small labelled samples. The aunt wraps the indigo separately and makes you read the names back before she hands them over. Farah laughs that she wishes her own bobbins were labelled as carefully.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.body:
Farah and Zuleika’s aunt invites you back when the first blue edge has come off the loom. She has placed four dyed scraps on a shelf. Zuleika says the safflower red looks faint beside the indigo. Her aunt asks her to move it away from the window and look again. ‘Better?’ she asks. Zuleika admits the sun was passing through the thin cloth and changing what she saw. Farah, still at the loom, calls that she will wait for the new comparison before choosing the next thread.

You ask how dyes reach the workshop. A trader from Kashgar has delivered walnut hulls and will return north after collecting his payment. He tells Farah that her last cloth survived the journey well, though the outer wrapping came loose. Her aunt says she will use a wider knot this time. She has a small labelled dye sample for you if you want to try the colours on your own cloth.

Zuleika asks you to hold the four scraps together while she writes the trader’s name on the wrapping. Farah is ready to teach the rhythm of this edge if you can stay another day.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_1_result: The aunt gives you the small dye packet, with indigo wrapped apart from the others. Zuleika reads each label aloud before it goes into your bag. Farah asks her to write the same clear names on the workshop shelf.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_2_result: The trader describes the road north to Kashgar and where his last bundle was rewrapped. Farah writes down the place so she can secure the next shipment. You mark Kashgar on your map while Zuleika finishes the new tag.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and practise the loom rhythm
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day at the loom. Farah counts the edge pattern slowly and has you repeat it while Zuleika works the shuttle. The aunt checks the finished blue against her scraps; you leave with the sisters’ method in your notes.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.title: Auntie’s Colour Shelf
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_1_result: You spend three days helping Rahman set supports beside the old brick. His mother keeps the children from stepping on the fresh channel edge. When water finally runs safely past, you record the family’s field and the exposed wall in your travel book.
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_2_result: Rahman’s mother gives you a small painted fragment from her own basket after the children have made a drawing of it. She says its curve may be a hand, or part of a leaf. You wrap it carefully and leave the sound bricks in the wall.
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_3_result: Rahman’s mother tells you how the old wall has appeared and disappeared under sand during her life. Her youngest child brings a second piece for her to compare. You write down what she knows, and she offers to walk with you along the higher terrace another day.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.body:
Rahman’s mother takes you along the upper terrace she mentioned. A wall end appears through the sand beside the path. Her grandson runs ahead with a painted shard and says he found it after yesterday’s wind. She asks him to set it on her palm before he trips over the irrigation ridge. The child asks whether its painted curve matches the one at home. ‘Close enough that we should draw both,’ she says.

You ask where the old path led. She remembers her father describing travellers toward Charchan, though the field walls have shifted since his time. Rahman has brought a spade to clear sand from a blocked channel and says he can show which terrace still carries water. He does not want anyone digging at the exposed wall while the ground beneath it is wet. His mother agrees and moves the children back to a dry place.

She has a loose painted fragment from her own basket to give you after the family records it. Rahman offers to explain the eastern road, or you can stay a day to hear how the terrace changed in his mother’s lifetime.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_1: Accept the family’s recorded painted fragment
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_1_result: The children draw the painted curve before Rahman’s mother gives you the loose fragment. She puts their drawing beside the first one at home. You wrap the piece carefully and leave the sound wall stones in place.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_2: Ask Rahman about the road to Charchan
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_2_result: Rahman tells you where his family has heard travellers bound for Charchan turn east. His mother adds which old field path has disappeared under new channels. You mark Charchan on your map, then help the child step safely over the ridge.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_3: Stay a day with the family on the upper terrace
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay a day while Rahman clears the channel and his mother tells you how the terrace has changed. The children compare both drawings beside her. When water finally runs through, you record the family’s account in your travel book.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.title: Rahman’s Upper Terrace
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.body:
The river washer from the entry yard calls you back after two days at Samira’s register. He is Yusuf’s cousin Harun, and he has found that two loads carried the same chalk mark after the rain. ‘One was ours to carry,’ he says. ‘The other belongs to a family across the channel. If a chest goes missing, I do not want them looking in the wrong house.’

You ask whether the family can tell the loads apart. Harun brings out a narrow strip of cloth tied to one handle. Samira’s brother says he saw that strip when the cart first arrived. The other family’s daughter comes over with their own receipt and points to a small tear in the paper. Harun remembers that the cart wheel brushed it against the wall. Their stories fit, but Samira asks them to keep both receipts until the next station has the correct names.

Harun offers to write an introduction to the river carriers who will receive the goods ahead. The daughter asks whether you can help spell her mother’s name on the outside.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_1: Take Harun’s note after checking the names
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_1_resul: You check the cloth strip against both receipts and ask Harun who will take the note at the next river yard. He names two carriers; the daughter writes her mother’s name beside theirs. Samira says she will bring the final copy before you leave.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_2_resul: You leave the correction with Samira. Harun and the daughter wait while she copies the two marks into separate lines. Once the ink dries, each family takes back its own receipt, and you continue on your way.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.title: The Washer’s Carrying Mark
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a_resolution.bod:
Samira brings the finished note to the water yard. Harun has signed beneath his carrying mark, and the daughter has added her mother’s full name. ‘I nearly wrote the short name everyone calls her,’ the girl says. Samira answers, ‘The next station may know a different woman by that name.’ Her brother reads the outside aloud and catches one letter hidden by the fold. Harun unfolds it and writes the letter again.

You ask whether the next carriers will have a way to check the boxes themselves. Harun has put the cloth strip back on the correct handle and copied the tear in the other family’s receipt. The daughter agrees that anyone can now match both loads without guessing. Her mother arrives to see the names and thanks the group for stopping the mistake early.

Samira offers you the note to carry ahead. If you want a day to copy the marks into your own book first, her brother has set out a dry table.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a_resolution.cho: You take the corrected note. Harun shows you where the cloth strip is tied; the daughter points to the receipt’s tear once more. You can now hand both names to the next carriers without confusing their loads.
Spend a day copying both cargo marks

You spend the day copying the two receipts and the names on the note. Samira’s brother checks your letters against the originals, and Harun returns the cloth strip to its proper handle. Your book now holds the corrected record.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.body:
After your visit to Samira’s family, a weaver named Farah asks whether you saw the channel by their house. Her aunt has heard that a shallow patch may leave grit in the water used for rinsing silk. ‘The river washer says it looked clear yesterday,’ Farah says, ‘but our new white cloth has a faint line.’ She holds up the edge so you can see it. Her sister Zuleika thinks the line may be from the old dye tub instead.

You ask whether they can test the water before washing another length. Farah fills one jar at the channel and another at the yard well. Zuleika puts a plain thread in each. Samira comes to check the jar labels; she once confused two cargo marks and does not want this family to mix their samples. The sisters wait while the threads dry. Their aunt asks them to write the time beside each jar, so they can check the water again tomorrow.

Farah asks if you want a copy of their test. Zuleika suggests writing down the time and which jar came from where, so the next weaver can compare it later.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_1: Take a checked copy of the sisters’ water test
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_1_resul: You ask the sisters to label both jars before copying the test. Farah writes the channel time, Zuleika writes the well time, and Samira checks the names. Their aunt says she will send you the final result when the threads are dry.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the test with Farah’s workshop
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_2_resul: You leave the notes with Farah. Her aunt hangs the two threads beside their labelled jars, where the sisters can check them in tomorrow’s light. Samira goes back to her register, satisfied that no one will mistake the water sources.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.title: A Weaver Asks About the Channel
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b_resolution.bod:
Farah’s aunt brings you the two dried threads. The line appears on the one rinsed in the old dye tub. The thread washed in channel water has dried clean. Zuleika grins because her guess was right; Farah asks her to help clean the tub before she celebrates. Samira reads the jar labels aloud, and the sisters mark the result in their workshop book.

You ask whether they will throw away the lined silk. The aunt says the length is sound and can be used for a hidden lining; she has another clean bolt for the customer. Farah says she will tell the buyer what happened rather than quietly swap the order. Zuleika carries the old tub outside to scrub it.

The aunt offers a copy of the test for your notes. Zuleika sets a clean thread beside the old one and asks Farah whether they should test the washed tub again before the customer arrives.

Farah holds the second length against the light and asks Zuleika to bring the clean jar, not the old one. Their aunt nods; the lesson has already changed how the sisters work.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b_resolution.cho: Carry the sisters’ test to other makers

You take the labelled copy. Farah writes the workshop’s name at the bottom so anyone with a question can find her. Zuleika holds up the clean thread while you fold the paper; their tested method goes with you.
Spend a day checking a second length of silk

You spend the day with the sisters as they rinse and dry another length. The cleaned tub leaves no line this time. Zuleika records the result, and Farah shows the customer both pieces before the order is settled.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days checking pack names with Samira. Her brother learns to keep the washer’s carrying mark separate from the merchant’s ownership mark. You record Khotan on your map and in your travel book. The river washer later comes to ask you about another mark.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_2_result: Samira’s brother takes you to his mother’s shelf of river stones. She remembers who brought each piece and lets you compare the smooth sides with the rough ones. You spend the day hearing the family’s account, note Khotan, and later receive a question from a weaver who knows the same channel.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_3_result: You inspect the sealed lot, pay 135 silver, and spend the day arranging carriage for it. Samira enters the merchant’s name and yours on separate lines before the package joins your cargo. The washer keeps his carrying mark in the register as well.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.body:
You return to Mahmud’s well before the first caravan arrives. His daughter has lowered a small weight on a cord to check the water level. It touches the surface sooner than yesterday. ‘Is that rain upstream?’ she asks. Mahmud says it might be, but he wants another morning’s reading before he tells people to expect more. The river washer arrives and says a channel higher up was cleared late yesterday; that may have changed the flow.

You ask whether they record both reports. Mahmud’s daughter writes the measured level first, then the washer’s observation beneath it. Her father says the two lines can be compared after the next rain. The washer sets down a smooth river pebble, which she uses to hold the page flat in the breeze.

Mahmud offers you his extra marked stone, or a careful account of the road east toward Pein. If you stay through the day, his daughter will show you how the well changes between morning and evening.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_1_res: Mahmud gives you the spare marked pebble after his daughter copies its sign into her book. It is a reminder of the well where the family measured before making a promise about tomorrow’s water.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask Mahmud about the road to Pein
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_2_res: Mahmud explains the road toward Pein and where travellers can refill before leaving the river valley. His daughter adds the names to the edge of the well record. You mark Pein on your map while the washer checks his empty jar.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and compare the water levels
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_3_res: You stay through the day and take the evening reading with Mahmud’s daughter. The level has changed only a little; she writes the number beside the morning mark. Her father thanks you for checking it together before the next caravan asks.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.title: The Morning Well Mark
ev.ev_ctesiphon_entry.choice_1_result: The girl points out the path around the fallen wall. You mark Ctesiphon on your map and continue.
ev.ev_ctesiphon_entry.choice_2_result: Her father gives you room beneath the cloth. After a day’s rest you feel stronger, and the girl helps you mark Ctesiphon beside the river on your map.
ev.ev_damascus_entry.choice_1_result: You ask Nura the way out of the city. She points to the gate beyond the market and tells her nephew to take the bottle first. “Walk, please. You've got glass in your hands.” You pass through with the other travellers and mark Damascus on your map.
ev.ev_damascus_entry.choice_2_result:
You help Nura wrap the bottle again, then accompany her nephew to his home. His mother opens the door in her cooking apron, smells the rosewater, and laughs that Nura has been sparing with it once more.

You stay in Damascus another day. That evening his mother tells you where the caravan for Tripoli meets and draws the road it takes out of town. You add it to your map.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You stay until evening, matching the wooden tallies against the register. Rahim had received one measure; Shirin adds the missing one to his sack when he comes by. Safiya carries the now-dry page inside. The families in the courtyard thank you for staying with the work.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_2_result: The trader waits while his animals are fed, then spends the day showing you the westward road toward Cambay. He names the watering places and draws a bend around a stretch that floods in heavy rain. You add the Delhi–Cambay route to your map; before leaving, you help Safiya keep the wet register away from the sacks.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_3_result: After the clerk confirms the tallies, you help Shirin call each family forward and explain the corrected measures. One neighbour grumbles until Safiya shows her his old mark on the wood. By the end of the day everyone has collected their grain, and Shirin asks you to come by if you need a place to sit in the shade.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_1_result: You stay through the next day, helping Hina give each family a dry place to sleep. Her nephew finishes sorting the letters while you carry bedding upstairs. When the last guest has a room, Hina thanks you in front of the neighbours and keeps a seat for you at supper.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_2_result: The westward driver spends the day checking addresses with you and naming the stages toward Cambay. He points out the stop near his sister’s home, then draws the road onward. You add the Delhi–Cambay route to your map before he takes the bundle.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_3_result: You spend the day sorting the eastern letters by their next carrier and copying the long road list toward Khotan. Hina pays you 0.8 silver for the work. Her nephew reads the addressees aloud once more before the bundles leave; you mark the Delhi–Khotan route on your map.
ev.ev_delli_entry.choice_1_result: The sister returns with both jars at their proper doors. You mark Delhi on your map and continue while the water carrier fills the caravan’s last skin.
ev.ev_delli_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with the scribe, checking his list of intermediate stops before the distant road reaches Khotan. The water carrier’s sister reads the place names aloud while the drivers pack. You mark Delhi, Khotan, and the long route between them on your map.
ev.ev_dongola_entry.choice_1_result: The reader points out the road beyond the ferry and tells you where the next water stop lies. The boy follows you a few steps before his mother calls him back to the strap. You fill your skin, fix the turn in mind and continue.
ev.ev_dongola_entry.choice_2_result: You stay for a day. The reader shows the boy the painted wall after the roof has been mended, and the water carrier's family shares supper with you. A full night's rest restores your strength; when you leave, you know the station and its ferry road well.
ev.ev_dongola_site_gap.choice_1_result: From the far bank, the daughter points out the northbound Nile road. She makes you repeat the turn where the ferry path ends and names the next place to find water. ‘When you reach Cairo, ask again before crossing Sinai,’ she says. Her father checks the river mark once more before returning to the boat.
ev.ev_dongola_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the new coil while the boatman draws each length through his hands. At the frayed part he shows you how the fibres have rubbed against the hull. His daughter reties the sound end under his eye, and he lets her test the finished knot.
ev.ev_dufar_entry.choice_1_result: The trader points you through the lane between the storehouses. The daughter is still checking the last pale pieces when you pass. Her father raises a hand in farewell, and you leave knowing the way through Dufar.
ev.ev_dufar_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day in the incense market. The daughter shows you why some pieces are kept for later sorting, while the trader explains which cargo goes by boat and which by road. The collector finishes his count before evening, and you leave with the town's trades and streets in mind.
ev.ev_dufar_site_gap.choice_1_result: The nephew leads you to the corner used by carriers travelling toward Esher. He points out the first turning and says which shop they use to ask about water farther on. You follow his directions on the ground before he returns to the jars.
ev.ev_dufar_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the jar while the boy fits clean paper inside. His uncle tests the lid and shows you how he separates good resin from bits still carrying bark. The boy tries the next jar himself, pleased that this one smells only of clay.
ev.ev_edessa_entry.choice_1_result: You fill your bag, thank Miran, and move on. Derya calls after you that a stone is still waiting for the place you visit next. You mark Edessa and the water stop on your map.
ev.ev_edessa_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Miran's family. Derya takes you along the water street and introduces you to everyone who knows the story of her uncle's return. In the evening the family shares a meal and gives you a place to sleep. You leave the next morning with renewed strength, and mark Edessa and its water stop on your map.
ev.ev_egrigaia_entry.choice_1_result: Saran’s brother points out the road from the weaving yard. His mother checks the washed edge as you leave. You mark Egrigaia on your map and continue.
ev.ev_egrigaia_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day as Saran washes and dries the corner, then shows it to the trader. He accepts the cloth after checking the weave. Her brother takes you to a place to rest, and you record what you learned in Egrigaia.
ev.ev_egrigaia_site_gap.choice_1_result: The herder names the camps toward Tenduc and points out the valley the animals use. Orin’s daughter helps you mark the road before returning to the cooking fire.
ev.ev_egrigaia_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the cord while Orin’s wife finishes the patch. His daughter checks the smoke from inside, and the family can put the cooking pots back. You remember how they set the opening to the wind.
ev.ev_ephesus_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Leyla and continue past the old stones. Nisa holds up the marble to show you the carved edge she found. You mark Ephesus and the path up the hill on your map.
ev.ev_ephesus_entry.choice_2_result: You stay with Leyla's family for the day. Nisa's grandfather washes the marble and shows her the tool marks along one edge. After supper he tells you both about the older streets below the hill, and Leyla gives you a place to sleep. You leave the next morning stronger and mark Ephesus on your map.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_1_result: You spend a day beside the customs clerk. He marks the horse after the plank is secured and shows you which incoming cargo will be taken toward Aden. The groom's daughter makes a second careful walk across the boards. When the loading is done, the clerk asks you to look at his next harbour list with him.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_2_result: A pilot names the boats that call at Dufar and shows you how he waits for a safe tide at the harbour mouth. The groom's daughter listens and asks which vessel will take their horse. You leave with the coastal departure clearer in mind; the clerk invites you back to hear about the next ships.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_3_result: You pay the groom for a horse after he leads it on level ground for you. His daughter checks the lead rope, and the clerk confirms the tag. The groom tells you how this town prepares horses for sea voyages and asks you to give the animal a drink before you leave.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.body: The harbour clerk waves you over when the next vessel comes in. His list shows cargo due from the coast, but the porter beside him has put a sack of frankincense under the wrong merchant's mark. “Read the tag again,” the clerk tells him. The porter turns it toward the light and moves the sack to the right place. A trader waiting nearby says he has another full sack for sale if you want one. You ask the clerk which ship will sail next. “One is bound toward Aden,” he says, “and a pilot has just come from Dufar.” The pilot joins them and spreads his route sheet over a crate. A woman carrying letters asks about the crossing to Axuma, so he marks that departure too. The clerk gives the porter his corrected list and asks him to read it aloud before the cargo leaves the shed.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the trader’s sack of frankincense
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay the trader for a full sack of frankincense. The porter checks its tag against the corrected list and lets you inspect the dry wrapping. The clerk tells you when that cargo arrived and hands over the sack after the count is complete.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_2: Ask about the Aden and Dufar passages
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_2_result: The pilot points out the coastal passage toward Aden and the call at Dufar. The clerk adds which ship is currently loading for each. You compare their marks on the sheet before deciding where to ask for a place.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day at the harbour with the pilot
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day helping the pilot match cargo marks to outgoing boats. When the woman with letters returns, he points out the passage toward Axuma and asks her to repeat the departure point. You follow it on the sheet too, more confident about the next crossing.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.title: Esher: Another Harbour List
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_1_result: You pay for a full trade sack of frankincense. The seller's sister checks its mark against the ledger and has him retie the label before handing it over. She tells you how they keep the resin dry, and you leave with the sack properly packed.
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_2_result: You buy a small serving of dates from the niece's tray and eat it in the shade. Her uncle finishes weighing the last sack while you rest. She offers you water before you leave; the food restores some of your strength for the road.
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_3_result: The seller's sister opens her route sheet and points along the coast toward Aden, then across the water toward Axuma. She asks the niece to repeat the names, and the girl adds the carrier who currently takes letters on each passage. You leave with both destinations in mind.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_1_result: The date seller's brother returns the water jar and shows you the street beyond the incense sheds. His sister is still waiting for the clerk to call her ship. You leave with the turns through Esher clear in mind.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at the harbour stalls. The clerk finally reads out the ship's name, and the date seller opens her uncle's letter beside you. She tells you which families carry food to the boats and which people keep the incense sheds. By evening you know the town's streets and its trade.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_3_result: You leave your shoes at the mosque and wait while the attendant shows a visiting family where to sit. Afterwards he points out the lane to the harbour. The date seller sees you returning and thanks you for making room for the family.
ev.ev_etzina_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Etzina on your map.
ev.ev_etzina_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Etzina opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_fuju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Fuju opens on your map.
ev.ev_fuju_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Fuju on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.body: At the canal quay, a weigher is trying to settle the weight of a bean sack. The seller has brought an old heavy sack; the buyer has only counted the beans. ‘I used this cloth because the thin bags split,’ the seller says. The weigher asks them to empty one sack and weigh the cloth separately. The seller’s son says that will spill the beans onto the boards. You offer a clean tray, and the buyer helps hold its edge. They tip the beans out carefully. The empty cloth is heavier than anyone expected. The weigher writes its weight on a separate line and asks the son to read the figure back. The boy has been watching boats on the canal and asks where the one bound toward Linju turns. The buyer comes by road from Linju. ‘The cart track turns past the last farm,’ he says, drawing the bend in the dust while the weigher puts the beans back. The son repeats both the weight and the turn, then asks his father to keep the two figures on the next sales note.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.choice.route: Ask the buyer about the Linju route
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.choice.route_result: The buyer marks the way toward Linju on your board, including the bend he had drawn for the boy. The weigher checks that the bean sack is closed again before the buyer loads it onto his cart. You carry away a clear route while they finish the sale.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.choice.scene_result: You hold the tray while the seller and buyer lift the empty cloth onto the scale. The weigher writes down the sack’s weight, and the son reads it aloud without losing his place. They agree on the bean weight and load the sack onto the buyer’s cart together.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.title: The Bean Sack on the Scale
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.body: At the ferry landing, a ferryman has taken down two weathered boards. One records the river level; the other marks the wind that makes the crossing rough. His nephew wants to paint them both at once, but the old writing is almost gone. ‘Ask the people who use them what they need to see first,’ the ferryman tells him. A woman carrying a basket says she watches the water mark before bringing her mule to the bank. A boat worker says the wind board matters when his craft is empty and catches the gusts. The boy asks you to hold a board upright so he can see how high it will hang. You notice that the lower hook is still within reach of floodwater. He moves the hook up a handspan and asks his uncle whether people can still read it. The ferryman checks from the path used by travellers and nods. He knows the road toward Sindafu and can draw its turn for you after the boards are hung.
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.route: Ask about the road toward Sindafu
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.route_result: The ferryman draws the turn toward Sindafu on your route board, then asks his nephew to read it back while he holds the water marker. The boy has not lost the new hook position. You leave with directions and a clear view of both signs.
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.scene: Help them set the boards above floodwater
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.scene_result: You hold each board while the nephew fixes its higher hook. The woman with the mule checks it from the path, and the boat worker confirms he can read the wind mark from the water. The ferryman thanks you when the two boards are secure.
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.title: Two Boards at the Ferry
ev.ev_gap_caiju.body: A vegetable seller by the bridge has put tender leaves and hard roots into separate baskets. Her younger brother has tied the leaf basket too tightly, and the greens at the bottom are already bending. ‘They will wilt before the buyer sees them,’ she says. He loosens the cord, but now the basket tips when he lifts it. You help him set the bundle upright while she moves the heavy roots to the other side of the carrying pole. A traveller asks if there are vegetables that will last on his cart journey toward Chinghianfu. The seller offers him the dry roots first; the leaves will go to a family cooking nearby. The boy asks why they cannot send everything on the cart. ‘Because their supper is today,’ she says, pointing to the family’s fire. The traveller knows the road onward. ‘After the bridge, where does the cart turn?’ you ask. ‘Past the grain store,’ he says, waiting while the boy reties the lighter basket. The seller asks you to listen to his directions, or help her finish sorting the produce before he goes.
ev.ev_gap_caiju.choice.route_result: The traveller marks the route to Chinghianfu on your board, including the grain store where the cart road turns. The seller hands him a small packet of roots for the trip. Her brother can now carry both baskets without crushing the leaves.
ev.ev_gap_caiju.choice.scene_result: You help the seller shift the heavy roots and tie the leaf basket loosely. Her brother walks a short stretch of the bridge and turns back without spilling anything. The family cooking nearby takes the greens while they are still fresh.
ev.ev_gap_caiju.title: The Vegetable Seller’s Two Baskets
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.body: A water carrier has set two buckets halfway up the stone steps from the landing. The lowest steps are slick with green growth, and his niece has brought sand to scatter there. ‘If I cover the whole stair, people will carry it into the well,’ she says. He asks her to use only enough for a firm foothold. You offer to take one bucket while he tests the bottom step. A woman waiting above says she knows a cleaner well near the western gate, but its keeper asks that visitors rinse their buckets first. ‘Where do we rinse the buckets?’ the carrier asks. ‘At the jar outside the wall,’ she says. His niece repeats the directions while tying the sand bag shut. You ask about the road toward Nanghin; the woman has travelled it and offers to draw the first turn. The carrier wants to finish bringing the water up before anyone rushes down the slick steps.
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.choice.route: Ask about the road toward Nanghin
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.choice.route_resul: The woman draws the road toward Nanghin on your board, beginning at the western gate. The niece repeats the turn while the water carrier lifts the last bucket. You leave with the route as they open the steps to the next person.
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.choice.scene: Help carry water up the steps
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.choice.scene_resul: You take one bucket while the carrier tests each step. His niece uses a little sand where his foot slips and keeps the rest in her bag. At the top he thanks you and points out the jar where visitors rinse their buckets before using the well.
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.title: The Water Carrier’s Steps
ev.ev_gap_chinginju.body: A dyer hands you a newly washed piece of blue cloth. It looks darker while wet and lightens as it dries. Customers complain that new cloth fades; he advises washing it separately twice. Should he pair this blue with white thread or yellow? He tests one corner before washing an entire bolt.
ev.ev_gap_chinginju.choice.route_result: “Go northwest on the main road to Chinghianfu.”
ev.ev_gap_chinginju.choice.scene_result: You compare both colours against the cloth. “White shows the pattern; yellow sits more firmly against the blue,” the dyer says. He keeps both for customers to choose.
ev.ev_gap_chinginju.title: Blue Cloth Beneath the Dyer’s Eaves
ev.ev_gap_coigangiu.body: By the Huai River, a boatman moves his fish baskets into the shade. Sun spoils fish quickly; dry grass under the catch absorbs water and keeps scales from sticking. He changes the grass as soon as it grows damp. For a northbound crossing, he advises reaching the ferry early: the afternoon wind blows against the boat.
ev.ev_gap_coigangiu.choice.route_result: “Go southeast on the broad road along the river to Paukin.”
ev.ev_gap_coigangiu.choice.scene: Ask how to line the fish baskets
ev.ev_gap_coigangiu.choice.scene_result: “Lay dry grass at the bottom, then put the fish above it. Leave room at the top, and do not seal the basket: heat needs a way out.”
ev.ev_gap_coigangiu.title: Fish Baskets at the Bow
ev.ev_gap_coiganju.body: At a street corner, an umbrella mender removes a split rib. Bamboo splits along its grain, he says, so it can be joined without shattering. A canopy pulled too tight turns inside out in the wind; a little slack makes it last longer. He hides the joint inside so rain does not follow the stitching through.
ev.ev_gap_coiganju.choice.route_result: “Follow the canal south, then turn east toward Tiju. Allow several days.”
ev.ev_gap_coiganju.choice.scene_result: You hold the handle while he binds the joint with fine thread. “Test it first in light rain. If something can be mended, there is no need to throw it away.”
ev.ev_gap_coiganju.title: The Umbrella Mender’s Bamboo Rib
ev.ev_gap_etzina.body: At Etzina’s well, a traveller hangs a waterskin upside down to dry. Water left inside turns foul in the sun. He rinses it, swirls a little wine inside, pours that away, and lets the skin dry. Before setting out, he squeezes each skin to hear whether air escapes through a leak.
ev.ev_gap_etzina.choice.route_result: “Go southeast to Egrigaia. Do not miss the wells along the road.”
ev.ev_gap_etzina.choice.scene_result: He points west towards the next posting stop near Etzina. “The wells are far apart. Check each waterskin before leaving, and repair any leak first.”
ev.ev_gap_etzina.title: An Old Waterskin at the Well
ev.ev_gap_fuju.body: At Fuju harbour, a pilot lowers a knotted rope straight into the water. Each knot marks about a foot of depth beneath the hull. As the tide falls, shoals appear and ships must wait for it to rise. A reading taken while the ship is moving is unreliable.
ev.ev_gap_fuju.choice.route_result: “Follow the coast southwest from here to Zayton.”
ev.ev_gap_fuju.choice.scene_result: You count six knots. “This ship can pass,” says the pilot. “Looking at the surface is not enough; you must know when the tide will turn.”
ev.ev_gap_fuju.title: The Tide Rope at the Harbour
ev.ev_gap_linju.body: At the Linju market, an umbrella maker opens a frame of bamboo ribs. He coats its paper with tung oil, especially the edge, to keep rain out. A rib too soft collapses; one too stiff breaks. He offers you the umbrella to test and warns you to keep the paper clear of mud.
ev.ev_gap_linju.choice.route_result: “Go northwest to Cacanfu, then ask for the ferry.”
ev.ev_gap_linju.choice.scene_result: You slowly open and close it. The maker says to fold along the ribs without crushing the paper. After rain, leave the canopy out to dry instead of holding it near a fire.
ev.ev_gap_linju.title: Paper Umbrellas at the Market
ev.ev_gap_mien.body: On the mountain road near Mien, a porter offers to show you the next fork before darkness makes it hard to see. His bamboo flask holds water boiled and cooled before filling; a clear stream can still carry silt. To recognise the road, he says, follow the bend of the river rather than a distant peak.
ev.ev_gap_mien.choice.route_result: “Go northeast along the main road to Kenjanfu.”
ev.ev_gap_mien.choice.scene: Ask him to show you the fork
ev.ev_gap_mien.choice.scene_result: He points out two small paths: one follows the river to the main road northeast, and the other climbs to a village. Stay near the river; do not follow the herb gatherers uphill.
ev.ev_gap_mien.title: A Tea Stall on the Mountain Road
ev.ev_gap_nanghin.body: At Nanghin’s gate, a guard blows a short whistle and a distant cart stops. One call asks people to slow; two ask for passage through the crowded entrance. He lets you try, but warns you not to blow near a horse’s face: a startled horse can kick. Watch its ears first.
ev.ev_gap_nanghin.choice.route_result: “Follow the Yangtze east toward Caiju. It is many days away.”
ev.ev_gap_nanghin.choice.scene_result: Your two notes have different lengths. The guard smiles. “On a narrow road, warn people first, then go around the back of the cart. Never suddenly step in front of a horse.”
ev.ev_gap_nanghin.title: A Bamboo Whistle at the Gate
ev.ev_gap_paukin.body: On a drying ground in Paukin, a farmer spreads grain thinly with a wooden rake. When the afternoon wind comes, thick patches stay damp after the rest has dried. He asks you to turn one side or test a handful. Grain that cracks under the teeth is ready for storage.
ev.ev_gap_paukin.choice.route_result: “Go south toward Cayu, then turn east for Tiju. Allow three days.”
ev.ev_gap_paukin.choice.scene_result: You roll a handful between your fingers. Dry husks are crisp and do not cling to the hand, the farmer says. Even then, check the weather before storing it: night dew can make it damp again.
ev.ev_gap_paukin.title: Grain on the Drying Ground
ev.ev_gap_pentam.body: A boat worker is using half a coconut shell to empty rainwater from a small craft drawn up beside the landing. Water drips through a crack in the shell. His nephew has brought a fresh one, but it is still full of flesh. ‘We cannot scrape it by smashing it,’ the man says. ‘I need the rim whole.’ You ask why he does not fetch a wooden scoop. He points to the shallow place where the boat will go: a heavy scoop is awkward when he has to reach beneath the boards. The nephew sits down to hollow the new shell with a blunt knife. He hears a pilot call from the quay and asks whether the craft is leaving at once. ‘Once the tide covers that pale stone,’ his uncle answers. The boy checks the stone, still dry above the water, and continues scraping. The worker tells you the same pilot can describe the route toward Java Major and the safer way through these local shallows.
ev.ev_gap_pentam.choice.route: Ask how to travel toward Java Major
ev.ev_gap_pentam.choice.route_result: The worker calls over the pilot, who marks the route toward Java Major on your board. His nephew points to the pale stone at the quay and repeats when their own small craft can pass it. You leave with the outward route while they finish the new ladle.
ev.ev_gap_pentam.choice.scene: Ask the pilot about the shoal
ev.ev_gap_pentam.choice.scene_result: The pilot shows you how he reads the dark and pale patches of water beside the landing. He lets the nephew describe where the little craft must turn, then corrects one spot where the boy guessed too early. The nephew checks the stone again and smiles when the tide begins to cover it.
ev.ev_gap_pentam.title: A Cracked Coconut Ladle
ev.ev_gap_sindafu.body: In a Chengdu tea house, a server sets bamboo tallies on the table. They record orders and refills so none is missed in the rush. He asks you to count how many rounds this table has had. When he first started, he confused them too, until the keeper taught him to sort them by colour.
ev.ev_gap_sindafu.choice.route_result: “Go northeast; beyond the river lies Cachanfu.”
ev.ev_gap_sindafu.choice.scene_result: You separate long tallies from short ones. The long mark refills, the short new tea. Each table needs its own bundle, or the count becomes confused.
ev.ev_gap_sindafu.title: Bamboo Tallies in the Tea House
ev.ev_gap_sinjumatu.body: At the Sinjumatu station, a groom checks the stitching on a leather bit. Loose seams rub the horse’s mouth; a whitening edge needs replacement. He leaves one finger’s width at the buckle, neither too tight nor too loose. Before harnessing the horse again, he lets it drink.
ev.ev_gap_sinjumatu.choice.route_result: “Go southeast along the watercourse to Coigangiu.”
ev.ev_gap_sinjumatu.choice.scene: Ask him to show you the inspection
ev.ev_gap_sinjumatu.choice.scene_result: He turns the bit over, checking from both sides towards the middle. Cracked leather must be replaced and a stiff buckle oiled. If a horse refuses to move, first see whether its tack hurts.
ev.ev_gap_sinjumatu.title: A Horse’s Bit at the Posting Station
ev.ev_gap_tiju.body: Outside Tiju, a knife grinder pushes a blade along a stone, lifting its tip slightly so the edge does not curl. He asks whether you want to try or need the way to Sinju (Zhenzhou), where many travellers take the river route. Once the blade is sharp, he wipes away stone dust that could cause rust.
ev.ev_gap_tiju.choice.route_result: “Go southwest through the canal country toward Sinju (Zhenzhou). The road takes more than a day.”
ev.ev_gap_tiju.choice.scene: Ask how to sharpen a knife
ev.ev_gap_tiju.choice.scene_result: He gives you an old blade to practise with. Push lightly and listen: a harsh sound means too much pressure. Stop if the edge heats, or you may soften the steel.
ev.ev_gap_tiju.title: A Whetstone at the Crossroads
ev.ev_hierusalem_entry.choice_1_result:
Nadia carries the basket as far as the corner and points to the gate. "Follow the stone road, then turn right at the cloth seller." She stops a messenger and asks him to walk with you as far as that shop.

When you look back, Nadia has turned into the narrow lane towards the inn. All six blocks are wrapped neatly in her basket.
ev.ev_hierusalem_entry.choice_2_result:
You help Nadia deliver the six blocks. The innkeeper counts them and offers you both a drink while he finds his coins. Nadia asks where tomorrow's caravan for Petra will gather. You spend the night in town, and in the morning she shows you the yard.

A driver is tying a bell to his mule. He tells you to leave by the eastern gate and join his group there. "Fill your water today." Nadia remembers that advice and fills the inn's water bucket on her way back to the shop.
ev.ev_ispahan_entry.choice_1_result: You follow Parvin’s directions through the lanes and mark Isfahan on your map.
ev.ev_ispahan_entry.choice_2_result: You stay in the shade for the day. Parvin’s nephew brings water after his last errand. You feel stronger when you leave, with Isfahan marked on your map.
ev.ev_java_major_battuta_a.choice_1_resu: You stay for the day while the steward and her assistant compare the seal marks with the cargo list. The merchant sees that his pack has remained closed and signs the corrected line. She thanks you in front of the waiting porters; by evening they greet you as someone who helped them finish the work.
ev.ev_java_major_battuta_a.choice_2_resu: After the seal is found, the merchant opens a corner of the fragrant wood for you to inspect. You pay for the full load. His assistant reties it, and the steward marks your name beside the new owner on the harbour list.
ev.ev_java_major_battuta_a.choice_3_resu: You spend a day by the water asking sailors where they stop on the way toward Samara. One draws the route across a board while another explains which landing has fresh water. The steward’s assistant copies the port names for his own list and asks the sailors to check his spelling.
ev.ev_java_major_entry.choice_1_result: The younger brother ties the fresh label securely while his sister from the spice house holds the crate steady. The sailor points out the road beyond the landing, and you cross the town with a clear sense of where its warehouses stand.
ev.ev_java_major_entry.choice_2_result: You spend another day with the family as they finish sorting the wet shipment.
