Their uncle arrives from the Chamba boat and marks its port and sea road on a board for you. The younger brother copies the names onto a new cargo list, this time keeping it beneath the roof.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a.choice_1_result: You walk the mulberry gardens with a silkworm keeper. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Cachanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a.choice_2_result: You buy raw silk from a cocoon market. You pay 8000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. You set the way to Egrigaia on your map.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a.choice_3_result: You stand at the roadside and watch the cocoon carts pass. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.body: West of the city a silk steward who walks the mulberry plains every morning draws you under a row of trees. He says Kenjanfu's wealth is leaf and worm — and that the roads to Cachanfu, Saianfu, and the north are written in the season of the harvest if you care to listen.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_1: Buy silk at the plain's harvest price
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_1_resul: He sells you silk at a price the workshops accept. The bolt is ready for the western road.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which road leads toward Saianfu
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_2_resul: Saianfu is marked on your map with the days between. The industrial road west is clear.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_3: Walk the gardens a day and note the mulberry season
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You spend a day among the trees. Cachanfu is named in the talk, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_a_followup.title: Kenjanfu: Among the Mulberry Plains
ev.ev_kenjanfu_b.choice_1_result: You tour the silk-and-gold workshops. You spend 2 days before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Saianfu on your map.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_b.choice_2_result: You buy lacquerware from an armourer's quarter. You pay 7000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The armourers speak of the buyer come from the western road.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_b.choice_3_result: You view Prince Mangalai's palace from the plain. You set what you saw into your travel book. A small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. The road to Kenjanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Kenjanfu on your map.
ev.ev_kenjanfu_entry.choice_3_result: You enter the sì at the hour of the evening drum. The abbot gives you tea and a parting line of scripture, which stays with you at the gate. You know the road to Kenjanfu well enough to draw it now.
ev.ev_kerman_a.choice_1_result: You stay at the forge for a day while Rashid fits a buckle to a leather strap. You record his method in your travel book. Before you leave, he invites you back to discuss the road’s demands on the metal.
ev.ev_kerman_a.choice_2_result: You pay 100 silver for the parcel of turquoise and write down where the trader says it came from. Rashid sees you looking at his workshop and asks you to return when he has finished the next fitting.
ev.ev_kerman_a.choice_3_result: The caravan masters name Yazd to the north and Hormuz toward the gulf. You mark both places on your map. They ask where you have travelled; after a long conversation, they treat you as a familiar traveller on this road.
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.body:
When you return, Rashid has laid out a finished saddle fitting and a piece of worn leather. His niece rides with a caravan next month, and he wants her pack saddle to last the whole journey. An unworked merchant bundle of Damascus steel waits on the shelf beside him.

‘She would rather I made her a sword,’ he says. ‘She needs this more.’ He offers you the bundle at his usual price, can explain the road toward Hormuz, or would be glad if you stayed the day to help him test the straps and later spoke well of his work.

His niece arrives with the pack saddle and asks whether the new strap will slip when the animal climbs. Rashid makes her pull it herself. She braces a foot against the bench and tugs; the buckle holds. ‘That is what I wanted to know,’ she says. You ask what is in the bundle on the shelf. ‘Damascus steel for a trader,’ Rashid answers. ‘I can sell you the full lot. The smaller fittings for my niece are already spoken for.’ He turns back to her saddle, waiting to hear whether you need the road or the goods.
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the merchant lot of Damascus steel for 146 silver
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 146 silver for the merchant lot of Damascus steel. Rashid checks the wrapping before handing it to you and shows you the piece from which he forged his niece’s buckle. You record what he taught you about the material and his forge.
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.choice_2_result: Rashid describes the passes and water stops he knows on the road to Hormuz. You mark the city and write his directions in your travel book.
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to test the straps and recommend his work
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day checking straps with Rashid. When his niece comes to collect the saddle, she thanks you for helping. Rashid introduces you to other craftsmen in the lane; your name is received warmly here.
ev.ev_kerman_a_followup.title: Rashid’s Saddle Fitting
ev.ev_kerman_b.choice_1_result: You spend the day in the workshop, watching Soraya secure the loose threads. You draw the finished pattern in your travel book before leaving.
ev.ev_kerman_b.choice_2_result: You pay 100 silver for the merchant bundle of silk. Soraya wraps it securely and suggests keeping one length aside. On the road you give that length to a travelling companion whose coat has worn thin at the cuffs. She thanks you and helps tie the rest of the bundle more securely before the party moves on.
ev.ev_kerman_b.choice_3_result: At the mews you pay 135 silver for a trained falcon. The falconer shows you how to hold its jesses and names Camadi beyond the hills. You mark the place on your map.
ev.ev_kerman_entry.choice_1_result: Soraya shows you the lane past the workshops. You mark Kerman on your map and continue.
ev.ev_kerman_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the market stalls, noting the metalwork and silk patterns in your travel book. Soraya helps you mark the town on your map.
ev.ev_kerman_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the mosque courtyard. A trader there gives you a small keepsake as a reminder of the visit, and the people you meet greet you warmly. You mark Kerman on your map.
ev.ev_keshimur_a.choice_1_result: You spend the day hearing the caretaker and cousin compare their versions. The boy finally asks his mother about the traveller who started the tale; you record what each person actually knows and look forward to their next account.
ev.ev_keshimur_a.choice_2_result: You watch the caretaker tend the lamp, then ask the wool carrier which direction leads toward Badakhshan. She names the place and the people who travel that way; you mark it on your map. Others remember that you listened respectfully.
ev.ev_keshimur_a.choice_3_result: The caretaker and wool carrier tell you where travellers turn toward Kabul and Badakhshan. You mark both places on your map and write down their different advice about the mountain weather.
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.body:
The shrine caretaker has asked the guide’s cousin to bring his mother. She remembers hearing the story of the speaking image from a traveller when she was young, but cannot recall what the image supposedly said. The boy is disappointed. ‘I thought you knew the words,’ he tells her. She says the part she remembers clearly is the traveller getting lost in the mist and being found near the lamp.

You ask the caretaker what he has learned from the other visitors. He has put their names beside the versions they told, so no one has to pretend they all heard the same thing. A wool carrier arrives with news of travellers toward Kabul and Delhi. She says the roads divide after the lower valley; the caretaker asks her to draw that on the back of his page.

The boy watches the pencil move. A guide waiting outside offers to accompany you for 4 silver if you decide to take a mountain stage. The caretaker asks his young visitor to repeat his mother’s version once more before she goes home.
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_1: Stay a day and hear the family story carefully
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_1_resul: You spend the day letting mother and son tell the story in their own words. The caretaker writes down what each remembers; by evening the boy understands why her version differs from his. You keep their account in your notes.
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the wool carrier about Kabul and Delhi
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_2_resul: The wool carrier shows you the lower valley where travellers divide toward Kabul or Delhi. You mark both places on your map and record her warning about mist at the high turn.
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_3: Pay 4 silver for the mountain guide
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You pay 4 silver to the guide. He checks your load, agrees on the next departure, and introduces you to the carriers he will travel with. You leave the shrine better prepared for the mountain stage.
ev.ev_keshimur_a_followup.title: What the Caretaker Actually Heard
ev.ev_keshimur_b.choice_1_result: You pay 6 silver and spend seven days with the guide. The cousin practises reading his corrected page beside you; by the end the guide has named the approaches toward Delhi and you have recorded his mountain advice.
ev.ev_keshimur_b.choice_2_result: You stay seven days with the valley families. The guide’s mother makes room at the hearth, and his cousin takes you to the bent pine once the mist lifts. You record the week and leave knowing them better.
ev.ev_keshimur_b.choice_3_result: You pay 100 silver for the full turquoise parcel. The merchant checks the wrapping and count with you; the guide’s mother gives you a dry place to tie it onto your load. The stone traders remember your fair dealing.
ev.ev_keshimur_entry.choice_1_result: The guide’s mother fills your bowl once more before you leave. You mark Kashmir on your map; the cousin reminds you to look for the bent pine where the path turns.
ev.ev_keshimur_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with the market families, listening to growers and wool carriers describe their work. By evening the cousin has learned which lane he missed in the mist. You record what you heard and mark Kashmir on your map.
ev.ev_keshimur_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the old hill shrine and speak respectfully with the people caring for it. The guide’s cousin shows you the way back; they remember your visit, and you mark Kashmir on your map.
ev.ev_kinsay_a.choice_1_result: You hire a boat and spend the day on the canals under the twelve thousand bridges. The boatman reads the water like a book, and at the turning of the afternoon he ships his oars to tell you what the bridges keep.
ev.ev_kinsay_a.choice_2_result: You cross Kinsay's bridges until you lose count before noon. A boatman laughs. “Stop counting bridges and look at the boats beneath them. More than a hundred may pass this channel in a day.”
ev.ev_kinsay_a.choice_3_result: You climb the drum-tower and see a hundred canals below, all alive with boats. The road south to Suju is now on your map, and the view is in your book.
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.body: The water officer who poled you through the city calls you back at the quay, his long pole still dripping. He points beneath the bridges. More than a hundred canals cross the city, he says, and stone-paved streets keep carts from sinking after heavy rain. Each bridge must be checked and repaired or ships and cargo will stop. He shows you the tax marks cut into the quay stones: every boat pays by the rule written there. “The City of Heaven does not run by itself.”
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_1: Ask the keeper how the tolls are reckoned on the water
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_1_result: Reading the tax marks, the officer explains that grain boats pay according to cargo, passenger boats according to the people aboard. Funeral boats pay nothing. “Do not tell the keeper of the accounts,” he jokes. “He would count every boat.”
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which water-road leads south to Suju
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_2_result: The keeper draws the water-road south on the flat of his hand: down the canal to the great lake, then by the river where the silk boats pass. The road to Suju is now clear on your map.
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to walk the bridges with the keeper
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day crossing bridges with the keeper, learning to read the toll marks and the state of each arch. It costs you a day of the road, but the twelve thousand bridges are no longer a number to you.
ev.ev_kinsay_a_followup.title: Kinsay: The Water-Keeper of the Twelve Thousand Bridges
ev.ev_kinsay_b.choice_1_result: You pay twenty thousand pieces for two sacks of pepper at the customs house. A merchant's fortune in spice now rides in your cargo, and the freight is written in your book.
ev.ev_kinsay_b.choice_2_result: You bathe in perfumed water and dine on ten courses in a house overlooking the market squares. The steward who served you clears the last dish and lingers, as if the account of the city is not yet closed.
ev.ev_kinsay_b.choice_3_result: You count forty cart-loads of pepper pass the customs in a single day. The sea-road to Zayton, where the ships bring it, is now on your map.
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.body: A merchant of the ten great squares of Kinsay takes you for a buyer and keeps you by the pepper stalls. He tells you that the pepper he sells comes by sea to the port of Zayton and up the river to Kinsay, and that the city consumes in a single day a quantity of it that a kingdom of the West would not use in a year. He speaks of the twelve guilds of the handicrafts, each with its twelve thousand houses and its own gate, and of the ten markets where, three days in every week, every stall is filled with the hunters' and the fishers' catch. If you mean to deal honestly, he says, he will show you how the day's accounts are kept — the pepper weighed, the price set, the cartage reckoned. What you do with the offer is your own.
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_1: Buy pepper at the merchant's own price
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_1_result: The merchant weighs out a load of pepper for you at his list price, a courtesy he shows to travellers who ask the truth of the markets before they trade. The pepper goes into your goods, and the account of the ten great squares goes into your book.
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_2: Ask which sea-port the pepper comes from
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_2_result: The merchant names the port of Zayton, where the junks put in from the southern seas, and the river-road by which the pepper comes up to Kinsay. The sea-port is now on your map.
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to watch the twelve guilds at their accounting
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day among the guild halls, watching the weights set and the prices entered in the great books. It costs you a day, but you have seen how a city with a million doors keeps its accounts straight.
ev.ev_kinsay_b_followup.title: Kinsay: The Account of the Ten Great Squares
ev.ev_kinsay_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You find junks bound for India in the port of El Zaitun and take passage in one belonging to El Malik El Zahir, the King of Sumatra, whose servants are Muslims. You go down the river from El Khansa, past Kanjanfur, to the sea, and set your course with a good wind for the open ocean and the long road home.
ev.ev_kinsay_battuta_a.choice_2_result: The sky grows dark and the storm drives the junk into a sea unknown to the sailors; they are terribly afraid and wish to put back, but it is impossible. You betake yourselves to repentance and prayer with all your hearts, and the merchants make many vows. After sunrise the wind calms in some degree, and God gives you a good wind to steer your course away from peril.
ev.ev_kinsay_battuta_a.choice_3_result: At daybreak the sailors point to a mountain in the sea, about twenty miles away, though you are far from land and no mountain was ever seen in that part of the sea. They look upon it with the utmost perturbation and take leave of one another, saying it is a Rokh, and that if he sees you, you shall assuredly perish. But a good wind comes, and you steer away, and see no more of him, nor ever know the particulars of his shape.
ev.ev_kinsay_c.choice_1_result: You hire a pleasure boat with musicians and wine and push out onto the West Lake. As dusk falls and the lanterns are lit on the water, the boatmaster leans close to speak against the music.
ev.ev_kinsay_c.choice_2_result: You stand on the bank and watch painted pleasure boats pass slowly across the lake.
ev.ev_kinsay_c.choice_3_result: You wait for the moon to rise over the lake. What the moonlight shows you, no one in the empire can argue with; it settles in you like a certainty.
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.body: The pipa player who sang among the lantern boats finds you on the lake shore the next evening, her instrument wrapped and her fee refused. She will not take payment, she says, for a song heard on the water is half the lake's own. She tells you that the lake is the pleasure-ground of the city of heaven: the boats go out at dusk with wine and lanterns, and the surveyors once counted the houseboats at more than a thousand, not one of them earning its keep by trade. The city works on the land and plays on the water, and a traveller who has seen only the markets has seen half of Kinsay. She asks what you mean to carry away from the lake — a blessing, a belief, or an evening's music.
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_1: Ask the singer for a blessing of the lake to carry on the road
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_1_result: The singer threads a reed into your collar and sings a line of the lake's own song over it. For the length of your stay by the water, the doors of the city seem to open a little wider for you.
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_2: Ask what the lake folk believe about the lanterns
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_2_result: She tells you that the lanterns are set on the water for the drowned, so that no soul is left to find its way in the dark, and that the pleasure boats are decked for the living to enjoy what the dead remember. The belief of the lake is now written in your travel book.
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_3: Stay until the moon rises to hear the boats' music
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.choice_3_result: You remain until moonrise. Lantern boats glide past one after another. A boatman's work song mingles with the pipa. After her last song, a woman asks, “Do people sing like this on the water where you come from?”
ev.ev_kinsay_c_followup.title: Kinsay: The Lanterns of the West Lake
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.body: The first answer does not end at the gate. A boatman who works the grain canal draws you aside by the wharf and asks what you intend to carry away from Kinsay. Beyond the question lies the canals and the grain boats; he offers to set a name to your name, a name the customs house will remember. Choose what you will make of the sign.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the name and ask the boatman who can vouch for it
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You take the name the boatman offers and ask who can vouch for it. He names two clerks of the wharf, and the matter opens again.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the boatman and keep your own counsel
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank the boatman and keep your own counsel. The matter closes at the wharf, and nothing more is asked of you in Kinsay.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a.title: Kinsay: The Mark at the Gate
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a_resolution.bo: You have agreed to carry the boatman's name with you — a name the customs house will remember. It will not decide the whole journey, but at the next canal toll his name may halve your wait.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_a_resolution.ch: You deliver the name before nightfall. The boatman's word now travels with your name, and the wharf folk have a reason to receive you.
Keep the boatman's name in your travel book
You keep the boatman's name in your travel book and spend a day setting it down plainly. The record is made; the favour waits for a road that may never call on it.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b.body: The answer sends a rumour along the road. Before the day is out, a grain porter finds you on the wharf with a second account of the canals and the grain boats — how the canal tolls run, and which bridge opens for a loaded boat. It is less grand than a traveller's tale, and more useful.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You follow the porter's practical advice and ask him to set it down. He writes the account out for you, and the canal's true measures come into your hand.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the account with the porter
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You thank the porter but decline his explanation. He takes back the paper. “I must return to work. You can find me at the quay if you change your mind.”
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b.title: Kinsay: The Road Behind the Answer
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b_resolution.bo: You have chosen to carry the porter's account with you — how the canal tolls run, and which bridge opens for a loaded boat. It will not decide the whole journey, but it will save you more than it cost to learn.
ev.ev_kinsay_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Tell the next boatman before nightfall
You tell the next boatman before nightfall. The canal's measures now travel ahead of you, and where they land, your name follows.
Keep the toll-schedule in your travel book
You spend a day copying the toll-schedule into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_kinsay_entry.choice_1_result: The clerks of the shìbó sī weigh your cargo on the wharf scales and write your name into the canal register. As you turn away, a boatman who works the grain canal calls to you from the water's edge.
ev.ev_kinsay_entry.choice_2_result: You ask several people and hear different answers. Near dusk an old boatman selling fish beckons. “Want to know how this city lives? Look at the river. Boats bring goods in, bridges carry people across, and the tax officer counts what each boat holds.”
ev.ev_kinsay_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day walking the great market of Kinsay and carry away a load of goods. The market of the city of Heaven is now written in your book.
ev.ev_kinsay_entry.choice_4_result: A traveller tells how he came down the river from Kinsay and took ship for the sea roads, and how the way back to his own land ran through the islands; he will tell the whole voyage, if you ask.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.body: The temple reader who taught you the cups meets you once more by the threshold, her two wooden cups wrapped in cloth. She does not ask what you have done with the divination; the cups, she says, do not keep accounts. Instead she lays out what remains of her working life: a set of carved cups that have answered for her these twenty years, a casting of the water-road south that the cups have blessed, or a day at her side to learn the cups' third answer — the laugh — by ear. Take what will serve you, she says, for a craft is only as good as the hand that carries it.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take the reader's carved cups as a parting gift
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: The reader wraps the cups in cloth and gives them to you without ceremony. What she taught you by the threshold is now written where you can consult it on the road.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask which water-road the cups would bless
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: The reader casts the cups once more, and they grant leave for the water-road south, past the lake, toward Suju. The road is now drawn on your map, and the cups' answer goes with it.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_3: Linger a day to learn the laugh of the cups
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You spend a day at the temple threshold learning how to hear the laugh of the cups — the cast that means the craft has no counsel yet. It costs you time, but the reader's ear is now partly your own, and the temples of the land have heard of it.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_followup.title: Kinsay: The Temple Reader's Parting Cups
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_jiaobei.choice_1_res: You pay the temple reader and sit at her low table while she lays out the three cups. The teaching is quick and exact, and at the end she closes her hand over the cups and gives you a parting throw.
ev.ev_kinsay_mentor_jiaobei.choice_2_res: The temple reader shows how the two cups answer by their fall. The art of the cups is now written in your book, though its practice stays with her.
ev.ev_kiovia_entry.choice_1_result: You follow the riverside path and mark Kyiv on your map before continuing.
ev.ev_kiovia_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day by the landing. Olena points out the northern road to Moscow and the people preparing to take it. You mark Kyiv, that road, and Moscow on your map.
ev.ev_kiovia_mentor_runes.choice_1_resul: You pay the traveller 50 silver and spend seven days learning how he draws and reads the runes. At the end he lets you cast them yourself, then packs away his sister’s stave.
ev.ev_kiovia_mentor_runes.choice_2_resul: He draws one mark and tells you how he reads it. You write down his account in your travel book, then return the stave to him.
ev.ev_kiovia_runes_ford.choice_2_result: You carry your bag aboard and cross with the other travellers. On the far bank, the ferryman hands back a strap that slipped from your pack. You thank her and continue.
ev.ev_linju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Linju opens on your map.
ev.ev_linju_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Linju on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar.choice_1_result: You pay 135 silver for the full lot. Mira and her daughter check every tag before wrapping it for you; the cousin’s parcel stays on their own mat. The girl promises to tell you more of his road when she is free.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar.choice_2_result: Mira’s daughter traces the river towns on your map and names the road toward Sachiu. You note how her cousin’s parcel came from a picker near Cotan; she is glad someone asked about his journey.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.body:
Mira’s daughter has finished reading her cousin’s note. He wrote that the river was high when he left Cotan and that the pickers would have to wait for lower water. Mira asks her to put the date beside his name in the ledger. ‘If he returns next season, we should know which stones he meant,’ she says. The daughter writes it carefully, then looks at the loose strip on her sandal and laughs at his reminder.

You ask whether the dealer has more jade to sell. Mira brings out another full trading parcel, priced at 135 silver. She lets her daughter show the marks on its wrapping; this one came with a different caravan and has its own tally. The girl asks if you want to hear where the river pickers work when the water falls. Mira says there is time before the next customer.

A porter comes to collect the cousin’s parcel. The daughter gives him the note to return with it, then asks him to tell her cousin that the sandal has finally been repaired.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_1: Buy the other full jade parcel for 135 silver
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_1_resul: You pay 135 silver for the separate lot. Mira’s daughter reads its tally aloud and helps you seal the wrapping. The cousin’s parcel goes with the porter; your own lot is ready for the road.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_2: Ask the daughter about the rivers and Sachiu road
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_2_resul: The daughter tells you when the pickers can work the riverbanks near Cotan. She also names Sachiu as a town on the road east. You mark it on your map while she folds the cousin’s letter.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and hear how the salt flats change
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.choice_3_resul: You stay a day. Mira tells you which salt flats caravans used last season and which wells had to be checked again. Her daughter compares the dates in the ledger, and you add their account to your travel book.
ev.ev_lop_bazaar_followup.title: The Parcel from Cotan
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai.choice_1_result: You pay Arslan 2 silver. He checks your water skins with you and marks the crossing toward Sachiu; the family’s daughter comes over to show how she fixed the stopper. He asks you back before departure to go over the stages.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai.choice_2_result: You pay 1.2 silver and spend eight days waiting for the shared caravan to assemble. The family uses the time to mend its load straps; you check yours alongside them. Arslan marks the road to Sachiu, and a place in the party is ready when you choose to leave.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai.choice_3_result: You pay 0.8 silver for the provision bundle. The innkeeper checks the seal on each water skin and wraps the dry food against dust. You take the supplies and remember what Arslan said about counting usable water.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai_followup.body:
Arslan has redrawn the route on a wooden board because the inn floor was swept before the family could copy it. The father holds the board while his daughter reads the well names back. She stops at a mark that looks like a grain sack. ‘That is where the cook found dry fuel,’ Arslan says. ‘I should have drawn a fire.’ The cook laughs and says a sack is closer to what she carried.

You ask how the party will know when to move. Arslan explains the hour he expects to leave and asks each traveller to show him a full water skin. The daughter raises hers with its new stopper. Her father asks if they must buy another bundle of food. Arslan gives him a list but says to count what the family already has first.

The innkeeper has an extra provision bundle for 12 silver. Arslan can also spend the next day explaining the stages in detail. He leaves the board against the wall so everyone can check the marks again.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai_followup.choice_1: Confirm your place with Arslan and copy the route

You copy the stages toward Sachiu from Arslan’s board. He checks that you know which well follows the salt flat and confirms your place in the party. You can choose your departure when you have finished preparing.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai_followup.choice_2: Buy the extra provision bundle for 12 silver
You pay 12 silver for the extra bundle. The innkeeper checks the dried food and water skins against Arslan’s list, then ties them where you can reach them easily on the road.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai_followup.choice_3: Spend another day learning the stages
You stay another day. Arslan takes you through the board one stage at a time, and the cook corrects the fuel marks. You leave knowing what to check before each move.
ev.ev_lop_caravanserai_followup.title: Arslan’s Route Board
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.body:
The well keeper from Aysen’s inn finds you while his granddaughter is drying a stained map against the wall. She has copied a list of wells, but the ink ran across one name when she spilled tea. ‘I can remember the place,’ the old man says. ‘I want her to see how I check it before she writes it again.’ He asks you to hold the map in the light.

You ask whether the damaged name belongs to a well still in use. The granddaughter says a caravan stopped there last season. Her grandfather asks which guide she heard it from. She recalls Arslan and points out his mark beside the name. The old man agrees to ask him that evening. He has another copy of the list for you if you want to carry it, though he asks you to keep the uncertain name marked as uncertain.

The girl smooths the paper on the table. She has saved a blank strip for the answer, and she waits for her grandfather to fetch Arslan.

The granddaughter asks him if the bitter well should stay on the list. ‘Yes,’ he says. ‘A warning is useful even when the water changes again.’ She puts a dot beside it, ready to add a new date after the next traveller reports back.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the copy and ask how they check the well
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.choice_1_result: You take the copy with the uncertain place left blank. The granddaughter writes Arslan’s name beside it so you know whom to ask. The well keeper says he will meet you again once they have checked the report.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank them and leave the list at the inn
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.choice_2_result: You thank the family and leave the list with the granddaughter. She weighs the corners with pebbles so it will dry flat. The well keeper wishes you a careful crossing.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a.title: A Note from the Well Keeper
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a_resolution.body:
By evening, the granddaughter has found Arslan. He remembers stopping at the well, but says its name changed when a nearby caravan camp moved. The well keeper repeats both names to you while his granddaughter writes them side by side. ‘If someone asks with the older name, they should still find the water,’ she says.

You ask whether the well is sweet. Arslan says it was when he last used it, and the keeper adds the date to the note. The granddaughter draws a small cup beside the name, then asks whether that mark is too childish. Her grandfather says it will help him find the line when he is tired.

The paper has dried. The family has supper waiting, and there is time either to take the checked account now or to stay one more day and copy the full list in your own hand.

The granddaughter writes only the names of those who saw the well themselves. Her grandfather checks the line and asks her to make the date large enough for tired eyes.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a_resolution.choic: You take the checked account before supper. The granddaughter reads the two well names back to you, and you repeat them once so she knows the writing is clear.
Spend another day copying the full list

You spend the next day copying the wells. The granddaughter checks your lines while her grandfather mends a water-skin stopper. By evening your book carries the full account, including the date of Arslan’s report.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_a_resolution.title: The Name of the Well
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.body:
The caravan cook from Aysen’s inn comes to find you with a list of water stops. She has put a mark beside every well where her party was able to cook. Her younger brother reads the list aloud and stops at one name. ‘We did not use that well last time,’ he says. She agrees: the water was too bitter, and they brought enough from the previous stop.

You ask whether another party might have a different report. The cook says Arslan did last season, before the late floods. She wants to date her own list so travellers can compare the accounts. Her brother says he will copy it once she has finished. He was with her on the crossing but still remembers the taste of each camp’s stew better than the well names.

The cook has a clean page ready for your book. She asks whether you want to keep a copy or let her take it back to the inn wall where more people can read it.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.choice_1: Keep a dated copy of the cook’s list
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.choice_1_result: You keep the dated copy. Her brother checks the spelling of the last well, then promises to bring another page if Arslan adds a new report.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.choice_2: Let the cook post the list at the inn
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.choice_2_result: The cook takes the sheet back to the inn. Her brother holds it while she pins the top corners. A traveller already waiting there reads the date before asking about the bitter well.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b.title: The Cook’s Water List
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b_resolution.body:
The cook’s brother returns with Arslan’s newer account. A well on her list has a repaired lining, and a caravan used it last week. The cook does not cross out the older warning. She writes the new date beneath it and asks her brother to read both lines aloud. He does, then asks if everyone will understand why the reports differ.

You suggest writing who made each report. The cook adds her name to the first and Arslan’s to the second. Her brother grins; he can now tell the travellers which person to ask. A man waiting to leave the inn listens and checks the water in his own skins before speaking.

The cook offers you the updated copy. If you stay the day, she can show you the inn’s full wall of dated notes and how often it changes.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b_resolution.choic: Share the updated list with the next party

You read both dated reports to the next party. Its cook notes the repaired well, then checks how much water they carry. Aysen hears you name both witnesses and thanks you for passing the account on clearly.
Spend a day copying the full wall of notes
You spend a day copying the dated notes. The cook’s brother checks the names with you and points out where an older warning still helps. Your book now holds a record that can be updated on the road.
ev.ev_lop_consequence_b_resolution.title: A Second Note on the Wall
ev.ev_lop_entry.choice_1_result: You rest for a day, check your water skin and talk with Aysen’s nephew while the caravan sorts its loads. The route toward Sachiu is marked for you; the old well keeper comes back after supper.
ev.ev_lop_entry.choice_2_result: The well keeper tells you which water has turned bitter and which is still used. You listen to Aysen and her nephew check the sacks, then record what you learned about the desert before the caravan leaves.
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.body:
Mergen and his niece find you outside the inn, where yesterday’s wind has left a fresh ridge of sand against the stones. He asks her to say what changed. She points out a narrow gap that had been clear in the morning. You ask whether a caravan could still pass through it. ‘After we check the ground beneath,’ Mergen says. His niece takes a stick and feels for firm gravel.

The cook walks by with a water list and asks whether their lesson has reached the wells yet. The niece laughs and shows her the old and new names on the page. Mergen says he learned to listen to the cook after once taking a dry path without enough water. His niece teases him for telling that story again; he says repeating a useful mistake costs less than making it.

He offers to copy his notes for you, spend a day answering questions about this crossing, or mark the road toward Sachiu on your map. His niece tests the gap one more time before anyone puts a foot on it.
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.choice_1_resul: Mergen copies the wind marks and the two well names into your book. His niece checks the last line and adds the date. You take their account onto the road.
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.choice_2: Stay a day and ask how to judge this crossing
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.choice_2_resul: You stay a day with Mergen and his niece. They compare the ground, the wind and the cook’s water list with you before suggesting a departure hour. You leave better prepared for the crossing.
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.choice_3: Ask the niece to mark the road toward Sachiu
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.choice_3_resul: The niece marks the road toward Sachiu on your map, asking Mergen to check the last well. He agrees with her line. She rolls up the map and makes you name the first stop before handing it back.
ev.ev_lop_mentor_followup.title: Mergen’s Second Look
ev.ev_lop_shrine.choice_1_result: You give Tuma 0.5 silver for lamp oil. Her grandson fills the little dish and sets it beside the wall. Tuma thanks you before asking the merchant to finish his dated note.
ev.ev_lop_shrine.choice_2_result: You listen as the merchant explains how the well changed. Tuma reads an older name on the wall and remembers the family who left it. You take their accounts into your travel notes.
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.body:
The merchant who spoke with Tuma has returned with two other travellers. One used the old well name, the other a newer one. Tuma places them before the cave wall and asks each to describe the same place. Her grandson draws a small cup beside both names. ‘Will people know these mean one well?’ he asks. Tuma tells him to write the distance from the next camp as well.

You ask how she keeps old reports from misleading people. Tuma says she lets later travellers add dates and names, then reads the reports together. The merchant points to a charcoal line left by monks who once stayed in the cave. He wants to copy it before the wind wears it away. Tuma brings him a lamp so he can see.

The grandson holds the light while the merchant writes. Tuma says she can read the older account aloud, or give you room to copy it yourself. There is also an empty oil dish for those who wish to help keep the lamp burning.
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_1: Ask Tuma to read the older account
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_1_resul: Tuma reads the older marks aloud, stopping when the merchant explains a newer well name. Her grandson copies both names. You leave knowing which parts of the cave account still help travellers.
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_2: Give 0.3 silver for the cave lamps
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_2_resul: You give Tuma 0.3 silver. Her grandson fills the lamp and returns it to the merchant, who can now finish copying the worn line. Tuma thanks you as the light steadies.
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_3: Spend a day copying the cave wall
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.choice_3_resul: You spend a day copying the wall. Tuma reads names you cannot make out, and her grandson holds the lamp when the light fades. Your notes preserve both the old account and the new dates.
ev.ev_lop_shrine_followup.title: A New Mark Beside the Old
ev.ev_maabar_entry.choice_1_result: The cloth seller points you toward the market well and the road beyond it. The boy carries water to the groom as you pass. You continue with the way through Maabar clear in mind.
ev.ev_maabar_entry.choice_2_result: You stay for a day. The mother sells her fish before the heat grows strong, and the cloth seller shows how she folds the last bolt for the carriers. The boy returns to tell them all about the horse. By evening you know both the coast road and the people of the market.
ev.ev_maabar_site_gap.choice_1_result: The carrier walks you to the corner where the land road turns toward Coilum. He shows which track his loaded cart uses and asks you to repeat the first turn. You leave him to collect his cloth once the weaver finishes.
ev.ev_maabar_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the neighbouring threads apart while the apprentice overlaps the broken ends and rolls them together. The weaver lets the loom move once, then checks that the join lies inside the edge. She shows you why the thicker strand would have left a mark across the cloth.
ev.ev_maldive_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You spend three days helping the clerk take down each family's account of the net. The two women agree how to share the next repair after seeing the work written side by side. The clerk pays you a small fee, and the households thank you for giving both a chance to be heard.
ev.ev_maldive_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You contribute to the wedding meal and stay for two days. The clerk's niece finishes her list in time to help her family, and you carry dishes between the house and the courtyard. Her relatives thank you for sharing the work and the cost.
ev.ev_maldive_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day at the landing with the pilot. He shows you where his boat waits for the tide and traces the sea passage toward Melibar on a board. The clerk's niece comes to ask whether he will attend the wedding before sailing; he promises to return for the meal.
ev.ev_maldive_entry.choice_1_result: You step ashore, help clear the landing and greet the people waiting for the boat. The stallkeeper tells you which path reaches the guesthouse, while the daughter returns her two shells to her mother for safekeeping. Your careful arrival earns a warm welcome in the village.
ev.ev_mecha_entry.choice_1_result: The woman points out the road through the town and tells you which shelter to ask at farther on. Her brother returns the patched skin to its owner before you leave. You continue with the turns through Mecha clear in mind.
ev.ev_mecha_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at the shelter. In the evening the cousin arrives, names Medina and traces the northward route on a board, including the first place to replenish water. The older traveller thanks the family for finding his skin. You leave knowing both the town and the way toward Medina.
ev.ev_mecha_site_gap.choice_1_result: The daughter points out the northern road toward Medina and names the first water stop on it. The traveller repeats her directions before loading the jar. You follow the turn on the ground, then thank her for showing you.
ev.ev_mecha_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the cart's side rail while she cushions the light jar with cloth. The potter shows you the difference between its thinner wall and the heavy jar left in shade. The traveller gives the packed jar a gentle push; it stays in place, and the daughter smiles.
ev.ev_medina_entry.choice_1_result: The keeper points out the road beyond the guesthouse and names the first place where you can ask for water. The traveller returns to her mat to finish packing. You continue with Medina's streets clear in mind.
ev.ev_medina_entry.choice_2_result: You stay for a day at the guesthouse. The keeper and the northern traveller compare their routes and share a meal with you after the crowd thins. You sleep well, regain your strength and leave knowing the station's doors and streets.
ev.ev_medina_site_gap.choice_1_result: The keeper takes you to the gate and points out the road toward Petra. He names a place to replenish water before the next dry stretch. His daughter repeats the turn for the traveller beside you, making sure both of you heard it.
ev.ev_medina_site_gap.choice_2_result: You bring the bucket while the daughter lifts the lid and clears away the leaf. The keeper pours the water slowly so no grit falls from the rim. She sets the ladle back on its clean cloth and offers the waiting traveller the first cup.
ev.ev_melibar_a.choice_1_result: You spend a day beside the pepper shed. The watchman shows the loader how to keep the sacks dry while the seller checks each mark against the ship's list. The pilot explains the handover as the boat moves off. When the last sack is secure, the seller invites you back to speak with her carriers.
ev.ev_melibar_a.choice_2_result: You pay for a full trade sack of pepper. The seller checks its seam and tells the loader to keep it above the wet cargo. She names the ship that will call at Cail, then asks you to meet her carriers before deciding how to take your sack onward.
ev.ev_melibar_a.choice_3_result: The pilot points along the coast toward Coilum and farther toward Maabar. He shows where vessels wait for the turn of wind and which road the shore carriers take. You repeat the two names to the loader, who has heard them often but never asked which came first.
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.body: The pepper seller calls you back to the shed while the carrier she trusts is checking an outgoing boat. Her son has copied the cargo marks, but one sack on the board is listed for Cail and another for a nearer landing. “Do not swap them because they look alike,” she tells him. He reads the marks aloud and moves the bags to separate piles. The carrier offers a full sack for sale at the market's price. You ask where he will take the rest. He traces the coast toward Coilum and Maabar on a board, then asks the boy to show the first turn again. A boatman bringing in a wet rope calls from the quay that the next departure depends on the wind. The seller nods and tells her son to keep the sacks under cover until they know which boat is ready. The son asks whether the sacks may stay there overnight. His mother checks the roof for leaks before she promises.
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the carrier’s sack of pepper
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay the carrier for a full sack of pepper. The seller's son compares its mark with the corrected list and helps you tie it for travel. The carrier points out the vessel calling at Cail before handing the sack over.
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_2: Ask about the Coilum and Maabar roads
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_2_result: The carrier marks the roads toward Coilum and Maabar, then the boatman explains which passage is open in the present wind. The boy repeats both directions until his mother is satisfied. You leave knowing the two destinations and how cargo reaches them.
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day with the harbour carriers
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day helping the carrier keep pepper sacks beneath the dry awning while boats come and go. The seller's son reads each cargo mark before a bag moves. By the last handover you understand why the same coast can give different cargoes different departures.
ev.ev_melibar_a_followup.title: Melibar: The Pepper Seller’s Carriers
ev.ev_melibar_b.choice_1_result: You stay through the day around the harbour shrine. The attendant makes room for visitors, and the pearl seller keeps her basket out of their way. By evening the sailor has shown the younger boatmen how he finds the northern star; you leave knowing what people here watch before travelling by sea.
ev.ev_melibar_b.choice_2_result: You hold a straight rod beside the mast while the older sailor shows the younger boatmen where the northern star rises above the water. He thanks you for keeping the sight steady, and the pearl seller moves her lamp so they can read the mark. The people at the harbour remember your help.
ev.ev_melibar_b.choice_3_result: You pay the seller for her parcel of pearls. She opens the wrapping under her brother's lamp so you can inspect them, then seals it again for travel. The sailor points out the safest way to carry the parcel through the crowded quay, and you feel more confident about the next stage.
ev.ev_melibar_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You spend the day while the pilot checks the boat's cargo. Between visits to the quay he points out the passage between Coilum and Melibar and makes you trace its first coastal turn on his board. At dusk he returns the board to the woman so her nephew can use the bench for supper.
ev.ev_melibar_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You pay the trader for his full sack of pepper. He and the nephew check its mark together, then lay it on the dry mat until you are ready to carry it. The woman calls them in for water before the trader returns to the quay.
ev.ev_melibar_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day helping the woman set out water and clear a path to the prayer room for guests who use it. Her nephew learns to keep the benches out of the way, and by evening everyone has a seat. The sailors thank you in front of the neighbouring port families.
ev.ev_melibar_entry.choice_1_result: The grower's son points you past the water stall toward the road through Melibar. His mother calls him back to cover the pepper sample before rain reaches it. You continue with the harbour's turns clear in mind.
ev.ev_melibar_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day among the pepper sellers. The cook returns with his captain, who smells the sample and waits while the grower weighs her cargo. Her son introduces you to the buyers and the water stall. By evening you know the market and its roads.
ev.ev_melibar_entry.choice_3_result: You leave your shoes at the shrine and make room for a family bringing offerings. The attendant shows you where to stand and later points out the lane back to the market. The pepper grower recognizes you on your return and thanks you for treating the gathering with care.
ev.ev_melibar_entry.choice_4_result: A family at the harbour lodging house is making room for late arrivals. Their daughter carries a folded mat inside and says the last boat has brought more guests than they expected. She asks you to come in and help them decide where everyone can sleep.
ev.ev_merva_entry.choice_1_result: The neighbour shows you which wells are still kept clear. You thank Hamid’s sister for the directions and mark Merv on your map before taking the road.
ev.ev_merva_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day, eat with the household and sleep beneath the newly patched roof. Hamid and the neighbour clear the narrow channel in the morning. By the time you leave, you feel rested and know which wells to follow.
ev.ev_merva_site_gap.choice_1_result: The boy names the wells and stopping places his father uses toward Sapurgan. Nuri checks two names with him, then lets you copy them. You mark the route while the letter finishes drying.
ev.ev_merva_site_gap.choice_2_result: Nuri grinds ink for you. You let the line dry before touching the page; her cousin copies your careful hand on the back of his draft. You learn how their paper is prepared, and he finally corrects the story of the melon rind.
ev.ev_mien_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Mien on your map.
ev.ev_mien_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Mien opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_moscovia_entry.choice_1_result: Darya shows you the way into town. You mark Moscow on your map and continue.
ev.ev_moscovia_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day in a room above the landing and regain your strength. Darya’s son draws the river bend for you, and you add Moscow to your map.
ev.ev_nanghin_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through Nanghin without stopping and mark the city on your map.
ev.ev_nanghin_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day in Nanghin's cloth market, record the traders' advice in your travel book, and mark the city on your map.
ev.ev_nicaea_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Eleni and continue beside the lake. Leon runs after you to show the firmest part of the shore path. You mark Nicaea and the lake on your map before the road turns away.
ev.ev_nicaea_entry.choice_2_result: You stay with Eleni's family for the day. Leon helps hang the blanket and then spends the afternoon telling you what he has seen from the shore. At supper Eleni finds the old peg he once lost, washed back among the reeds months later. Leon keeps it in a box now. They give you a place to sleep; you depart the next morning rested and mark Nicaea on your map.
ev.ev_ninive_entry.choice_1_result: The girl makes room for you on the path. You mark Mosul and Nineveh on your map before joining the other travellers.
ev.ev_ninive_entry.choice_2_result: You rest a full day in the shade above the landing. By morning you feel stronger. The father shows you where to mark the town and its opposite bank on your map.
ev.ev_novogardia_entry.choice_1_result: Anfisa’s father makes room between the wax bundles. You mark Novgorod on your map and go on.
ev.ev_novogardia_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day near the river and regain your strength. Anfisa’s daughter draws the landing for you on a scrap of bark; you use it to mark Novgorod on your map.
ev.ev_ormus_a.choice_1_result: You pay 3 silver and the clerk registers the pearl basket separately from the cargo you cleared on arrival. The pearl sorter’s son shows you the dry side of the yard, and his mother introduces you to the people working there. You record what you learned; the clerk asks you back to see the harbour ledger.
ev.ev_ormus_a.choice_2_result: The pearl sorter tells you which boats cross toward Calatu and who can name the divers’ working grounds. You mark Calatu on your map and note the route she described.
ev.ev_ormus_a.choice_3_result: You spend the day with the watchman, learning which boats enter at different tides. Below, the boy finally finishes counting the shells. You write down what the harbour workers taught you and keep a reminder of the wall.
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.body:
The customs clerk has moved his ledger away from the spray. The pearl sorter’s son is helping him copy the shell count onto a dry page, sounding out every number before he writes. His mother checks the baskets below the watch wall and calls back when he skips a line. The clerk slides the book toward you so you can see how cargo marks and boat names fit together.

‘Do you put every traveller in here?’ you ask. ‘Only when I can read the name tomorrow,’ he says. The boy laughs because his own first attempt is still blotched. The pearl sorter comes up the steps and asks whether the clerk has entered the boat bound across toward Calatu. She knows its pilot and the working water beyond the harbour.

The watchman calls a new ship from the wall. The clerk gives his pen to the boy, who has to finish the shell line without losing his place. You can ask to be entered in the harbour book, hear the pearl sorter describe Calatu, or spend the day watching the arriving boats with the watchman.
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_1: Ask to enter your name in the harbour ledger
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_1_result: The clerk writes your name beside the cargo mark and asks the boy to read it back. The pearl sorter recognises you from the working yard; people at the harbour know whom to ask about your goods. You keep a reminder of this place.
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the pearl sorter where Calatu lies
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_2_result: She points across the water and names Calatu, then tells you which pilot has recently made the crossing. You mark the port on your map and record the pearl workers’ account.
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day with the harbour watchman
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.choice_3_result: You stay the day with the watchman, matching each arriving boat to its entry in the dry ledger. Below, the boy learns to write the counts without the clerk’s help. You record what the port taught you.
ev.ev_ormus_a_followup.title: The Clerk’s Dry Ledger
ev.ev_ormus_astrodice_tide.choice_1_resu: You cast the three dice beside the pilot. His niece reads the figures, then asks what you will check before sailing. You give your answer and finish the reading together.
ev.ev_ormus_astrodice_tide.choice_2_resu: You ask the captain about the tide instead. He checks the waterline, calls his crew to secure the cargo, and tells you the boat can leave when they finish. You mark this departure in your notes.
ev.ev_ormus_b.choice_1_result: You pay 150 silver for the full pepper lot. The trader and porter check the ship and buyer names on its tag, then carry it into your share of the warehouse. The trader invites you to see the deeper storage rooms later.
ev.ev_ormus_b.choice_2_result: You pay 3 silver for the small ginger portion and eat it while it is warm. The trader’s wife pours you water, and the boy brings her the corrected tags. You feel ready to continue and remember the busy spice stall.
ev.ev_ormus_b.choice_3_result: The porter names the boats toward Calatu and the caravan yards used for Cobinan. You mark both places on your map and write down how pepper changes hands at the warehouse.
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.body:
The spice trader’s son has redone the labels in the inner warehouse. His father asks him to read the buyer’s name on a new pepper sack; he gets it right, then notices the ship name is missing. The porter returns with the boat record and waits while they add it. ‘Now I know where this sack came from and where it goes,’ the boy says.

The trader’s wife checks a second group of sacks. This full pepper lot is available for 108 silver, and she wants every seam checked before the new buyer takes it. You ask why the price differs from the first lot. She shows you a page with the cost of storing it and the time at which this ship arrived. The figures, not a promise about tomorrow’s price, explain her offer.

The porter also knows an inland caravan road toward Cobinan. The boy has been learning to keep the labels facing out so each sack can be checked; he offers you a place at the table if you want to spend a day watching the warehouse work.
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the full pepper lot for 108 silver
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 108 silver for the full pepper lot. The trader’s wife checks the seams one last time and the boy reads the new label aloud. You keep the cargo and a reminder of the spice warehouse.
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the porter to show the Cobinan caravan road
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_2_result: The porter walks you to the yard where caravans set out toward Cobinan and names the water stops he uses. You can now take that inland route; you record his directions with the warehouse notes.
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and learn their warehouse routine
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day checking labels, seams, and storage spaces with the family. By evening the boy has written every ship name in the right place, and his mother lets him close the ledger. You keep a reminder of the visit.
ev.ev_ormus_b_followup.title: The Second Pepper Sacks
ev.ev_ormus_c.choice_1_result: You pay 1.5 silver and spend two days with the guide. He has you compare the sky with the water at the landing and asks the dates seller’s sister what she sees before opening the shutters. You record the signs and agree to meet him again.
ev.ev_ormus_c.choice_2_result: You wait three days with the family. The boy carries the small jar to the lower room each morning; when the wind settles, his mother lets him take it back up. You are better prepared for the next stretch of travel.
ev.ev_ormus_c.choice_3_result: You watch the neighbours tie cloth, close shutters, and move water out of the heat. The seller shows you where the first gust slipped under his awning; you record their habits and remember the day the port lane went quiet.
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.body:
After two days with the guide, you find him comparing yesterday’s sky with a fresh line of clouds. The dates seller’s sister brings a jar of water up from the cooler room and asks whether she can open her shutters now. He does not answer immediately; he looks at the cloth on the roof and asks her whether its loose end still moves.

‘A little,’ she says. Her son wants to run outside, but she gives him the job of holding the jar while she checks the lane. You ask what the guide watches first on a day like this. He shows you where the dust hangs low, then points inland toward the road to Kerman. The seller has heard that caravans are moving there and asks when they plan to leave.

The guide sets his notes between you and the family. He can show you the signs he uses, walk you to the inland caravan yard, or let you spend another day in the cool room until the wind truly eases.
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_1: Learn the guide’s signs of hot wind
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_1_result: The guide shows you the dust line and the way the roof cloth moves before a stronger gust. The seller’s son repeats the signs back to him; you record the lesson and remember this windy day.
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_2: Ask for the inland road toward Kerman
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_2_result: The guide takes you to the caravan yard and points out the road toward Kerman, including where travellers can refill water. You can use that inland route now and record his directions.
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_3: Stay another day until the wind eases
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.choice_3_result: You spend another day with the family in the cool lower room. The boy brings the small water jar down himself; when the wind settles, he carries it up again. You are better prepared for the next leg.
ev.ev_ormus_c_followup.title: The Guide’s Weather Notes
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.body:
The pearl sorter finds you after the customs work is done. Her son is carrying a basket of counted shells and keeps asking whether the pilot has a space on his next crossing. She says the diver who owns the basket is her cousin; the family needs the shells moved before the next market opens. ‘I know a pilot who may take them,’ she tells you, ‘but I cannot promise his boat is free.’

You ask why she has come to you. She says the clerk saw you help match the cargo marks, and she wants someone who will copy the boat name correctly when the pilot answers. Her son puts down the basket and reads the name from a damp scrap. The first letter has run. His mother asks him to tell it from memory; he can, but insists the pilot may spell it differently.

She writes down two pilots who know that boat and hands you the paper. The son waits to see whether you will take it. His mother reminds him to keep the shells in the shade until they have a confirmed place.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the pilots’ names and ask about the boat
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.choice_1_resul: You take the paper and ask at the pilots’ bench. One man recognises the boat name but wants to inspect the shell basket before agreeing. The sorter’s son returns to fetch it, and you follow him toward the shade.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank her and let the family ask the pilot
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.choice_2_resul: You thank her and return the paper. She folds it into her son’s hand and says they will speak to the pilot together. He takes the basket carefully, already practising the boat name aloud.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a.title: The Pearl Sorter’s Boat Name
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a_resolution.bod:
The pilot inspects the shell basket and asks the boy to show its mark. The boy reads the boat name from memory, then points to the clean label his mother wrote. ‘Good,’ the pilot says. ‘Now tell me who will receive it on the other side.’ The sorter names her cousin’s brother and the stall where he works.

A porter calls that the boat already has two water jars near the stern. The pilot checks the space between them and says the basket can travel there if it is tied down. You ask whether he will put the arrangement in writing. He nods and asks for the customs clerk’s copy so the recipient will know which cargo arrived. The boy runs to fetch it.

His mother keeps hold of the basket until the paper comes back. If you have time, she would also like you to spend a day learning how her family sorts and records the shells; the pilot is ready to confirm the boat now.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a_resolution.cho: Confirm the basket’s place on the boat
You and the pilot check the label and receipt together. The basket is tied between the water jars; the boy tells his mother he will remember where it went. You keep a copy of the arrangement.
Stay a day to learn how the family sorts shells

You spend the day at their shaded table. The boy teaches you the marks he uses for each basket, and his mother makes him check the last count before supper. By then the boat and recipient are both written down.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_a_resolution.tit: A Place for the Shell Basket
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.body:
The pilot’s mate comes to the landing with a damp piece of sailcloth. He and his sister have been marking a reef on it, but each drew the shape from a different tide. ‘If we leave both lines, the new crew will think there are two reefs,’ she says. He says the outer line was what he saw at low water.

You ask which mark a boat should follow now. The sister calls over an older helmsman who passed the channel this morning. He points to the deeper side and tells the mate where the current pushed him. The mate redraws the line while she holds the cloth flat. He asks whether you can copy it onto dry paper; the sailcloth is already fading at the edges.

The young sailor from the landing brings his mother’s empty bowl back. His mother asks whether their own boat will pass that reef today. The mate checks the wind before answering, then holds out the new drawing for you to inspect.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.choice_1: Help copy the reef and tide marks
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.choice_1_resul: You copy the deeper channel and the tide at which the reef shows. The sister checks your page against the helmsman’s account, and the mate asks you to keep it until they make another copy.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.choice_2: Thank them and ask again nearer departure
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.choice_2_resul: You thank them and leave the cloth on the pilots’ bench. The mate says to return when your captain fixes a departure time; his sister folds the paper away from the damp sailcloth.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b.title: The Pilot’s Mate and the Reef
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b_resolution.bod:
The mate’s sister has made two clean copies of the channel drawing. She puts one on the pilots’ bench and asks the young sailor to carry the other to his captain. He stops at the reef mark. ‘Is this the place we passed yesterday?’ she asks. He says yes but cannot remember the tide.

The older helmsman arrives and names the hour from his log. You add it beside the line. The mate asks whether anyone has checked the reef since the wind changed; the helmsman says a small fishing boat came through at dawn and can be asked. The sailor’s mother arrives to collect her bowl and reminds him to eat before he runs off with the chart.

The mate can let you carry the warning to crews waiting at the harbour. His sister is staying a day to compare the paper with the next boat’s report and offers you a place at the bench if you want to help. She sets the two copies beneath a bowl so the wind will not lift them.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b_resolution.cho: Carry the channel warning to the waiting crews

You take the dated drawing to the waiting crews. A captain compares it with his own marks and thanks you for naming the tide; the young sailor finally sits down to eat. You keep a copy for the next crossing.
Stay a day and compare the next boat’s report
You stay a day at the pilots’ bench. The small fishing boat’s crew confirms where the reef appeared at dawn, and the mate’s sister corrects one line on both copies before they are sent out.
ev.ev_ormus_consequence_b_resolution.tit: The Dry Copy of the Channel
ev.ev_ormus_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days helping the customs clerk match marks to bundles. The trader’s daughter shows you which cargo is bound inland, and you mark Hormuz on your map. A pearl sorter comes to ask about the newly cleared shipment.
ev.ev_ormus_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day with the pilot and sailor, writing down how they watch the tide and pack water for a crossing. The sailor’s mother brings a second bowl of food; as you finish your notes, the pilot’s mate arrives with news of the wind.
ev.ev_ormus_entry.choice_3_result: You spend the day checking the full Damascus steel lot and pay 146 silver. The trader’s daughter writes you a clean tally and has the porter move the goods inland. You record the trade and what you saw at the landing.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_astrodice.choice_1_re: You pay 70 silver and spend seven days learning how the pilot names and reads the three dice. His niece makes you put them away in the same order every evening; her father asks about the tide before every exercise. When you finish, he promises one last meeting at the landing.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_astrodice.choice_2_re: The pilot lets you examine the marks on the dice while his niece reads them aloud. He explains how he frames a question, then turns to check the boat’s actual water and wind. You write down the method.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.body:
At the landing, the pilot is packing the three dice into a leather cup. His niece has been making copies of the tide notes from your seven days of lessons. She asks why the page for the third day has no wind mark. The pilot remembers that the boat stayed tied up then because a rope had frayed; he has her write that beside the empty space.

You ask whether the dice told him to wait. ‘The rope did,’ he says, showing the old fibres. His niece asks him to cast once more for your journey, and he agrees after the crew’s water jars are counted. A sailor from across the strait has arrived with news of Calatu and is willing to describe the passage.

The pilot leaves the cup on the table while he checks the jars. His niece offers you a seat by the tide notes; she would like a full day to compare the three dice with the observations she copied.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_1: Accept one last reading with the pilot
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_1_res: The pilot casts the dice after the jars are counted. His niece copies the figures and the question you asked, then gives you the page as a parting gift. You record what he taught you at Hormuz.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask the sailor how to sail toward Calatu
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_2_res: The sailor walks you along the quay, names the crossing toward Calatu, and shows which pilot is taking a boat that way. You can use that sea route now; you record his directions with the tide notes.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and compare the dice with tide notes
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.choice_3_res: You spend the day with the niece, matching each question to what the crew actually observed. The pilot returns with a corrected water count, and she adds it to the page. You leave more confident in planning the next passage.
ev.ev_ormus_mentor_followup.title: The Pilot’s Three Dice
ev.ev_paukin_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Paukin opens on your map.
ev.ev_paukin_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Paukin on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_pein_entry.choice_1_result: The old woman points out the wells used by travellers leaving Pein. You thank the family, mark the town on your map and continue with the caravan.
ev.ev_pein_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day and watch the family sort stones, sell cotton and settle their count before sunset. The daughter explains which marks on a bundle tell her who packed it. You add Pein and what you learned to your travel book.
ev.ev_pein_site_gap.choice_1_result: Rustam names the wells used on the route to Yarcan. His daughter corrects the order of two stopping places she visited last month, and he lets her draw them on your map.
ev.ev_pein_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the dish while Rustam’s wife shows the buyer the grit left in each cup. The family closes the sale with everyone clear about the measure. You remember the simple test they used at Pein.
ev.ev_pentam_entry.choice_1_result: The girl finishes marking the new jar while her grandfather takes the empty one back to the well. She tells you which lane reaches the far side of town. You pass the boatyard and learn how the landing connects to the streets inland.
ev.ev_pentam_entry.choice_2_result: You stay another day. The girl checks each receipt as the jars come down from the well; the sailor returns with his mate and collects the water at the promised time. Her grandfather introduces you to the pilot, who shows you where the deep water gives way to a shoal.
ev.ev_petra_entry.choice_1_result: You drink and thank Rashida. Sami points out the well-trodden path beyond the gorge, then carefully moves his pebble to the other side. You walk between the rock walls and mark Petra on your map.
ev.ev_petra_entry.choice_2_result:
You spend the day in the shelter and help Sami hang the empty waterskins to dry. At dusk his father comes back with the goats. He gives Rashida a small bag of flour, then drinks from the skin she saved for him. “I was thinking about this water all the way back,” he says. Sami moves a pebble across to count his father's share.

They make hot soup and ask you to eat with them. You sleep in the shade of the rock and leave the next morning, your legs rested. You mark Petra on your map.
ev.ev_road_00.choice_1_result: Your party follows the girl's sketch. A cart sinks at the washed-out bend, and its driver asks you to keep the animals back while they lift the wheel. After two extra days, at the far well, the keeper lays the sketch beside his own worn map. “The stone needs to stand here,” he says, tapping the shared turning. He sends his nephew back to show both camps. You leave the sketch with him and continue your journey, after the driver discovers that the wheel hub cracked in the rut. It must be bound for the next stretch; the driver gives up his spare leather to hold it together, and the animals flinch at every deep track.
ev.ev_road_00.choice_2_result: The guide takes your payment and leads the circuit. At the first well his aunt asks why the usual road is empty. “They moved the stone after the rain,” he tells her. “Then tell the keeper before another wheel breaks,” she says, filling your skins. After four extra days, a rider brings word that both camps have met at the marker. The guide shows you their agreed line on his map before your party moves on.
ev.ev_road_01.choice_1_result: You pay the boat fare and carry the clerk's letters down the steep path with your baggage. The keeper's mother makes several trips with the people and letters. Meanwhile he repairs the heavy landing, rolls the carts onto the larger ferry one at a time, and leads the animals aboard separately. After two extra days of crossings and waiting, the clerk reaches the far bank, checks every seal and laughs at the mud on his boots. “I owe your mother a better sign,” he tells the keeper. She makes him draw the landing on the back of his spare paper; you travel on after seeing him nail it beside the road.
ev.ev_road_01.choice_2_result: You pay a fee and join the keeper's escorted carts. At each guarded landing the keeper gives the clerk a receipt for the letters and explains which boat will carry them next. After three extra days, the clerk arrives at the river office with his bag dry. “Will the road sign point to your mother now?” he asks. “After you hand over those letters,” the keeper answers. The office clerk recognizes the receipt and thanks your party for bringing the packet through.
ev.ev_road_02.choice_1_result: The nephew leads you between the channels, then stops where your baggage has brushed a branch. “Move the pack to the other side, or the next cart will do worse,” he says. Your party helps him set a sign on the proper road. After two extra days you reach the junction beyond the boundary wall. A passing farmer sees the sign and turns away from the irrigation gate. The nephew grins: “Tell my uncle that the water stayed in the orchard.” The people using the public road thank you for the new marker.
ev.ev_road_02.choice_2_result: The escort collects a fee and leads you onto the longer public road. Your escort points out a spring where the animals can drink and warns the next cart away from the orchard gate.
