After four extra days, the nephew reaches the same junction with an empty market basket. “The apricots sold,” he says. “Did anyone drive through our channels?” The escort tells him about the warning. He gives you the last fruit and starts home before the light goes.
ev.ev_road_03.choice_1_result: You take the short channel. The pilot calls out the depth while the cook shifts the sound jars away from the rail. During the second extra day the hull brushes sand. “Back water, slowly,” the pilot tells the rowers, and the boat floats free. You reach the inlet after two extra days, though the cook finds a second jar cracked by the jolt. “Fill the sound ones first,” she says. The boatbuilder's spare oar gets you to the jetty, where a local repairer takes the broken jar.
ev.ev_road_03.choice_2_result: You pay a fee and follow the sheltered harbours. At the first stop a local repairer fits a firmer oar; at the next, the cook trades her leaking jar. “We have water enough to share now,” she says to a fisherman waiting by the quay. After four extra days you reach the inlet with the jars full. The pilot points out the quiet channel you used on the chart, and the cook asks him to show it to the next crew.
ev.ev_road_04.choice_1_result: You wait while the grandson leads the riders along the streambed, then follow. Rain softens the far bank; you help a driver pull his cart onto firmer soil. After two extra days you reach the next station. A rider from the first station catches up with news. “The boy found the horse with the eastern herd,” she says. “His grandfather has fixed the streambed marker.” She hands a traveller a red strip to tie at the next turning. The rider thanks your party for leaving the searchers room to work.
ev.ev_road_04.choice_2_result: After taking a fee, the guide leads you through the grazing ground. He asks each well keeper whether a white-legged horse has passed. “A boy came asking yesterday,” one woman says. “He has his grandfather's eye.” After four extra days a rider brings news to your last stop: the horse was found with the eastern herd. The guide reads the message to the people at the stop, who have been asking after the animal at every well.
ev.ev_road_05.choice_1_result: You pull on the fastening with the pilgrim while her father watches the iron. It holds. At a wet step he asks everyone to pass the water jars one at a time. After two extra days your party reaches the halt above the hill. The pilgrim adds the narrow resting place to her drawing. “People will need that more than another chain,” she says. You leave with her directions to the next safe set of steps, and her father thanks you for testing the handhold.
ev.ev_road_05.choice_2_result: You pay a fee and let the porters take the gentler road. At each rest stop they put your baggage down so the animals can drink. After five extra days the pilgrim and her father catch up near the next halt. She shows you the old iron link wrapped in cloth. “This wore thinner than it looked,” she says. “The water carriers used the new one all morning.” One porter asks to see it, then checks the strap he uses on the steepest part of his road.
ev.ev_road_06.choice_1_result: The courier checks the girth of your hired horse while his sister counts the payment. You ride out beside him. His sister checks the knot on his satchel and asks you to keep pace at the first bend. After the extra day, at the river office, the clerk breaks the seal and checks the names against his register. “All here,” he says, and gives the courier a signed receipt. The courier asks whether the saddle rubbed your leg, then checks its strap before his ride back.
ev.ev_road_06.choice_2_result: You take the potter's bowls down the ordinary road. After the two extra days, at the next halt, a cook pours hot water into one and listens for a crack. “Good. I can use these tonight,” she says. She pays for the batch. You keep the fee the potter promised from the proceeds and send him the rest. You send her marked order slip back to the potter with a returning driver. He later has the cook's name for his next delivery, and people at the halt know you kept his bowls whole.
ev.ev_road_07.choice_1_result: You pay a fee and leave with the mounted caravan. At its first halt the sailor checks the horses' girths once more. “Easy with them on the next climb,” he tells the leader. The leader gives him time to tighten a loose strap before the group rides on. The trip adds two days before you rejoin your route. A rider returning to the coast carries your note that the inland road was clear; the sailor can use that news when he sends the horses.
ev.ev_road_07.choice_2_result: You take three extra days to carry the tack to the inland stable. Its keeper tests a strap on a patient horse. “He kept the old measure,” she says, pointing to the sailor's knot. She pays the sailor’s price; you keep your agreed share from it and send the balance back. You tell her the sea horses were drinking well when you left. She hangs the straps near their stalls and asks a boy to keep a trough ready for their arrival.
ev.ev_road_08.choice_1_result: The caravan driver takes a fee and makes room for your baggage. The potter's father shows the driver how to wedge the crate before the carts depart. At the next stop a fresh team is ready, and you reach a town after the extra day's travel. The driver sets your bag down and asks whether the cups beside it survived. You hear no rattle when he lifts the crate. He smiles: “Tell her father the straw held.”
ev.ev_road_08.choice_2_result: You carry one wrapped crate along the ordinary road over two extra days. The tea seller opens it cup by cup; one has a chipped lip, and she sets it aside before paying for the rest. “Your potter will want to know which one broke,” she says, marking the order slip. She pays for the sound cups; you keep the fee the potter promised from the proceeds and send the balance back with her marked order slip. She serves tea in the new cups that evening. Her careful count helps you spot the same loose corner in your own baggage before the next stage.
ev.ev_road_09.choice_1_result: You pay a fee and leave with the merchant train. Before the merchant cart rolls, the dyer's daughter trims the paired bolts to equal lengths and shows the buyer both edges. “Now they will hang evenly,” she says. Your train changes animals at a prepared stop and reaches the exchange point after two extra days. A woman there asks where the neat white cloth came from; you give her the dyer's name and hear her send a messenger back to the market.
ev.ev_road_09.choice_2_result: You take the cloth with your party on a detour that adds three days. At the next market a family preparing a wedding examines the weave. “We will use this for the tent,” a woman says, “but who dyed it?” You give the dyer's name and show her daughter's measurements on the slip. The family pays for the cloth. You keep the agreed share of the price, and a driver carries the rest back with the signed slip. By evening the first length is already cut, and the family asks you to bring another bolt if you return.
ev.ev_road_10.choice_1_result: The guard counts your payment and waves you into the departing caravan. As the carts pull away, the apprentice calls out the missing pearl's number; it was caught in the tablecloth. “Put it in the box before you count again,” the seller tells him. At the next market after the extra day, the guard helps unload your baggage and checks the seal on your baggage. The apprentice arrives later with the closed pearl box and waves when he sees you by the gate.
ev.ev_road_10.choice_2_result: You bring the shell beads to the workshop after two extra days. A maker compares them with an unfinished necklace. “These will fill the gap,” she says, and writes a receipt for the seller. You keep the agreed share of the price and send the rest back with a returning trader. While you wait, she threads a few beads onto dark cord and asks which colour holds the eye. You choose one; she sets it on her workbench to try in the next necklace.
ev.ev_road_11.choice_1_result: You pay a fee and ride with the couriers. The boy watches his mother check each seal, then calls out the next station's name as your horses leave. After two extra days you reach a station on your route, with the packets still dry. A courier signs for each one. “The boy will want to know how far we came,” your rider says. You write the two station names on the back of a scrap and give it to the returning courier for him.
ev.ev_road_11.choice_2_result: You carry the harness bundle over three extra days. At the next camp a driver tests its leather loops on his cart and buys them. “That knot is the trader's,” he says, recognizing the label the boy tied. You keep your agreed share and send the rest back with a rider. In the evening the driver shows you a quieter track to the next well. He says the trader once gave him the same directions when his wheel broke, and you set out on it with a clearer idea of the road.
ev.ev_road_12.choice_1_result: The courier accepts a fee and gives you a place with the group. The assistant checks her copy against the original before she seals it. “Read the page number back to me,” she asks; the clerk does, and she hands over the packet. After the extra day the receiving office signs for it beside your baggage. The courier shows you the receipt before he returns, and you see the clerk's assistant has written the correct page number on the outside.
ev.ev_road_12.choice_2_result: You carry the paper to the school over two extra days. The teacher measures a sheet against a child's copybook. “This will do,” she says, paying the assistant's price. You keep the agreed share and send the balance with the signed order slip back by messenger. A student who has been waiting for paper starts a map of the nearby road and asks where you crossed the river. You show her on the page, and she adds the ferry to the route.
ev.ev_road_13.choice_1_result: You pay the fare and climb aboard with the sailor. He waits until the tide lifts the boat clear of a shallow ridge, then has you look for the darker strip of water beside it. “Follow that at the next inlet,” he says. After this extra day afloat, you put in at a port on the way. A buyer asks whether the fisherwoman's baskets came aboard. “Her son is still drying them,” the sailor says. “They will come on a later boat.” He marks the safe channel on your chart before you leave.
ev.ev_road_13.choice_2_result: You stay by the drying racks for two extra days. The fisherwoman shows you how to turn each fish without breaking it, and her son packs the finished bundles under a dry mat. A buyer from the next market comes to collect them. “Tell your mother these stayed dry,” he says to the boy, lifting the first basket. When another family asks where to bring its catch, the fisherwoman sends them to you for the rack's empty space. Your help has become known along this stretch of coast.
ev.ev_road_14.choice_1_result: You add two days to the journey with the keeper, asking each station what water was available to its last carts. At the second halt a stable boy shows her the covered well behind the wall. “My father moved the trough after the drought,” he explains. The keeper crosses out the old mark and adds the new one. At the second halt, drivers read the corrected sheet aloud to one another. She writes your name beside the change and thanks you for checking it with her.
ev.ev_road_14.choice_2_result: You pay the caravan fare and join the drivers who know the current wells. Their lead cart stops at the covered trough beyond the bend. “This is the one missing from the old sheet,” a driver tells you. The detour adds a day. You water your animals at the halt, then return to your planned road. The driver promises to pass the well's location back when his next cart returns.
ev.ev_road_15.choice_1_result: You ask the elder which bank the repaired bridge meets, then have the courier read his new line back to her. She corrects one character in the place name. “There. Now a driver can ask for it,” she says. The courier seals the report and thanks you in front of the station keeper, who remembers your careful help when your party comes through again.
ev.ev_road_15.choice_2_result: You take an extra day to walk with the elder. At the bridge she points to a newer set of boards laid across the old stone piers. “Carts use the southern bank after rain,” she says, showing you the marks left by their wheels. You return to the station by the firm path and describe it to the courier. He adds the bank to his report; you can use the route yourself on the next crossing.
ev.ev_road_16.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day with both families, walking the route from the hollow to the well before anyone moves the stone. The woman brings a skin of water and asks her brother to set the marker where a rider can see it from either approach. They try it once more with the animals. “Now I can send the lambs ahead,” she says. The families thank you for staying until both sides agree on the turn.
ev.ev_road_16.choice_2_result: You follow the son along the older stones for an extra day. He finds a watercourse hidden behind reeds and tests its depth with a staff. “This will take the smaller herd,” he says, calling to his aunt. You walk back by the line of stones and show the families where the channel rejoins the well path. The boy scratches its turning into the dirt for you, so you can recognize it on another journey.
ev.ev_road_17.choice_1_result: You lay out the saddles beside the keeper's list while the stable boy checks the storeroom. He finds the new strap looped around a pack frame, where he put it to keep it clean. “That was my doing,” he admits. The saddler fits it to the right saddle; the keeper corrects his count and tells the camp steward who helped settle the mix-up. By the time your party leaves, the horses are ready and your name is known at the gate.
ev.ev_road_17.choice_2_result: You take an extra day to carry the finished bundle to the next post. A groom there compares each buckle with the order and signs the saddler's delivery slip. “The bay mare has been waiting for this,” she says, setting aside the right strap. You send the slip back with a returning rider. The saddler has already given you the agreed wage for the journey; the groom pays only for the tack she ordered.
ev.ev_road_18.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day comparing the old token with the clerk's register. He restores the full family name and measures out the grain. At the house, the mother counts the sacks while her youngest child holds the door. “Next time, ask for us by this name,” she says, pointing to the corrected slip. The clerk posts the change at the granary, and neighbours who saw you help call you over when your party returns to that street.
ev.ev_road_18.choice_2_result: You ride with the grain cart for an extra day. Its driver knows which street can take a loaded wagon and which has a broken drain. At each stop he lets the households check their own sacks. Before departure, the clerk fills out the mother's name from the old token. She finds her family's allotment on the cart and shows the driver the completed slip. Before you leave town, he draws the passable streets on the back of a scrap for you. Your party can use that route with its own loads.
ev.ev_road_19.choice_1_result: You ask the merchant to say his sister's town name slowly while the clerk reads two entries from the register. They settle on the river branch and the eastern gate, then write both names on the envelope. “Now the next clerk can find it,” the merchant says. The station keeper thanks you for resolving the address before the mail leaves and recognizes you when you bring another letter later.
ev.ev_road_19.choice_2_result: You take an extra day to carry the letter to the next post. The clerk there reads the merchant's name for the town, then checks the river branch on your map. “The eastern gate is ours,” she says, and stamps the letter for delivery. You send that receipt back by a returning rider. The merchant paid your agreed wage before you set out; his sister will receive the letter through the ordinary post.
ev.ev_road_20.choice_1_result: You hold the falcon's perch steady while the falconer replaces the thin strap. The apprentice counts each knot as his teacher ties it, then checks where the leather touches the bird's leg. “This one is smooth,” he says. The falconer lets the bird settle before returning it to the glove. A road guard who watched the repair asks where the group will camp; the falconer points out your help, and the guard knows your party when you pass.
ev.ev_road_20.choice_2_result: You spend two extra days following the apprentice around the marsh. He leads you from one dry rise to another, showing where a wooden pole remains visible after rain. At the second pole he pauses to let the falconers' birds rest. “That notch means the ground stays firm,” he tells you. When you reach the next station, you can show your driver the same marks. He keeps the loaded cart on the higher path and thanks the boy for sharing it.
ev.ev_road_21.choice_1_result: You and the porter use the first extra day to reach the previous station. Its keeper finds the tag folded inside a receipt book; the driver left it there while counting loads. On the second extra day you return with the keeper's mark beside it. “That is the bale,” the steward says, releasing the seal. The daughter runs to fetch her father, who thanks both witnesses before he harnesses the cart. The steward tells the next caravan why he trusts your word.
ev.ev_road_21.choice_2_result: You pay the guide and leave with the departing party. He chooses a firm track past the low ground and takes the one-day detour with you before you rejoin your road. At its fire a rider from the old station reports that the tag was found in a receipt book and the driver released. You ask her to tell the daughter you heard the news. She nods and turns back with the guide's note on the safe track.
ev.ev_road_22.choice_1_result: You read each parcel name while the niece sets it beside the right saddle. She finds her mother's letter inside a cloth bundle that was meant for another town. “This one travels back,” she says, tying it where the return courier can see it. Her uncle signs the list and thanks you in front of the lodging keeper. Later, when your party needs a place to rest, the keeper remembers how you helped the family set out.
ev.ev_road_22.choice_2_result: You add a day to your journey with the merchants, keeping their packet away from the damp side of the pack. At the next lodging house the niece checks the seal before she hands it to its buyer. “And my mother's letter?” she asks her uncle. He shows her the return courier's receipt. The merchants pay your agreed delivery wage. She adds your name to her travel list so she can remember who helped on her first stage.
ev.ev_road_23.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day following the boy through the dry grass. The channel appears where a fallen branch holds back the bank. You clear a little silt with your hands and watch water run toward a lower trough. “The smaller horses can drink here,” he says. His aunt brings them over one at a time. Before you leave, the boy shows you a crooked willow that marks the channel from the main track; you add it to your own route notes.
ev.ev_road_23.choice_2_result: The water carrier spreads the camp's well list on the boy's aunt's table. You check her marks with her, then make a copy for the caravan leader. He checks the last well against the mark on his own water skin, pays the agreed copying wage and leaves with the copy. The boy asks you to add the pool's low level in the margin. You do, so the leader can plan for the horses he has today. Your party then continues from the camp without losing the day.
ev.ev_road_24.choice_1_result: You hold one line while the aunt moves the posts far enough apart for both herds. The elder brother counts his horses again, and the younger leads his last gelding through the new gap. “The mare can still be found,” their aunt says, “but these ones can sleep.” Both brothers accept the arrangement and tell the next arrivals who helped them clear the camp. Your party has room to pass without waiting.
ev.ev_road_24.choice_2_result: You follow the younger brother for an extra day. The mare's hoofprints turn away from the crowded camp toward a strip of sheltered grass. “She always goes where the flies are fewer,” he says when he sees her. He ties a loose lead rope, then shows you the hollow's firm exit before you return to the main road. You remember that exit when your own animals need a sheltered place to rest.
ev.ev_road_25.choice_1_result: You ask the messenger to read the broken-handle line again. The borrower shows the new pin she fitted and agrees to send the bucket with tomorrow's water cart. The messenger writes that date on the reply and lets her check it. “My brother will stop worrying when he reads this,” he says. Both families know you helped them settle a small quarrel before it reached the well queue.
ev.ev_road_25.choice_2_result: You take an extra day to carry the reply. At the next camp the bucket's owner opens it beside you, reads the agreed return date and asks to see the repaired handle when it arrives. “I made this with my father,” he says. You tell him the new pin looked sound. The borrower paid your agreed wage before you left; the owner writes a short answer for the messenger to take back.
ev.ev_road_26.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day going from cart to cart with the horse keeper. One skin listed as full has a loose stopper; the leader replaces it before the water is divided again. The tired driver takes a smaller load, and a wagon with spare room carries the rest. “Now we know whose water is where,” the keeper says, marking the tally. The drivers thank you for staying until they can leave together.
ev.ev_road_26.choice_2_result: You spend two extra days with the young scout. Beyond the first bend, a bank that looked steep has a firm gap where the animals can descend. The scout tests it with an unloaded horse while you watch the far side. “This is wide enough for the carts,” he says. You mark the turn with a loose stone and rejoin the main road. Your party can recognize this crossing when the channel is dry again.
ev.ev_road_27.choice_1_result: You ask the elders to read their families' names back to the scribe. The last woman points to her carts beside the south fence. “Those are mine,” she says, and checks that the written name matches. The scribe hangs the complete list near the track. As the carts begin moving, the elders thank you for making sure no family was left waiting without a turn.
ev.ev_road_27.choice_2_result: You spend an extra day checking the water carrier's well list and copying it. The caravan head traces the route with a finger and asks which one still has a working trough. You mark it after asking the camp's water carrier, who filled there yesterday. The caravan head pays the agreed copying wage and folds the copy into his saddlebag. The scribe uses the space beside you to finish the cart list before both groups leave.
ev.ev_road_28.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day with the drivers, pulling each bundle to the bank before the current reaches its seams. One carter tests the shallows with a pole while you set a visible marker above the firm ground. “Next wagon follows this line,” she says. Your own party crosses after the animals settle. The driver shows you the marker from the far bank, so you can find the ford again when water rises.
ev.ev_road_28.choice_2_result: You take the rescued bundles on pack animals lent by the merchant over two extra days. At the next station the merchant's partner checks each mark against his list. “The cloth stayed dry inside,” he says after opening the first wrap. The merchant pays you the wage he promised through his partner, who had it set aside with the receipt. You leave the signed list for the returning driver and continue on after returning the borrowed animals.
ev.ev_road_29.choice_1_result: You give a small offering for the meal. The cook buys enough grain to fill the last pot and invites the late travellers to sit down. After eating, the elder asks the congregation to pray for those still on the road, including your party. The child brings you a piece of bread for the morning. You leave with the blessing and a little food for the next stretch.
ev.ev_road_29.choice_2_result: You sit with the elder as the meal is prepared. She tells how the people in the old tale gathered after hearing the caliph's threat and chose whom to ask for help. The child interrupts twice to check which part was a prayer and which part happened at the council. You write both down as parts of the story the elder told, then read her version back to her before you go.
ev.ev_road_30.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day taking repaired shoes to the families who left them at the bench. The boy's sister tries hers on and walks a few steps across the room. “They fit again,” she tells the cobbler when you return. He writes each household's name beside the pair it received. Neighbours notice that you carried the shoes carefully and thank you when you pass their doors.
ev.ev_road_30.choice_2_result: You sit beside the cobbler while he finishes the sole. He tells the boy how the community in the old tale asked the one-eyed cobbler to pray, and how the story was passed down afterward. “That part is what people say,” he adds when the boy asks for proof. You record the tale as he told it. Then he points to the footpath behind the prayer house: its stones stand above the washed-out turn, and you can use it on your way.
ev.ev_road_32.choice_1_result: You help the carpenter carry planks from the dry shed and keep the carts in a firm strip beside the shelter. On the second extra day she wedges the last board into place. The driver with the old list walks across first, then waves his cart forward. “I will change the drawing before I give it to my son,” he says. The carpenter asks the waiting drivers to remember who stayed to help; they greet you again when your party moves on.
ev.ev_road_32.choice_2_result: You pay the guide’s fee. He walks ahead to test the ford, then waits while the ferry takes the heaviest bags across. The detour adds a day before you rejoin your road. At the next shelter, a returning cart brings word that the carpenter has begun laying the new boards. You tell its driver which part of the ford held firm, so he can pass that news to the travellers still waiting.
ev.ev_road_33.choice_1_result: You and the driver lower the mule’s top sacks before the keeper leads the mother elephant into the cut. The calf follows after the bell is wrapped in cloth. “Leave that space between them,” the keeper asks, and the drivers hold their animals back. One extra day passes before both strings are safely through. The keeper thanks you in front of the people who use this road; when your party returns, they make room for you without having to be asked.
ev.ev_road_33.choice_2_result: The guide takes you up the higher track over two extra days. At one bend he lets you choose between a tempting patch of smooth earth and a rougher strip by the roots. Your staff sinks into the smooth patch. “That is why we keep to the trees after rain,” he says. You reach the main road again with your shoes muddy and a useful route in mind. The elephant keeper’s group has already passed the cut below.
ev.ev_road_34.choice_1_result: You find the merchant at his cart and ask him to read the mark on his receipt. He remembers the apprentice’s blue cord on the chest. “She brought it in before the rain,” he tells the clerk. The clerk changes the name, then lets the apprentice check the line for herself. The old guard folds the receipt into his sleeve. The merchant thanks you in front of the caravan, and the people at the shelter remember who helped put the pay in the right hands.
ev.ev_road_34.choice_2_result: Before you leave, the clerk and the receiving merchant check the chest and correct the name together. You take the corrected copy to the merchant’s partner on a one-day detour. He compares the seal with his own account before accepting it. “Now I can pay her family when the next cart comes,” he says, and gives you the delivery wage they agreed. You send the signed receipt back with a returning driver. The apprentice’s name is written clearly on both copies when you rejoin your road.
ev.ev_road_35.choice_1_result: You follow the cousin along the edge of the dry stream. He finds a ring of stones under blown sand, then the shallow hole where the old marker stood. The herder touches the stone and calls her neighbour over. “This is where Mother brought us,” she says. He walks the line with her and agrees which side their animals can use. The search costs an extra day. Before you leave, the cousin points out the stream bend and the stone ring; they will help you recognize a grass boundary on another journey.
ev.ev_road_35.choice_2_result: You spend two extra days walking the grazing ground with both households. The neighbour counts his animals; the herder shows him where her youngest lambs can reach water without crossing his flock. Together you set small stones where the two feeding lines part. “Bring them through here in the morning,” she tells her cousin. When both flocks settle, the neighbour invites your party to share the evening fire. They tell the next travellers that you stayed until everyone had a place to graze.
ev.ev_road_36.choice_1_result: The youngest traveller lays out two letters while you untie the parcel tags and open the one addressed to their household. Her brother recognizes his coat by the patch sewn on the sleeve. “Aunt made that before we left,” he says. The other tag names the aunt’s village, so the courier puts her bundle back in his bag. The family receives its things at the lodging house. The innkeeper thanks you for keeping the cousins’ parcels straight and remembers your party when you need a room.
ev.ev_road_36.choice_2_result: You take the aunt’s parcel along the side road, adding a day to the journey. She is mending a door hinge when you arrive. “The blue cloth is mine,” she says, then reads the name under the string before taking it. She pays the agreed delivery wage and sends a short note back to her family with a returning cart. You rejoin the main road knowing the bundle reached the person who packed it.
ev.ev_road_37.choice_1_result: You count the sacks with the clerk and the driver, then compare the receipt with the earlier account. The seal is genuine; the changed number comes from a second cart that arrived the previous evening. The guards separate the two deliveries and let the waiting families take the grain assigned to them. “Now I can put my name beside the right load,” the driver says. The extra day costs your party time, but the guards and households remember who helped clear the mistake.
ev.ev_road_37.choice_2_result: You pay the guide, board the cart he arranged and turn away from the queue. At the alternate crossing he asks you to watch where the cart wheels leave the hard bank. “After rain, keep the left wheel by that stone,” he says. The detour adds a day before you rejoin the road. You repeat the marker to your travelling party and send it back with a returning traveller for the people still waiting at the storehouse.
ev.ev_road_38.choice_1_result: You give the keeper enough for food and water. He fills a clean vessel while the mother warms a little broth for the child. “Keep the cup by him,” she tells the father, “and ask again when he wakes.” Before you leave, the family gathers for a short prayer for people on the road. You join them, then carry your own water carefully through the next stretch. The father returns to his old story only after his son is resting.
ev.ev_road_38.choice_2_result: You spend an extra day asking at the nearby settlement. A woman grinding grain points you to the healer’s house and offers to take a message ahead. The healer agrees to see the child, and you bring the family along the shaded lane. “Thank you. We can take him inside now,” the mother says. The keeper and neighbours thank you for returning with clear directions. The father folds his old story away and helps lift the child inside.
ev.ev_road_39.choice_1_result: You and the niece set the bales in a row while the driver reads their marks aloud. Two lines on the account point to the same seal. “That is one bale written twice,” the merchant says. He sends a note to the clerk and corrects the delivery list before anyone pays or takes the wrong cloth. The buyers check their own bundles at the shed. The merchant thanks you in front of them; the next time your party passes, they remember you as the traveller who helped settle the count.
ev.ev_road_39.choice_2_result: You go with the merchant’s party to the next market, adding a day to your journey. His niece counts this separate, smaller delivery of eight bales and writes a new list before departure. At the market the buyer checks each seal and signs the receipt. “Eight here, and eight on the list,” she says. The merchant pays you the delivery wage he promised. A returning driver takes the receipt back to the trading shed, and you rejoin your road.
ev.ev_road_astrodice_counsel.choice_2_re: You walk on. A mark is set on this affair.
ev.ev_road_bazi_counsel.choice_2_result: You walk on. A mark is set on this affair.
ev.ev_road_desert_voices.choice_1_result: You take a lamp and follow the call over one low ridge. By the time you turn, the campfire has disappeared behind another. The guard calls from the rope line, but the wind takes his words apart. It takes your party three extra days to find you by the old water marks and get everyone back on the road. The cook sets hot water beside you without asking for a story. That night you keep waking at every sound beyond the tent.
ev.ev_road_desert_voices.choice_2_result: You stay beside the rope line. The guard calls once toward the dunes, then listens while the wind repeats only the last syllable. “That could be what I heard,” the camel keeper says, though he still checks that his brother is asleep. You mark the place and the direction of the wind on your route notes. At dawn the whole party leaves together, and the story of the voices goes into your account of the desert road.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01.choice_1_result: The merchant sends his hired driver behind the lead cart while you walk with the animals along its tracks. At the far bank, his sister comes out with two porters. She checks the seals on the oil jars and laughs when she finds that he has packed extra straw around every one. “You do this every winter,” she says. He asks for a cloth to dry his hands before they count the jars together. The first day is spent bringing the carts and animals across in separate turns. On the far bank a wheel needs mending before the merchant can reload; the crossing and repair add two days to your journey. You note the delay in your book and travel on once the wheel holds.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01.choice_2_result: The merchant's cart is already across when the scouts return at supper with wet boots. One has found a split near the upper crossing. You spend three days at the waystation while the keeper and the scouts mark a safer line with branches. Each morning you help them carry the branches to the bank; each evening the keeper asks what the people on the far side have seen. On the third morning he walks you to the line they have marked, then returns to meet the next group of travellers.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.body: The river is behind you now. At a roadside camp, a driver spreads his map on a folded blanket and tries to place the crossing. He remembers the waystation and a clump of trees on the far bank, then stops. “If I come back when the ice has gone, I'll need to find the ferry instead,” he says. His companions are packing for the next market. The driver offers you his charcoal pencil for a moment; you can mark the crossing with him or join the departing group.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.choice_1: Mark the crossing and the waystation on the map
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.choice_1_r: You draw the river bend, the waystation, and the place where you crossed. The driver adds the ferry landing he used last summer, then folds the map so the fresh charcoal will not smear. He thanks you for remembering the clump of trees. You put the route in your book as well, ready for another season's journey.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.choice_2: Travel on to the next market
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.choice_2_r: You leave the driver with his map and travel with the group to the next market. The pack animals crowd around the water trough before anyone thinks of selling. One of the drivers buys bread and brings you a piece while you wait your turn. It is evening when you arrive, and a few stalls are still open.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_01_followup.title: The Road Beyond the Ice Crossing
ev.ev_road_fadlan_02.choice_1_result: The guide takes his fee and walks beside the young driver. At each stone marker he asks the driver to choose the next one, then shows him the mark under the snow. After a day's travel the animals are eating beside the shelter he promised. “You can find this place next time,” he tells the driver, who has been counting the turns aloud all afternoon. You write down how the road is marked for later journeys.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_02.choice_2_result: The young driver finds a third stone and the caravan follows him. Near midday the tracks vanish into windblown snow, and the drivers stop to search the ridge for another marker. They find it before dark. At the shelter, the young man warms his hands over the fire and draws the turn they missed in the snow for the others. The journey to the shelter has taken two days, and the caravan master has everyone check the markers together from then on.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_03.choice_1_result: You sit by the fire and read the old passage to the brothers. The boy points toward the sunset clouds and asks again about the riders. His brother shows him how the light fades from the clouds before the sky turns dark; Ibn Fadlan's red mist, the account says, lasted into the night. You spend the next day at camp comparing the two descriptions with your companion and put the old account's source in your book. By supper the boy can tell the difference himself, and he asks to hear the passage once more.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_03.choice_2_result: Inside, a companion moves his bowl so you can sit by the stove. He asks what the boy made of the old account, and you tell him the herder is reading it aloud by the fire. Wind rises during the night, and your party waits a full day for it to ease. You help the herder mend the sheep pen latch while the others secure their packs. The sky clears by evening, and you set out the next morning.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_04.choice_1_result: You ask the merchant how the king's words reached this page. He shows you the name at the top: Ibn Fadlan, who wrote that he had asked the king about the stranger. The merchant copied the passage at a bookstall years ago; he has read it so often that the folds are wearing through. His niece asks whether the king named the traders who found the man. The page gives no names. You note where the story came from, and she offers you the last warm piece of bread before asking what tales people tell on your own road.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_04.choice_2_result: At dawn the merchant's niece is already packing the bread she baked. She gives your caravan a piece for the road and asks you to bring back a story from the next stop. You travel through the day to a watering place, where the drivers finally unhitch the animals. As they settle in, one of them asks if you remember how large the merchant said the man's head was. The story has travelled with you after all.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_05.choice_1_result: You stay for the day and read the old account with the young man. He stops at the passage about the clothing sewn for the dead and remembers his grandfather measuring canvas for boats in the same ledger. You mark where Ibn Fadlan begins his own observations, and where he reports what others told him. When his sister arrives, he reads her the part about the boat and gives her both the ledger and the cloak. She asks to copy the page before taking it home.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_05.choice_2_result: You accompany the young man to the well where his sister is waiting. She takes their grandfather's cloak and notices the old book under his arm. He tells her he found it in the work ledger; she remembers their grandfather reading aloud from it on winter evenings. The three of you spend the rest of the day sorting his tools and folding the cloth he left behind. When your party departs, brother and sister are still deciding which pages they will copy together.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_06.choice_1_result: You pay the sailor for the chart. His daughter waits until the ink dries, then rolls the chart around a wooden rod. She shows you the harbour they drew from memory and the notes her father copied from travellers' accounts. At the blank inlet she leaves space for a name. The sailor asks you to tell him what the coast is like if your journey takes you there; you copy the island stories into your book before packing the chart.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_06.choice_2_result: You leave the chart on the crate and join the inland merchant. The sailor's daughter gives him a scrap of paper with the harbour name she has just inked, in case he meets anyone travelling toward the coast. After the extra day's march, he unfolds it at supper and asks you to repeat the story of the island where people heard voices. By the end of the meal, two drivers have added tales of their own.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_07.choice_1_result: You hold the cord while the broker ties off the tusk. Then he has the apprentice lay out the beaver and ermine skins again, each in its own stack. He explains which river traders bring them and why the buyers in Khwarazm want the bundles kept separate. You write down the goods and the route south. When another buyer asks who helped sort the load, the broker introduces you by name and invites you back to his stall.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_07.choice_2_result: The caravan master calls for the last animals, and you hand the cord back to the apprentice. He has finally tied the beaver skins apart from the ermine. The broker lifts the tusk bundle onto a cart and promises to finish his story when you pass this way again. You spend an extra day travelling with the departing caravan, watching the market disappear behind the dust.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_08.choice_1_result: You stay for the next exchange. The young trader puts his polished bone down again, this time beside a blade, and the group withdraws. When they return, a small sable skin lies by the pair. He picks it up carefully and asks the older trader if his father will think the bargain fair. “Show him what you brought back,” the trader says. Over two extra days you watch how each offer is laid out, accepted, or left in place, and write down the method without ever seeing the people on the other side of the clearing.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_08.choice_2_result: You leave the traders to their next offer and follow the forest edge. Late in the day, the tracks made by the long boards cross your path. Your driver pauses to let the animals sniff them, then leads the caravan on. After the extra day's travel you reach a sheltered camp. The young trader and his polished bone are still in your thoughts, though you never learn how his next bargain ended.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_09.choice_1_result: You walk out to the mound with the pilgrim and his daughter. From the top, she sees how the grass parts around the old stones at its base and draws those lines first. Her father reads her the old passages about a gold-tiled dome and the giants of Iram; you keep the names with the source in your travel notes. The visit and return add two days to your journey. The girl shows you her finished drawing and points to the stones she saw with her own eyes.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_09.choice_2_result: The pilgrim's daughter folds her drawing and gives you a small copy of the page about the dome. “Tell me what you see on your road when we meet again,” she says. You take an extra day with the caravan, stopping at a well before dark. One of the drivers asks to hear the part about the boats disappearing, and you read it aloud beside the water.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_10.choice_1_result: You spend two extra days at the market with the seed seller and the gardener. A woman who tends a plot beyond the well says her vines need shade in the hottest part of the day; another grower describes how he stores melons after harvest. The seller separates his seeds into small packets while you write each answer beside the name of the person who gave it. You also copy the old description of Khwarazm from his page. By the time your caravan is ready to move, the growers know your name and have asked to hear how the seeds fare on your next visit.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_10.choice_2_result: You buy bread and dried fruit from the next stall. The gardener asks the seed seller to keep one packet for him until the following market day, and the seller writes his name on the wrapping. You leave them discussing where the well casts shade in the afternoon. After an extra day on the road, you open your provisions at the next camp and find that the stallholder tucked in an extra handful of raisins.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_11.choice_1_result: The courier lays the old page beside his freshly mended bag. He traces the sequence of letters from Samarra through Armenia, the Alan ruler, and the Khazar tarkhān. The younger clerk repeats the names while he seals today's letter for the next station. You write down the route as part of Sallām's account. When the courier shoulders his bag, he thanks you for staying to listen and asks the clerk to keep today's letter flat until the ink dries.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_11.choice_2_result: You leave the courier finishing his stitches and join your party on the road. During the extra day's travel, you pass two small stations where messengers change horses. At the second, the clerk from the morning catches up with a sealed letter and recognizes you. He lifts the bag to show you the repaired seam before hurrying on to his next stop.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_12.choice_1_result: You tell the map seller which shelter was open when you passed it and where the last well lay. He corrects two marks on his current list, then shows you the older page and explains the routes Ibn Khurradādhbih recorded for the Radhaniya and the Rus. The waiting customer copies the new shelter note, and the seller writes your name beside the correction so he can ask you about the next stretch when you return.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_12.choice_2_result: You pay for the current list. The seller circles a recently opened well and a short track that rejoins the main road beyond it. He reads the distances aloud while you copy the halt names into your book. Your party follows his notes over one extra day and reaches the next stop before sunset. At the fire, the drivers pass the list around and check where they will water the animals next.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_13.choice_1_result: The apprentice reads the passage aloud and stops at the khaqan's fate. The copyist points out where Mas'udi says the king sometimes defended him. You mark the source and both reported outcomes in your notes. When the page is dry, the apprentice folds it carefully into the book and asks if you will bring him any other accounts of distant courts.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_13.choice_2_result: You hand back the page and set out with your own company. A broken axle holds the party at the next water stop; by evening the driver has fitted a sound peg and everyone can travel again. The repair adds a full day to your journey. The copyist's apprentice passes on horseback just before sunset and waves with ink still on his fingers.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_14.choice_1_result: You remain at the camp through the next daylight and night, noting the sun's position and the teacher's marks on the stick. The pupil spills the water bowl once and has to set it level again. At dawn you compare your record with the book's account of Bulghar. The teacher writes today's place and date at the top of your page, then returns to the road with his book repaired.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_14.choice_2_result: You leave the teacher and his pupil at the camp. Farther along, your party finds the short bridge closed while its planks are replaced. The detour takes an extra day. At the evening halt you make room by the fire and wonder what the pupil will find when she reads her marks in the morning.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_15.choice_1_result: You help unfold the bundle and match the maker's marks to the trader's order sheet. The nephew finds the tailor's dark pelts at the bottom and reties them with a fresh strip of cloth. The trader tells you how his family buys and carries fur along this road; you record his account beside Mas'udi's much older route. He remembers your name when the carts move on and introduces you to the next driver.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_15.choice_2_result: You take the open track around the carts. It runs behind a low ridge and rejoins the main road only after a long bend. Your party spends an extra day crossing it and reaches water at dusk. The fur trader arrives there later with his bundles sorted, and his nephew holds up the newly tied labels when he recognizes you.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_16.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day going from seller to seller with the broker's daughter. She knows which woman brought the wax and which family carved the wood; you ask the owners before writing their names. By evening the broker has a fresh list of today's stock and you have a separate note about Muqaddasi's older Bulghar list. He reads your entries back to the sellers and sends his daughter home with the completed page.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_16.choice_2_result: You buy provisions and let the broker's daughter return to her work. The market keeps you an extra day as it empties, and your party leaves with the last carts as the sellers pack away their awnings. One of them shares the track to the next camp and points out where the ground stays firm after rain.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_17.choice_1_result: You pay the keeper for the ride. He stows your bag low on the sled, gives the lead dog a strip of dried food, and shows you where to hold on. After the extra day you reach the far post, while the walkers are still on the ice road. The keeper checks every dog's paws before he unhitches them. You write down how the team and sled were prepared, with Biruni's older northern account noted separately.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_17.choice_2_result: You follow the line of poles across the ice, carrying only what you need for the day. On the second morning a loose pole has fallen flat; you put it upright for the next walkers. The post keeper's sled crosses in the distance, and he lifts an arm when he sees you. Your party reaches the next post after two extra days and finds warm water set out by the keeper.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_18.choice_1_result: The boy draws a line of names on a spare sheet: the chronicler, the Novgorod merchant, his servant and the people who first told him the story. He reads it from the end back to the beginning and sees why each name matters. His father lends you the book long enough to check the detail about iron and fur, and you keep the source in your own notes. They place the boy's sheet beside the old passage before putting the book away.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_18.choice_2_result: You give the book back to the boy and take the longer firm track with your party, adding a day to the journey. At the next halt a singer is asking everyone for a story, and one driver begins to repeat the mountain tale. You listen while making supper. By the time the singer finishes his own version, the fire is low and the animals are settled for the night.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19.choice_1_result: Over two extra days, the merchant takes you along the edge of the low ground. He teaches you to feel the slack in the line, count each person at a stop and mark a dry return point before fog thickens. His companion changes the knot at her wrist until it sits comfortably. You write down the method and the father's far northern account as two different stories. When the merchant's group finally enters the fog, you know which marked place they plan to return to.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19.choice_2_result: You thank the merchant and take the clear road around the low ground. It adds a day to your journey. At the evening camp you meet a family bringing sheep the same way; they share a well with your party and point to the dry rise where you can make your next halt. Across the plain, the merchant's rope team is still arranging its packs.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.body: At the next halt, you meet the fur merchant and his companions coming off the fog road. Everyone is present. The woman whose wrist hurt has wrapped a strip of cloth beneath the rope, and she shows you how the knot held without rubbing her skin. The merchant spreads out a damp route sketch. One marker had fallen, so they stood together until the lead walker found the dry rise. His father is long gone, but the merchant still tells the northern story while they dry their packs.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.choice_1: Write down where the group lost and found the marker
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.choice_1_r: You ask each traveller what they could see from the fallen marker. Their answers put the dry rise in the right place on your sketch. The merchant checks your page and copies the correction into his own route notes. When the group sets off again, they leave the damaged marker with the next road keeper so it can be repaired.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.choice_2: Ask the woman how she adjusted the rope
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.choice_2_r: She unties the rope and shows you the cloth beneath it. "I can feel when the next person stops," she says, "and I can still use my hand." You make a small drawing of the knot in your book. She keeps the cloth for the return journey and joins the others by the fire.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_19_followup.title: The Rope Team Returns
ev.ev_road_fadlan_20.choice_1_result: You wait until the horses have drunk, then join the march that adds two days. The carter's sister keeps a small pot near the front of the cart and melts ice whenever the animals stop. At the next shelter her brother can work his fingers again and takes the reins. You note the way the party prepared water and protected its hands during the winter crossing.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_20.choice_2_result: You help gather the wood already stacked at camp and keep the fire going while the horses rest. The carter's sister warms water for them and changes the cloth around her brother's fingers. You leave after the rest and reach the next shelter after three extra days. There, the brother thanks you by taking the first turn at watering the horses.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_21.choice_1_result: The seller reads the distances from his old route list while the courier names each person who passed on the northern stories. You put a small mark beside the tower, just as the seller did, and copy the stages he can trace. The courier asks to take your corrected copy to his uncle. You lend it to him until the next halt, where he promises to return it.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_21.choice_2_result: You let the courier roll up the map and travel an extra day's road with your party. At a well, another traveller asks the courier where the northern towns lie. You hear him say, "My uncle heard of them; I haven't been there myself." He has remembered the map seller's careful answer by the time you all reach camp.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_22.choice_1_result: You pay the boatman after his daughter finishes the seam. She tests the patch with a scoop of water, then loads your pack low in the boat. The animals cross separately, and the work adds a day to your journey. On the far bank you ask the daughter how she keeps the hide taut around its frame; she shows you the spare lacing she carries. You add her explanation to your notes on steppe crossings.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_22.choice_2_result: You go upstream with the caravan. The first attempt fails when a horse pulls free of the guide rope, so everyone brings the animals back and finds firmer ground. The crossing adds two days to your journey. Your pack gets wet in the current, and you spend the evening drying its contents beside the drivers. By morning the horse is calm and all the carts are across.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23.choice_1_result: You hold the remaining horses while the daughter and her brother follow the tracks. A rider from the neighbouring camp brings news of a man seen leading three mounts toward the reeds. Your watch keeps the family from losing another horse, and the search adds a day to your journey. At dusk the father tells his neighbours you stayed when his children needed someone at the tether. He invites you to wait for the searchers with him.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23.choice_2_result: You wait until the family has brought its remaining horses inside the camp, then leave with your party. An extra day's march takes you past the last well. The daughter rides by later with her brother, still following the three sets of hoofprints. She thanks you for waiting until the camp was secure before taking the road.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.body: Back at the camp, the daughter and her brother return with two of the missing horses. A young man from another tent admits he took all three and traded the last one to a passing buyer. His father offers a replacement from his own herd, and the two families sit with the camp's elders to agree on its value. The daughter gives the recovered horses water before she joins them. Her father thanks you for watching the others and asks whether you will stay to hear the agreement.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.choice_1: Stay for the agreement and the family's meal
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.choice_1_r: You remain for two days while the elders check the replacement horse and the families settle the loss. At the shared meal, the daughter says she can now put all three horses back in their places at the tether. Her father introduces you to the guests as the traveller who kept watch. One elder gives you the name of the family at the next water stop, where your help will be remembered.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.choice_2: Hear the agreement and leave with your party
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.choice_2_r: You listen until both families accept the replacement, then take the road. The return to your party and the onward march use a day. At the next halt you hear the daughter's brother recounting how they followed the hoofprints to the reeds. He recognizes you and says the horses are back with their family.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_23_followup.title: The Family Finds Its Horses
ev.ev_road_fadlan_24.choice_1_result: You take the offered bowl and sit by the fire. The host's son finishes the saddle strap, then draws the next stretch of road in the dust. His mother gives you the well's name and asks you to repeat it so she knows you heard it correctly. The family remembers your name, and you keep their directions with your notes on the welcome you received.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_24.choice_2_result: You buy raisins and pepper at a nearby stall and bring them to the tent. The host thanks you and divides the raisins among the children after everyone has eaten. Her son repairs your loose saddle strap while he talks through the route to the next well. When you leave, the family calls after you to use the firmer track around the low ground.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25.choice_1_result: You share the first night's watch with the shepherd's family. The wolves come near enough to stir the goats, then move away when the watchers gather at the tether. At dawn the sister counts every animal. She stays with the herd while your party travels onward and reaches the next halt by the second evening. The watch and march add two days to your journey.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25.choice_2_result: At first light you depart with the loaded carts. The drivers keep the animals close, but a wolf follows along the far side of the road for part of the day. One horse shies and its load shifts; the party stops to tie it again before reaching the next camp after an extra day. The shepherd and his sister remain behind with their goats.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.body: At the next halt, the shepherd's sister catches up with news of the herd. She and her brother counted every goat that morning; the wolves had crossed the road farther out and left fresh tracks beside the old ones. She has brought a twig marked with the place where they turned. "I want to know whether they are still following the carts," she says. The drivers offer to keep a watch for another day. You can help with that watch or walk out with her to look at the tracks.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.choice_1: Keep watch with the drivers for another day
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.choice_1_r: You take a turn at the outer tether while the drivers repair their gear. The extra watch uses a day. The sister goes back to her goats before sunset, satisfied that the wolves have moved away from the road. One driver replaces a loose knot you spotted and thanks you for keeping an eye on the animals.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.choice_2: Look at the fresh tracks with the shepherd's sister
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.choice_2_r: You follow the sister to the place she marked. The newer prints bend away from the road toward open grazing ground; none lead back to the carts. She points out which tracks belong to the same animal and shows you how their direction changed. You return with her to the halt, where the drivers have already finished loading.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_25_followup.title: Tracks Beyond the Camp
ev.ev_road_fadlan_26.choice_1_result: You share clean water and stay through an extra day, tending the fire while the mother cares for her daughter. Her brother arrives with the healer by evening. You make room for them and bring the water bowl when asked. The mother later tells the next travellers you helped keep the camp ready; you note the family's arrangement for calling the healer and set out the following morning.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_26.choice_2_result: You give the mother some water and travel on. At the next stop, after an extra day's journey, you meet her brother leading the healer's horse back toward the family camp. You tell him his sister was still waiting there and show him the shortest way around the low hill. He thanks you and urges the horse into a steady trot.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_27.choice_1_result: The sister lays out the family's old Aral route list and traces its wells with her finger. She also points to the mark for the place where this particular load was bought, much nearer to your present road. You ask about both journeys and note the different sellers. Her brother straightens the scale hook while she speaks, then weighs the cook's parcel accurately and sends it on with the next cart.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_27.choice_2_result: You leave the family to repair its scale and walk an extra day's road with your party. By evening, the salt merchants catch up with the small parcel tied safely above the larger blocks. The brother says the scale is working again and asks the cook's camp to show him where to unload. You point out the fire where the cook is waiting.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_28.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day comparing the aunt's drawing with the copied traveller's account. The keeper fills his marked bowl several times to show the boy how it measures time. The boy writes down the question his aunt could not answer from memory. You note the old eclipse as a reported event and label the two accounts separately. Before supper, the aunt shows him how she drew the curve of the sun from memory.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_28.choice_2_result: You thank the family for showing you the drawing and take the longer road, adding a day to your journey with your party. At the evening halt, the young rider catches up. Her brother is still trying to work out the marks in the old account, she says, and their aunt has promised to read it again with him. Your horses settle beside theirs for the night.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29.choice_1_result: You remain through an extra day while the group waters its animals and makes ready to move. The woman and her brother tell you their names, and two others say where they were taken from. You ask the traveller who knows the village to repeat each name before he goes. He promises to tell the woman's mother that both children were alive at this well. You keep the names and the route in your book. The woman asks you to make sure her brother's name is legible.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29.choice_2_result: You continue with your party and spend an extra day travelling to the next camp. The traveller who recognized the village leaves by another track at noon. Before he goes, you hear the woman repeat her mother's name to him, and he says it back so she knows he will remember it. Your party reaches shelter by dusk.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.body: At the evening fire, the traveller who knows the woman's village asks for the names you heard. He is taking a road that passes her mother, and he wants to carry an accurate account. You read your page aloud. He repeats the siblings' names and the well where you met them, then asks which road the guarded group took. The woman had asked him to remember; he holds out a clean piece of paper for your answer.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.choice_1: Copy the names and the route onto his paper
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.choice_1_r: You add the route to the names and let him read it back before he folds the page. He tucks it inside his coat and sets out toward the woman's village. You keep your own account with the source of each detail marked. The next time you reach a well, you remember how carefully he repeated the names.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.choice_2: Tell him the names and fold your own page away
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.choice_2_r: You tell him what the woman said, and he repeats it until he can say both names without looking at your page. You fold your account and place it with your other road papers. He sets out to find her mother; you travel with your own party, knowing he has the names she asked him to carry.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_29_followup.title: A Copy of Their Names
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30.choice_1_result: You help carry the family's bundles to the dry rise and drive the pegs deep while the father holds the tent cloth. The rain runs past the carts; the little boy keeps the spare rope under his coat so it stays dry. The storm and the soft ground add two days to your party's journey. When the clouds clear, the family invites the neighbours who helped them to share supper before everyone packs.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30.choice_2_result: You join the drivers on the road as the rain eases. A gust throws one cart's cover loose, and everyone stops to tie it down before the lightning returns. The extra day's march ends at a sheltered hollow. The horses are shaking from the wet wind, and the drivers spend the evening drying their harnesses and checking the loads.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.body: At a sheltered stop after the storm, a driver from your party spreads a torn cart cover on the ground. One corner caught on a peg when the wind rose. He and his daughter can stitch it before moving on, and the horses need time to recover from the storm. She suggests resting until the ground firms. He asks whether you will stay near them or go ahead with the other carts.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.choice_1: Stay two days while they mend the cover and rest the horses
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.choice_1_r: You help hold the cover while the daughter stitches its corner. The driver walks the horses on dry ground, then gives them time to feed. After two days the cover is sound and the ruts at the edge of camp have hardened. The family sets out with you, and the daughter checks her stitches once at the first halt before she rolls the cover tight.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.choice_2: Travel a day with the carts already leaving
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.choice_2_r: You leave the driver and his daughter at the sheltered stop and join the carts going on. The road is still wet, so the lead driver walks ahead to choose firmer ground. A full day later, at the next camp, he shows the others where he found a dry line beside the wheel ruts. Your party reaches its shelter before the next rain.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_30_followup.title: The Road After the Rain
ev.ev_road_fadlan_31.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day with the elder and her grandson. He measures the cut with a cord; she places each pottery fragment on the cloth near the spot where she found it. Your sketch shows the opened side and the stones still in place. The elder looks it over, then asks her grandson to help fill the cut before rain. He tucks a copy of the sketch into the family's bundle so they can remember what was found.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_31.choice_2_result: You leave the elder and her grandson to finish the mound and travel an extra day with your party. At the next camp, someone asks whether the old hill still stands beside the road. You tell him the family was filling the opening and collecting the scattered pottery. He knows the elder and says he will ask her how the work went when he passes home.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32.choice_1_result: You pay the toll after the clerk writes your load on a stamped receipt. The ferryman's daughter calls your animals forward when the queue thins, and the crossing adds a day to your journey. On the far bank, the clerk's assistant reads the receipt and helps find the sack that had been set with another party's goods. He hands it back and remembers your name when you thank him.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32.choice_2_result: You take the upstream route with your own baggage. The shallow crossing is farther than it looked from the first ford, and the party spends three extra days reaching it and getting the animals over. One load slips in the water; the drivers pull it back and dry it on the bank before continuing. At the next waystation the main road meets yours again.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.body: The two river routes meet at a small waystation. Its keeper has a fenced place for animals and a dry room where travellers can sort their loads. A driver from your party has a chafed harness strap, and the keeper offers a repair kit with the room. He asks a fee for two days' lodging and feed. The open road continues past the station; if you move on, your party can reach the next halt in a day.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.choice_1: Pay for two days at the waystation
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.choice_1_r: You pay for the room and take it while the driver repairs his harness. The keeper sets out feed for the animals, then checks the strap before they are hitched again. Two days later your party leaves with its loads in order. The driver keeps the trimmed end of the old strap to show the next person who asks why he stopped here.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.choice_2: Continue with your party to the next halt
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.choice_2_r: You take the road past the waystation. The driver wraps his chafed strap in spare cloth and checks it whenever the animals stop. After a day's travel, your party reaches the next halt; he borrows a needle there and repairs the strap before supper.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_32_followup.title: The Waystation Beyond the Ford
ev.ev_road_fadlan_33.choice_1_result: You spend an extra day beside the bootmaker's apprentice, loosening the outer lacing and fitting the sole. The bootmaker shows you how far to keep a soaked boot from the fire, using the customer's old mistake as her example. By evening the apprentice can fit the boots without her hands guiding his. She explains which layers she adds for a winter journey, and you keep the method beside Ibn Fadlan's much older account of cold travel. The apprentice brings you the finished pair to inspect before you leave.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_33.choice_2_result: You thank the bootmaker and take the road with your party. It takes an extra day's travel to the next halt. A cart driver there is rubbing a worn heel; you tell him where the bootmaker is working. He knows the place and says he will bring his pair to her when he turns back.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_34.choice_1_result: You follow the daughter around the salt ground for two extra days, taking water from the wells she knows rather than from the shining surface. She shows you where the crust changes from firm to thin and asks you to help move one of the route markers to drier soil. When her father meets you again, she points to the new mark on his list. You add the changed edge of the flat to your own route notes.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_34.choice_2_result: You take the father's marked track and travel beside the salt ground for an extra day. The cart driver who mistook it for water stops at the real well and lets his animals drink. He thanks the guide's daughter when she catches up, then calls the next driver over to show him the white ground from a safe distance.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35.choice_1_result: You wait while the guide checks the marked line from bank to bank. His pole finds a thinner patch near a bend, so he moves two branches and leads the first sled around it. The crossing adds a day to your journey. On the far side, the driver's daughter asks to try the pole on firm ice; the guide shows her how he checked each stretch. You keep his method with your notes on winter crossings.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35.choice_2_result: You take your place with the first group on the marked line. One horse slips and pulls its sled sideways; the driver and his daughter steady it before the runners leave the path. Everyone reaches the far bank, but moving the loads and checking the horses adds a day to your journey. The guide keeps the group together until the last sled is safely off the ice.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.body: The last sled is off the ice. On the far bank, the guide counts his marking branches and finds two missing from the thinner bend. The driver's daughter volunteers to bring them back, but he asks her to wait until he has checked the bank. He wants a small drawing of the safe line for the next party. You can help him make it while the route is fresh, or continue toward the next halt with your own companions.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.choice_1: Help the guide draw the crossing for the next party
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.choice_1_r: The guide draws the bank and the thinner bend while you place the two missing branches on his sketch. The driver's daughter adds the place where the first sled entered and asks him to check it. He puts the finished sheet in a dry case for the next crossing party. You keep the method in your winter road notes and leave him marking the bank in the afternoon light.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.choice_2: Travel one more day to the next halt
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.choice_2_r: You leave the guide and the driver's daughter to finish the markers and travel with your companions. A day's march brings you to a sheltered halt. The driver of the first sled checks the lashings before he unloads; his daughter has tied the loose end neatly. They will ask the guide for his drawing when they return this way.
ev.ev_road_fadlan_35_followup.title: The Branches on the Far Bank
ev.ev_road_fork_tarot.choice_2_result: You choose by experience alone. The matter is marked and will not be forgotten.
ev.ev_road_geomancy_counsel.choice_2_res: You walk on. The matter is marked and will not be forgotten.
ev.ev_road_jiaobei_counsel.choice_2_resu: You walk on. The matter is marked and will not be forgotten.
ev.ev_road_runes_counsel.choice_2_result: You walk on. The matter is marked and will not be forgotten.
ev.ev_sachiu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass the monastery as the family gathers around their mother. The farmer gives you a melon slice for the road. You carry a memory of their rite and record the place in your travel book.
ev.ev_sachiu_site_gap.choice_1_result: Yulduz and the rider name the stopping places toward Etzina. Her son notices one board is written with an older station name, so she gives you the name travellers use now. You mark the route on your map.
ev.ev_sachiu_site_gap.choice_2_result: You and the boy clear the hard thorns while Yulduz measures the feed. The young horses eat safely, and she explains why she dries each sack before tying it. You remember the station’s way of caring for animals.
ev.ev_saianfu_a.choice_1_result: You watch the silk weavers at their looms. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Sinjumatu on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_a.choice_2_result: You buy fine silken stuff from a weaver's stall. You pay 9000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The road to Cachanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_a.choice_3_result: You ask the magistrates which towns owe tribute. You set what you saw into your travel book. A small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.body: In the noble city that rules twelve others a clerk who keeps the tribute lists of the subordinate towns draws you into the magistrate's outer court. He says Saianfu's silk and ginger roads are the same roads that feed those twelve — and that a traveller who buys without hearing the list rides half-blind toward Sinjumatu and Cachanfu.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_1: Buy silk at the magistrate's measured price
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_1_result: You leave with silk sealed for the circuit road. The price is fair, and Saianfu's name goes with the bolt.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which of the twelve roads leads toward Sinjumatu
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_2_result: Sinjumatu and Cachanfu are marked on your map. The rich circuit is no longer a blank.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day with the weavers and hear the circuit names
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day among the looms. Kenjanfu is named in the talk, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.title: Saianfu: The Twelve Cities' Clerk
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_1_result: You walk the hunters' market beside the workshops. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Kenjanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_2_result: You buy ginger from a victualler's stall. You pay 2000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_3_result: You walk the northern approach where the host once lay siege. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. You set the way to Saianfu on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Saianfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the sì (Buddhist monastery). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Saianfu on your map.
