ev.ev_samara_entry.choice_1_result: Ismail points out the higher path along the landing. His daughter calls the full barrels by their red cloth marks as you pass. You mark Samara on your map and continue.
ev.ev_samara_entry.choice_2_result: You rest for a day beneath the family’s shade. Ismail’s mother shares rice and fish, and his daughter shows you the well after she finishes marking the barrels. You leave rested and add the landing to your map.
ev.ev_samara_site_gap.choice_1_result: The pilot shows you the sea passage to Chamba and names the harbours where a ship can wait for wind. Lela’s son marks the first stretch on your map, and the pilot adds the final approach to Chamba.
ev.ev_samara_site_gap.choice_2_result: You help Lela spread the old sail in moving air. She points out a worn seam and shows her son how to follow the old needle holes. You remember how this family prepares a boat before the wind turns.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_1_result: You spend two days with Hamid and the students. His niece brings the gardener’s account into their discussion, and you leave with a new way to compare a traveller’s report with what the ground shows. Hamid invites you to the next lesson.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_2_result: You stand beneath the small dome and watch the light move across its blue tiles. Hamid’s niece tells you who repaired the roof after a winter storm. You remember the room and its careful work.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_3_result: You walk with the gardener, help move the branch and follow the canal to his plot. He introduces you to neighbours drawing water in turn. They welcome you when you greet each family by name.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.body:
Hamid has brought an astrolabe to the tiled porch. His niece turns it to catch a shaft of sunlight, then asks how the same marks help at night. A traveller who stayed for yesterday’s lesson points to a familiar star on a table. Hamid asks him where he saw it rise on the road. He cannot remember until the gardener names the bend in the canal where they camped.

You ask why the gardener is in the lesson again. He says the students promised to help keep leaves out of the channel, and he wants to hear whether their reckoning matches the hours he knows. Hamid lets him trace the water route beside the star table. The niece writes both accounts down, laughing when the two men disagree by a little more than one hour.

Hamid will spend a day on the tables with you. The traveller knows the road east toward Cascar and is leaving after lunch. The niece wants to hear your own road account before anyone folds the chart away.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_1: Spend a day with Hamid’s star table
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_1_res: You spend a day with Hamid and the niece, checking the table against sun and night sky. The gardener comes back at dusk to compare his water hours. You record what they taught you.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the eastbound traveller about Cascar
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_2_res: The traveller names the stopping places on the way to Cascar. Hamid’s niece checks them against the family’s old route notes, and you mark the destination on your map.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_3: Tell the students about your own road
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_3_res: You tell the students about a road you know. The niece asks a sharp question about water, and you answer with a place name the gardener recognises. They invite you to speak again beneath the tiled porch.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.title: The Sky Above Hamid’s Canal
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_1_result: You pay 100 silver for the full paper bale. Yusuf and Mariam check its dry edges and tie it for travel. Mariam keeps one separate sheet for her sister’s letter.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_2_result: You spend the day watching Yusuf press, dry and polish the sheets. The apprentice finally keeps his sandals away from the drying yard. Yusuf invites you back to see how Mariam finishes her sister’s letter.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_3_result: You pay 10 silver for the bound manuscript. The calligrapher shows you where his sister painted one border, then wraps the book against dust. You thank the family and put it safely in your pack.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.body:
Mariam is finishing the letter to her sister while Yusuf polishes another batch of paper. She asks him to leave one sheet unpolished so her young apprentice can feel the difference. The boy rubs both with a finger and says the smooth one will make the ink run faster. Mariam dips a pen and proves the opposite: on the finished sheet, her line keeps its edge.

You ask where the clean linen for the paper comes from. Yusuf says one dealer travels west through Bochara, while others bring rags from nearby households. Mariam adds that her sister saves worn clothes for them and sends a parcel with every reply. The apprentice asks whether he may write the address. ‘After you move your sandals from the drying yard,’ Mariam says. He does it at once and returns for the pen.

Yusuf has another full paper trading bale for 100 silver, separate from the one in front. He also has a polishing stone ready if you stay a day to try the work. Mariam sets the letter aside until its ink is dry.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the other full paper bale for 100 silver
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_1_res: You pay 100 silver for the second bale. Yusuf shows you its separate tally and Mariam checks every edge before wrapping it. The apprentice keeps the address sheet safely away from the workbench.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_2: Spend a day learning to polish paper
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_2_res: You spend a day at the polishing stone. Yusuf guides your hand until one sheet takes ink cleanly; Mariam uses it to make a fair copy of her letter. You carry the method in your notes.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_3: Ask Yusuf about the linen road from Bochara
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_3_res: Yusuf names the westbound dealer and the town of Bochara. Mariam points out the mark on her sister’s last parcel, so you know which caravan line carried it. You add Bochara to your map.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.title: Mariam’s Letter and the Polishing Stone
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_1_result: You touch the rain-cooled stone while Rashid’s mother tells you about the season she remembers. His daughter asks one more question, and you stay to hear the answer.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_2_result: You join the family for evening prayer. Rashid’s daughter folds her cloth beside her grandmother’s, and when you leave the courtyard they wish you a good road.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_3_result: Rashid’s mother reads a dated line and tells you which part she saw herself. His daughter asks to compare the next page. Rashid invites you back to hear the rest of their account.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.body:
Rashid has brought the courtyard notebook to the bench. His mother asks him to find the year the roof beam first leaked. He names a date; she remembers that they repaired the beam after her daughter’s wedding, which was a year later. Rashid asks his daughter to fetch the old repair receipt. The girl returns with it folded inside a prayer book and proudly reads the mason’s name.

You ask whether the stone also appears in the book. Rashid shows several notes about rain collecting on it, each written by a different visitor. His mother tells him to keep their names beside the dates. A family from Sapurgan arrives and says they came to see the courtyard after hearing a relative describe it. Rashid offers them the bench while his daughter explains what she saw this morning.

The stone has dried. Rashid is ready to read the full account if you stay a day, and the visitors can tell you how they reached Samarcand. His mother still holds the receipt, waiting for the corrected date.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_1: Touch the stone and hear Rashid’s mother
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_1_res: You touch the dry stone and listen to Rashid’s mother place the wedding and roof repair in order. His daughter writes the corrected date. You leave remembering how the family held the story together.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_2: Spend a day reading the weather book with Rashid
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_2_res: You spend a day reading the notebook. Rashid checks the receipt and dates with his mother, and his daughter copies the visitors’ names. You add the family’s record to your own account of the city.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_3: Ask the visitors how they came from Sapurgan
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_3_res: The visitors name the stopping places from Sapurgan. Rashid’s daughter marks the city on your map while her grandmother offers them tea. They thank you for asking after their journey.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.title: The Courtyard Weather Book
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.body:
The student who waited near Shirin’s desk catches up with you in the lane. His name is Nadir, and he has been asked to carry a note to an older teacher who remembers the street names used before the last flood shifted a canal. The writing on the note is faint. ‘Shirin says you copied the market lanes,’ he tells you. ‘Can you help me check which bridge this means?’

You ask why he does not take it straight to the teacher. Nadir says he already tried one house; its owner invited him in for tea but had never heard of the teacher. His little sister is waiting at home for him to return with a book the teacher promised her. He shows you the name beside the address, then admits he copied one letter badly.

A neighbour steps out to shake a mat. Nadir asks her whether she knows the old bridge name. She does, but wants to see the note before sending you across town. Nadir holds it up in the light and waits.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_1: Help Nadir check the old bridge name
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_1_: You and Nadir ask the neighbour to read the faded address. She points you toward the right bridge, and Nadir asks you to come along so he can check the teacher’s name in person.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_2: Let Nadir carry the note on his own
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_2_: You thank the neighbour for her help and leave the note with Nadir. He repeats the corrected bridge name twice, then hurries homeward by the lane she showed him.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.title: The Address on Shirin’s List
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a_resolutio:
The older teacher opens the door before Nadir has finished knocking. His sister has come ahead and is already sitting at the table with the promised book. She tells him she followed the old bridge name that their mother still uses. Nadir shows her the faded note and asks why she did not tell him it had two names. ‘You left before breakfast,’ she says.

You ask the teacher whether the road around the canal is still passable. He lays out a small street sketch and dates the last repair. Nadir’s sister adds a missing footpath she used that morning. The teacher lets her mark it herself, then asks Nadir to read the new directions back so no one goes to the wrong house again.

The family invites you to take the corrected sketch now. If you stay another day, you can copy the old and new street names into your book with the teacher’s help.
You take the corrected sketch. Nadir and his sister check the bridge names one last time; their teacher thanks you for helping the note reach the right door.
Spend a day copying old and new names
You spend a day copying the teacher’s street names. Nadir’s sister walks the route with you after breakfast and points out the little footpath. Your book now has both the older and newer directions.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.body:
After you have heard the neighbours’ stories, paper maker Yusuf finds you in the market with two lists in his hand. One names the caravan that carried his sister’s letter west; the other names a party who brought linen rags for his workshop. The same driver appears on both lists, but the departure dates differ. ‘Mariam says I copied one of them wrong,’ he tells you. ‘She is probably right.’

You ask why the dates matter. Yusuf says his sister promised to send news of their mother, and Mariam keeps asking when a reply might come. He does not want to tell her to wait for the wrong caravan. An old porter at the next stall remembers the driver but not the date. Yusuf asks him whether the man carried paper or cloth on his first trip. The porter can answer that much.

Yusuf sits down to compare the lists. He offers you a clean copy once they agree on the order, or you can leave the family to settle it together.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.choice_1: Help Yusuf put the two journeys in order

ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.title: The Paper Maker’s Two Lists
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b_resolutio:
Mariam has found her father’s mistake: he put the cloth caravan’s return date beside the letter caravan’s departure. Yusuf reads the corrected line aloud and asks her whether she will now stop asking about the reply every morning. ‘I will ask on the right mornings,’ she says. The old porter, back for paper, laughs so hard he almost drops his parcel.

You ask whether the letter caravan used the west gate. The porter tells you which yard it left from, and Yusuf adds that name to the paper. Mariam asks him to include the driver’s name too; he did promise to look after her aunt’s reply. She copies the whole entry with a steadier hand than her father’s.

They offer to share the corrected dates with the next student going west. You can tell that traveller now, or spend a day making a careful copy for your own route notes.
Tell the next westbound student today
You give the westbound student both dates and the driver’s name. Mariam asks him to repeat them back; he does, then promises to pass word if he meets her aunt’s caravan.
Spend a day copying the corrected account
You spend a day copying the dates, loads and names. Yusuf compares your page with Mariam’s clean version. By evening you have a useful account and she knows when to expect her aunt’s reply.

ev.ev_samarcanda_mentor_followup.body:
Bashir’s sister has brought him a clean sheet of local paper. She wants a map for a caravan carrying blue pigment from Badashan, but the old drawing shows a bridge closed for repairs. Bashir asks her which route the drivers used last week. She tells him, then asks why he has drawn the closed bridge at all. ‘So the next person knows why the road bends,’ he answers.

You ask where the blue pigment comes from. The sister says traders bring lapis from Badashan for painters, while the tile makers prepare their own blue glazes. A tile maker passing with fired pieces confirms that no single recipe gives every roof the same shade. Bashir sketches the detour while the two compare the colour of the pieces in daylight.

He can give you a copy of the revised street notes now, mark Badashan on your map, or spend a day with you checking the route in person. His sister holds the paper steady while he draws the repaired bridge’s new date.
ev.ev_samarcanda_mentor_followup.choice_: Bashir copies the changed bridge and the detour into your book. His sister checks the date; you take their revised notes with you.
Ask his sister about Badashan’s lapis road
His sister names the caravans that bring lapis from Badashan and marks the city on your map. The tile maker shows you the difference between two blue glazes before returning to his yard.
Spend a day walking the revised route
You spend a day with Bashir and his sister, crossing by the repaired bridge and noting the old detour. Back at the paper shop, she gives you a clean sheet for the finished drawing.

His wife has another full bale of cotton cloth for 108 silver, separate from the one offered earlier. A buyer wants to wait for tomorrow’s posted grain price before choosing his load. ev.ev_tauris_a_merchants_followup.body:
After the market closes, the third traveller brings his road book to Narin’s pearl table. The merchant from Baldacum notices a well missing from one page and asks whether it dried up. ‘It was there in spring,’ the traveller says, ‘but I did not stop.’ Narin’s daughter writes both facts rather than letting either man erase the other’s account.

You ask which road leads farther south toward Ctesiphon. The traveller opens a separate page and shows a river crossing, a tax desk, and a place where pack animals rest. Narin’s daughter asks why the rest place has a question mark. He says his mule was ill that week, so he cannot judge it fairly. The broker who helped at the market comes to look. He has a caravan leaving soon and wants the uncertain mark copied clearly, not hidden.

They set another lamp on the table. The broker asks you to show him what you learned before the book goes back into its leather cover.
ev.ev_tauris_a_merchants_followup.choice: Ask for the southward road to Ctesiphon

The traveller and the Baldacum merchant compare their southward accounts. You mark Ctesiphon on your map along with the river crossing. Narin’s daughter leaves the uncertain rest place marked with a question.
Share the uncertain well note with the broker
You tell the broker what both travellers said about the well. He adds a water reserve to the caravan list and thanks you in front of the merchants. Narin’s daughter keeps both accounts in her book.
Spend a day checking the water stops with the traders

You spend a day checking each water stop against the travellers’ dates. At the end Narin’s daughter draws a clean copy, with the doubtful places left plainly marked. You keep the record of how the roads were compared.
ev.ev_tauris_a_merchants_followup.title: Comparing the Road Books
ev.ev_tauris_b.choice_1_result: You help Mariam check the cloth order, then sit with the western merchant. He shows you Constantinopolis on your map. The apprentice reads the correct order aloud and the seller thanks all three of you.
ev.ev_tauris_b.choice_2_result: You pay 20 silver and study Persian with Mariam for twenty days. Her daughter tests you at supper by asking for the names of ordinary market goods. By the end you can answer her without waiting for a translation.
ev.ev_tauris_b.choice_3_result: The northern traveller points out Caffa and tells you which market families have kin there. Mariam’s daughter writes the city name carefully, and you add it to your map.
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.body:
After you speak with the western merchant, Mariam’s daughter asks you back to the interpreter’s bench. A pearl seller has brought a full trade parcel, and two buyers have written its name differently. One writes for the road toward Ninive; the other is preparing a note for a family still in Tauris. Mariam asks each person to read the label aloud. Her daughter catches the difference in the final word, a detail her mother had missed while the market was loud.

You ask whether the parcel will be sold today. The seller says it is available for 135 silver and wants the buyer’s name recorded before anyone takes it away. A clerk nearby knows the road toward Ninive and offers to mark it on a spare sheet. Mariam’s daughter wants to spend a day seeing how the tax book records pearls and cloth; her mother says she may come if she keeps the two orders apart. The seller sets the pearl parcel on the table and waits while the labels are rewritten.
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the full pearl parcel for 135 silver
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 135 silver for the parcel. Mariam and her daughter read the corrected name aloud before the seller seals it. The buyer who wrote the other order watches and confirms that her own parcel is still on the bench.
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the clerk about the road to Ninive
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_2_result: The clerk shows you Ninive on a spare sheet and names the places where travellers usually ask for water. Mariam’s daughter copies the place name and asks you to check its spelling on your map.
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_3: Spend a day checking the market tax book
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day with Mariam and her daughter matching labels to the tax book. By evening the two orders are distinct, and the clerk thanks you for a clear record. The market households speak well of your patience.
ev.ev_tauris_b_followup.title: A Second Entry in Mariam’s Book
ev.ev_tauris_c.choice_1_result: You rest at the garden for fourteen days. Shirin’s nephew learns to carry wash water before offering fruit, and the neighbour’s pomegranates receive their turn. As you prepare to leave, Shirin brings out the water list to show you one more change.
ev.ev_tauris_c.choice_2_result: You pay 1.2 silver for the small packet. The nephew wraps the fruit so it will keep on the road, then asks Shirin whether the ants can have the fallen pieces. She tells him to put them well away from the water channel.
ev.ev_tauris_c.choice_3_result: You walk the qanat channels with Shirin and watch her move the gate after each household’s turn. Her neighbour shows you where leaves gather before the water reaches the pomegranates. You record the garden’s way of sharing water.
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.body:
Shirin brings you to the bend where her neighbour’s pomegranate channel branches from the apricots. Her nephew has drawn a new mark on the water-turn list, but he drew it beside the wrong household. The neighbour points it out and asks whether she will lose her turn because of the ink. ‘You will not,’ Shirin says. She has the boy cross out the mark without covering the old one, then read the corrected order aloud.

You ask how far the channel runs toward the road to Ispahan. Shirin says it ends near the dry ground, and travellers must ask again at the next village. Her neighbour knows a family there who keeps a well and offers the name. Meanwhile the nephew has brought another packet of dried fruit, this one prepared for the journey and priced at 5 silver. Shirin asks him to put it somewhere safe from both ants and splashing water. He chooses the high shelf and waits for her approval.
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_1: Buy the travel packet of dried fruit for 5 silver
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 5 silver for the packet. The nephew takes it down from the high shelf, wraps it tightly, and checks that the string will not loosen on the road. Shirin smiles at how carefully he has learned to pack it.
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_2: Ask about the road toward Ispahan
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_2_result: Shirin’s neighbour tells you the family name at the next village well. You mark Ispahan on your map and note where the garden channels end, so you know where to ask again.
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_3: Spend a day helping correct the water-turn list
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day going from household to household with Shirin’s nephew, reading each turn back to its owner. The neighbour’s pomegranates receive their water at the right hour. Shirin thanks you for doing the slow work with him.
ev.ev_tauris_c_followup.title: When the Water Gate Moves
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.body:
When your two days at the tax desk are finished, broker Davud calls you to a long bench by the market. He has a letter for a cloth merchant in another town, but the seal has cracked in his bag. His apprentice says a fresh seal is enough. Davud asks him to read the address first; one line is smudged and they cannot tell which cousin should receive it.

You ask whether the letter can be opened and rewritten. Davud says the sender is still in the city and would rather sign a new copy. His apprentice offers to run back, then remembers he promised to deliver Farah’s corrected ledger page. Davud asks him to finish that errand first. He knows two people on the market street who can witness the new seal when the sender returns.

Davud offers to introduce you to the sender and those witnesses. His apprentice sets the cracked letter safely beneath a cup so it will not blow away, and waits to hear whether you want the introduction.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.choice_1: Meet the sender and the two witnesses
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You ask Davud for the three names and go with him to the sender’s stall. The apprentice catches up after delivering Farah’s page. Together they prepare a fresh letter and ask you to return when the seal is ready.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank Davud and leave the letter with its sender
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank Davud and help return the damaged letter to its sender. The apprentice arrives with Farah’s corrected page, and Davud can turn his attention to the rest of the market.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.title: The Broker at the Long Bench
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a_resolution.bo:
The sender has rewritten the letter, and the two market witnesses are checking the address with Davud. One knows the recipient’s family name; the other knows which street they use when they come to market. They speak over each other at first. Davud asks one to give the name and the other to give the place, then puts both on the page.

You ask who will carry the letter. A caravan messenger is expected before dusk, but he is already loading his animals. The apprentice offers to take the sealed copy to him. Davud says the apprentice must first check that the seal has dried. The sender agrees and places the letter in the shade.

Davud asks whether you would carry the verified letter to the messenger now, or stay a day to help his apprentice with the remaining market notices. The apprentice tests the seal with the back of one finger and waits.

The sender asks the apprentice to check the town name as well. He does, then finally lets the page rest.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a_resolution.ch: Take the sealed letter to the caravan messenger

You deliver the verified letter before the caravan leaves. The messenger reads the address aloud and places it with the other letters. Davud’s apprentice returns to tell the sender it is safely on its way.
Stay a day helping the apprentice with market notices
You stay a day with the apprentice, checking names and street marks on the remaining notices. Davud sends the sealed letter with the caravan himself. By evening the bench is clear of loose papers.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a_resolution.ti: A Fresh Seal for the Letter
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.body:
After your walk through the old lanes, the water keeper at the public well calls you back. Her name is Leyla, and her grandson has found an older stone marker under a pile of repair bricks. He wants to wash it in the well bucket, but Leyla says the drinking water is for the people waiting in line. She gives him a separate basin and asks him to use only what is left from rinsing the jars.

You ask what the marker says. Leyla recognizes a family name but cannot read the worn second line. A neighbour remembers that family’s former house near the east lane. The grandson asks whether they can put the marker back where it came from. Leyla says they must first ask the household now living there; a wall was rebuilt after the old stone was moved.

She offers to show you the well and the east lane on a drawing. The grandson holds the wet marker steady while the neighbour tries to make out one more letter.

A woman waiting for water asks whether the basin will be put back for everyone. The grandson says he will wash it first.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.choice_1: Keep Leyla’s drawing and ask the east-lane household
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You take Leyla’s drawing and ask the household at the east lane about the old marker. They remember it and invite the grandson to bring it by. Leyla says she will come after the well line clears.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the drawing with Leyla and thank her
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You leave the drawing at the well. Leyla places it under a clean stone so her grandson can use it when the line quiets down. The neighbour helps carry the basin away.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.title: At the Public Well
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b_resolution.bo:
The household at the east lane has come to the well to see the marker. Its grandmother recognizes the carved name: her own grandfather lived in the old house before the wall was rebuilt. Her son asks whether the stone belongs in their doorway. Leyla explains where her grandson found it and asks him to show the old brick pile.

You walk with them to the site. The grandmother remembers how the street turned when she was small, and the grandson compares her account with your drawing. Her son suggests keeping the stone by the well, where all the neighbours can see it. Leyla wants the family’s consent before setting it there.

The grandmother nods and asks who will tell the next visitor why the stone matters. Leyla’s grandson looks at you; he has heard the story but wants to be sure he can repeat it.

The grandson traces the carved name with a dry finger, careful not to press too hard on the worn edge.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Help the grandson tell the neighbours the marker’s story

You stand with Leyla’s grandson while he tells the neighbours whose name is on the stone and why it moved. The east-lane grandmother corrects one detail and thanks you both. People at the well remember your part in bringing them together.
Stay a day making a clear note beside the well
You spend a day checking the family account and writing a clear note for the well. Leyla’s grandson reads it back to the grandmother. She approves it, and the marker is set where visitors can see it.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b_resolution.ti: The Stone in the East Lane
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days matching your loads to the tax ledger. Farah’s brother helps carry the heavy bale to the scale; the porter shows you where to wait in the shade. When the record is complete, a broker asks whether you need another name in the market.
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day following the porter through lanes his grandmother described. Where an old wall has been repaired, he shows you the difference in brick. At the public well a water keeper asks what you have learned and offers her own family’s account.
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_3_result: You spend the day weighing and tying Farah’s full bale, then pay 145.8 silver. Her brother reads the corrected tag back to you. The steel is yours, and Farah records the transaction in her ledger.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice.choice_1_r: You study the marked dice for seven days and pay 70 silver. The teacher asks you to name each sign before casting and records the result you read aloud. Lucia’s nephew comes over to compare it with his little diagram.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice.choice_2_r: The dice teacher shows you the signs on his board and asks you to describe one without looking. You remember more than you expected; he adds the part you missed.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.b:
The dice teacher has laid his marked board on the same bench where Lucia’s nephew repairs card boxes. The nephew asks whether the dice can settle an argument about the southern road. The teacher says the dice can give them a way to talk about it, and asks him what he actually knows of the road to Ormus. ‘Only what the caravan family said,’ the boy admits.

You ask to check those directions yourself. The teacher calls over a traveller who has carried a load south and asks her to point out the last well. She moves the nephew’s mark one space on the map. He wants to know why his sketch was wrong; she explains which hill hides the well from the road. The teacher sets the dice down and asks whether you want to keep a record of this cast, note the road, or spend another day practicing how to read the signs. The traveller stays to hear your answer.

The nephew asks the traveller to draw the hill herself. She does, and gives him the charcoal to finish the road.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.c: Record this cast in your own notes
You draw the dice as they landed and write the teacher’s explanation beside them. The nephew checks the marks against the board. The record is yours to use when you practice again.
Ask the southbound traveller about Ormus
The traveller shows you Ormus on your map and corrects the last well’s position. The teacher lets his nephew ask one more question about the hidden hill before she goes.
Spend a day practicing with the marked dice
You spend a day practicing with the teacher. At dusk the nephew can name every mark too, though he still draws the well too large. The teacher thanks you for helping him take the lesson seriously.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.t: A Second Look at the Dice
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.body:
When you return to Lucia’s table, her nephew has finally drawn both roads on one card. The lines meet at a well and separate again. He asks whether that makes the drawing clearer. Lucia says it tells a better story, though the traveller still has to decide where to go. The nephew points out that his well is too large; the real one is no bigger than a thumb.

You ask about the southern road toward Ormus. Lucia knows a caravan family who carried goods that way and says they can show you the port on a map. She has also made a clean copy of the nephew’s card and offers it as a keepsake from your lessons. A visitor at the next table wants to hear how people plan a sea journey; Lucia invites you to stay for the day and explain what you have seen. The nephew turns his card around and waits for your opinion of the two roads.

Lucia tells the boy the well can stay large on his own card if that helps him remember it. He grins.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: You take the card Lucia copied. Her nephew signs the back beside the little well, and she asks you to bring a story when you return to town.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask the caravan family about the road to Ormus
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: Lucia introduces you to the caravan family. They point out Ormus and the last inland water stop on your map. Her nephew moves his painted well to match the real one more closely.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_3: Spend a day talking with travellers at Lucia’s table
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You spend a day comparing travellers’ accounts at Lucia’s table. One woman explains how she packed for the sea, and her son adds what she forgot. Lucia thanks you for letting everyone finish their story.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.title: Lucia’s Last Card
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_1_resul: You pay 60 silver and study with Lucia for ten days. Her nephew brings fresh examples from the travellers at supper, and Lucia makes you explain each picture in plain words. At the end she invites you to return to the table.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_2_resul: You study the other table’s star dice for seven days and pay 70 silver. Lucia’s nephew helps you compare the marks on the dice with the small diagram beside them. The teacher asks you to return once you have tried reading one cast yourself.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_3_resul: Lucia spreads the cards and asks what you see before she offers her reading. Her nephew gives a different answer; she lets you compare them. You leave understanding how she talks about the pictures.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_1_result: You stay for the day. Yuhanna’s daughter reads the page herself by evening, and her father lets her tell the visitor’s tale in her own words. You remember the families named in the church record.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_2_result: Yuhanna and his daughter show you where the roads divide toward Cambaluc and Cacanfu. She checks the spelling of both place names before you mark them on your map.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_3_result: You give 1.2 silver for lamp oil. Yuhanna’s daughter enters the gift in her book and the woman who came to borrow oil thanks you. The church family treats you as a welcome visitor.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.body:
After the evening gathering, Yuhanna’s daughter is copying a list of households that lend water or shelter to travellers. The woman who borrowed oil comes back with the empty bottle and says one name on the list is missing. Her sister has taken in a family whose wagon broke beyond the west well. Yuhanna asks his daughter to add the sister’s house, but she first wants to hear the name from the woman herself.

You ask how the list is used. Yuhanna says a stranger can carry it from post to post and know whom to ask when the weather turns. His daughter asks whether the roads to Cambaluc and Cacanfu should be shown on the same page. The woman says the water stops matter as much as the towns. They set out another sheet, and Yuhanna lets you look over the names while his daughter sharpens her pen.

The daughter asks whether the missing house has a well. The woman says the well is shallow but her sister keeps a full jar by the door. ‘Then I’ll mark the jar,’ the daughter says. Yuhanna reminds her to ask whether it is there through winter too; the woman says she will confirm before the page travels farther.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_1: Copy the roads and water stops on the list
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_1_result: You copy the roads toward Cambaluc and Cacanfu, including the water stops named by the woman. Yuhanna’s daughter checks the house names with you before you fold the sheet.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_2: Give 1.2 silver for lamp oil and travel supplies
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_2_result: You give 1.2 silver for oil and supplies kept for visitors. The woman offers to carry part of it to her sister’s house; Yuhanna’s daughter enters both gifts in the book. People here remember your care.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to copy the household list
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day copying the list. The daughter reads each name back to its speaker, and the woman corrects her sister’s doorway mark. By evening the page is ready for another traveller.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.title: After the Evening Reading
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_1_result: You spend a day watching the sellers settle their marks and counts. Sira’s cousin makes fewer corrections by evening, and the neighbour finally recognizes his new hand. You record how the market works.
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_2_result: You pay 108 silver for the full bale. Sira and her cousin check the fresh label with you before tying it to the cloth. The weaver offers to help you balance the load, glad the mark is right this time.
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_3_result: The grain trader tells you where to take water on the northern road and points out Egrigaia on your map. Sira adds the name of a household there that receives cloth from this market.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_1_result: Miriam records your name and lets you pass. Her father refills your cup, and the young cousin waits his turn with the bundle. You know where to return if you need the posting books.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Miriam and the seller comparing the market mark with the posting book. The cousin had copied the right sign onto the wrong bundle. He redraws it, the seller gets her cloth back, and you learn how the yard keeps track of travellers and goods.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_3_result: You hold the ribbon while the family ties it securely to the roadside stones. The grandmother thanks you and tells her grandson to leave space for the next traveller’s strip. They remember your help.
ev.ev_tiju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping and mark Tiju on your map.
ev.ev_tiju_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at Tiju's salt fields, record what the worker says in your travel book, and mark the city on your map.
ev.ev_trapezus_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Tamar and move on. Davit runs up from the boats just in time to catch the cloak Ana tosses him. You mark Trebizond on your map before taking the next street.
ev.ev_trapezus_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Tamar and Ana, walking from the houses down to the water. A sailor who has crossed toward Caffa names the places where he has stopped, and Ana asks him to repeat the unfamiliar ones. You mark Trebizond, Caffa, and the sea route between them on your map. At dusk Davit returns to try his cloak; Tamar adjusts the hem while you finish your notes. You leave the next morning.
ev.ev_tripolis_entry.choice_1_result:
Hassan wipes his sticky hand on the sailcloth and points towards the road along the coast. "Leave by that gate. You can reach the next station before dark." His sister adds, "There is a well with a whitewashed rim. Fill your water there."

You make a note of the gate and pass through the carts. Hassan has gone back to folding the cloth.
ev.ev_tripolis_entry.choice_2_result:
You hold up the cloth while Hassan gathers the spilled sugar in its centre. A carpenter replaces the bottom board, then the brother and sister put the sugar back. His sister draws her little moon on the crate again. She watches until the sailors set it safely aboard.

The two give you space to rest in the shed. In the morning Hassan says the southbound caravan has just left through the sea gate. After a night's rest, you feel stronger.
ev.ev_tyrus_entry.choice_1_result: You drink, thank Salma, and continue along the coast. Her brother runs after you to point out the turn past the old stones. You mark Tyre and the shore road on your map.
ev.ev_tyrus_entry.choice_2_result: You stay at the shelter for the day. Salma lets you rest under the cloth while she finishes the sandal. By evening her brother has walked the whole shore in it and returned to show that the seam has held. Salma shares warm food with you, and you sleep there before leaving the next morning. Your strength returns, and you mark Tyre on your map.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.body: A broker at the canal landing has found that rain reached one roll of fine silk. His apprentice wants to put it back with the dry ones before the owner notices. ‘The damp will spread if we pack them together,’ the broker says. He asks her to undo the wrapper without pulling the threads. You hold the dry end while she lifts the wet edge onto a clean board. A merchant waiting to buy silk sees the work and asks whether any of the other rolls are sound. The apprentice brings a sealed one from the shelf and shows him the intact wrapper. He says he will buy it once he has checked its length. The broker gives his apprentice a second board and asks her to leave space between the rolls. She wants to know whether the damp one can be sold later; he says they must let it dry and inspect the colour first. You can spend a day helping with that work, or buy the verified dry roll from the merchant’s stock now.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_a: Spend a day drying and checking the silk
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_a_result: You stay another day, lifting each section of damp silk onto clean boards while the apprentice checks the colour. The broker shows both of you how to spot water marks before a roll is packed. He thanks you in front of the buyers, and his apprentice lets you inspect the final list.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_b: Buy a verified dry roll of silk
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_b_result: The merchant measures a dry roll with you, then ties its wrapper shut. You pay for the full piece and take it with you. The broker keeps the damp silk separate until it can be checked again.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.title: The Damp Silk Roll
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.body: A ginger seller has brought his bags to the ferry, but the boat is not ready to load. His younger cousin wants to stack them directly on the damp bank. ‘Put the boards down first,’ the seller says. He has promised the buyer that the ginger will arrive dry. The cousin asks why one bag is lighter than the rest. A seam has opened and a few roots have fallen out. You help collect them while the seller finds a needle. The ferryman calls that a crossing is possible now, but only people and light parcels can go before the heavier cargo. The seller asks the cousin to decide whether to wait and mend every bag or pay to put the smaller parcel on the early ferry. The cousin says she will mend first, because the buyer will count the roots on arrival. You can spend the next day helping the family load the full shipment and earn a share of the work, or pay the ferryman for a place in the early boat and ask him to show you the route toward Sindafu.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_a: Spend a day loading the ginger shipment
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_a_result: You stay another day and help the seller move the repaired bags onto dry boards before they go aboard. The cousin checks each seam. Once the shipment is counted, the seller pays you for the work and tells the ferryman who helped him keep his promise.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_b: Pay for an early crossing and directions
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_b_result: You pay the ferryman for a place on the early boat. As he takes the craft across, he points out the road toward Sindafu and names the next place to ask for water. The cousin waves from the bank, still sewing the last ginger bag.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.title: Ginger Bags at the Ferry
ev.ev_unique_caiju.body: At a grain warehouse near Caiju’s waterway, a clerk has found two sacks with the same painted mark. The boat owner insists they came from different farms. His older son knows which sack he carried first, but the mark has smeared where rain touched it. ‘We can weigh them and ask the farm hands,’ the clerk says. The son asks whether that will delay the boat. The owner tells him to finish the count before promising a departure. You help turn the sacks so the seams can be checked. One is stitched with black thread, the other with pale hemp. The clerk writes the difference beside each entry and asks the owner to read the names aloud. A carter waiting at the door has a list of carts leaving for Chinghianfu. He offers to copy the road stops for a small fee while the warehouse family completes its count. The son wants to keep learning the tally work; he asks whether you will stay a day to help him compare the remaining sacks.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_a: Stay a day and check the grain tally
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_a_result: You spend another day with the clerk and the son, turning sacks to check their stitching before each mark is read. By the final load the son can tell the two farms apart. The clerk thanks you in front of the waiting owners, and you understand how the warehouse keeps its accounts.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_b: Pay for the carter’s road list
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_b_result: You pay the carter for a copy of his road list. He marks the way toward Chinghianfu and the place where his carts rest. The son brings the corrected grain list to the door as you leave.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.title: The Warehouse Tally Board
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.body: A weaver has set gold thread beside an unfinished cloth. His apprentice has wound one bobbin too tightly, and the thread pulls against the pattern. ‘I wanted every turn to match,’ she says. He asks her to feel how the thread moves when he loosens it a little. You hold the bobbin while she tries again. A buyer arrives with a sample of the cloth he ordered. He wants to know why a narrow strip costs more than a wider plain one. The weaver lays the sample beside the loom and shows the small turns where the gold thread must be guided by hand. His apprentice points out how often they have to stop and adjust it. The buyer says he will wait until they finish measuring the next section. The weaver could use your help for a day winding and checking thread; he also offers a paid lesson on how he counts materials and labour before naming a price.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_a: Spend a day winding the thread
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_a_result: You stay another day at the loom, handing the weaver evenly wound thread while his apprentice watches the pattern. He shows you how to feel a snag before the cloth is damaged. The family thanks you for helping finish a difficult section, and their buyer learns your name.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_b: Pay for a lesson on cloth prices
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_b_result: You pay the weaver for his time. He lays out the plain and gold-thread samples, counts the material used in each, and shows where the extra handwork appears. His apprentice checks your figures, leaving you better able to judge the next cloth offered for sale.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.title: The Loom’s Gold Thread
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.body: At Chinginju, carts bring game and silk to a crowded market. A stall keeper asks for help sharing food with newly arrived travellers. A hunter offers a prepared meal for the road.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.choice_a_result: You spend a day carrying food to the new arrivals. People in the market know your face, and you learn to meet strangers with care.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.choice_b_result: You pay 240 silver. The hunter packs a hearty meal and shows how to keep it dry, giving you strength for the next stage.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.title: The Market at First Light
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.body: The grain fleet has filled the canal at Coigangiu. A boatman needs an oarsman for a hard day against the current; a pilot offers a place on the leading boat for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_a: Row against the current for pay
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day at the oars and earn 200 silver. Your arms ache, but the boat families remember you.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_b: Pay to ride with the pilot
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_b_result: You pay 180 silver. From the leading boat you see the waterway toward Paukin and learn its turns.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.title: One More Boat for the Fleet
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.body: Merchandise arriving by the Caramoran is checked at Coiganju before it is sent onward. A river clerk needs help sorting crate marks. The office also issues a sealed trade note for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_a_result: You spend a day matching marks to the river ledger. The clerk pays 150 silver and remembers your careful work.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_b: Pay for a sealed trade note
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_b_result: You pay 260 silver. The clerk enters your name in the office book; local merchants accept your seal and you understand their accounts better.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.title: At the River Office
ev.ev_unique_etzina.body: Outside Etzina, camels drink before the road reaches the sandy desert. A herder asks you to mend the straps on his waterskins. A driver offers to show the next known stopping place before he leaves.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_a: Mend the waterskins and fill your own
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_a_result: You spend a day checking seams and filling skins. You recover strength for the desert and learn to prepare the journey.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_b: Pay the driver to mark the next stop
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_b_result: You pay 160 silver. The driver marks the known road toward Egrigaia and tells you where to keep water close.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.title: The Camel Yard
ev.ev_unique_fuju.body: At Fuju, shipwrights lower a new hull toward the broad river. The ropes strain under its weight. One worker asks for help with the hard launch; another offers to show how ships leave the river for the coast.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_a: Take a rope at the launch
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_a_result: You spend a hard day steadying the hull and earn 220 silver. Your strength is spent, but the yard workers respect your help.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_b: Pay to study the river exit
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. A shipwright points out the passage toward Zayton and explains where the deep water begins.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.title: A Hull on the Great River
ev.ev_unique_linju.body: Linju has both busy workshops and men trained for war. A veteran offers to drill you in watching road traffic. A hunter sells a fresh meal for a traveller who needs to regain strength.
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_a: Spend a day learning the watch
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_a_result: You spend a day tracing the roads with the veteran. The watchmen accept you, and your sense of travel improves.
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_b_result: You pay 190 silver and eat well before setting out. You regain strength for the next stage.
ev.ev_unique_linju.title: A Soldier’s Market
ev.ev_unique_mien.body: After the long road into Mien, you find the towers raised for former kings. A keeper will recount how they came to be built. A porter offers to lead you back through the difficult approaches for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_a: Stay and hear the keeper’s account
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_a_result: You spend a day hearing the story and copying what you can verify. Your care with other people’s accounts grows.
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_b: Hire the porter for the return approach
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. The porter points out the safer way toward Sindafu and saves you from guessing at the mountain forks.
ev.ev_unique_mien.title: The Two Royal Towers
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.body: In Nanghin, silk and gold cloth pass a table where duty is collected. A clerk will teach you to reckon the rolls if you stay. Or you may pay for a sealed passage note.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_a: Study the duty ledger for a day
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_a_result: You spend a day matching each roll to its mark. You earn no wage, but learn how duties change a merchant’s margin.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_b: Pay for the sealed passage note
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_b_result: You pay 230 silver. The clerk seals your note, and merchants at the gate treat you as a known traveller.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.title: The Silk Duty Table
ev.ev_unique_paukin.body: Water spreads on both sides of the stone causeway into Paukin. A cart has stopped where a wheel slips against the stones. Its driver asks for help with the heavy lift; a guide offers to walk the raised road with you.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_a: Help lift the cart from the stones
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day freeing the wheel. Your strength falls, but the driver tells the gate workers who helped him.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_b: Pay the guide to walk the causeway
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_b_result: You pay 150 silver. The guide shows where the stones hold firm and marks the onward road toward Tiju.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.title: The Stone Causeway
ev.ev_unique_pentam.body: A larger vessel waits beyond the shallow water. Its pilot has borrowed a small boat to test the channel, but the sounding line is knotted where two lengths were joined. His daughter says the old knots have swollen and the marks are now hard to read. ‘If we call the depth wrong, the captain will send the big ship too early,’ she says. The pilot asks her to take the end of the line while he loosens the worst knot. You offer to hold the little boat against the quay. A deckhand from the large ship arrives with a message: their cargo is ready, and the captain wants a departure time. The pilot refuses to guess. He points to a pale rock that will disappear beneath the rising tide. His daughter has been watching it all morning and can tell the deckhand how quickly the water is coming in. The pilot offers to wait until she has checked the channel through a full tide, or to take you in the little boat now for a paid sounding of the route toward Java Major.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_a: Stay a day and check the channel with them
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_a_result: You spend another day with the pilot and his daughter, comparing the line’s marks with the water over the pale rock. She records where the boat can turn without touching bottom. When the captain returns, she gives him the depth she measured herself, and you carry away a steadier sense of how the channel changes.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_b: Pay for a sounding trip with the pilot
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_b_result: You pay the pilot for a place in the small boat. He takes the sounding line, calls each depth to his daughter, and points out the passage toward Java Major while she writes the turns down. At the quay she gives you a copy, with the dangerous shallow marked clearly.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.title: The Pilot’s Sounding Line
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.body: The river divides Sindafu into its old parts, and bridge traffic is heavy. A boatman asks for help securing his mooring ropes. Another offers a dry boat crossing for a small fee.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.choice_a_result: You spend a day at the river and earn 150 silver. The boatmen remember your care with their ropes.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.choice_b_result: You pay 190 silver. The boatman spares you the muddy bridge queue; you recover strength during the quiet crossing.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.title: Between the River Bridges
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.body: At Sinjumatu a southern river is divided for the boats that carry trade onward. A foreman asks you to spend a day settling an argument between crews over the loading order. A pilot sells his channel marks.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_a: Settle the loading order with both crews
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_a_result: You spend a day hearing both crews and agree on turns at the quay. The dock workers trust you, and you grow better at dealing with strangers.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_b: Pay for the pilot’s channel marks
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. The pilot shows the branch toward Coigangiu and how the current changes at the split.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.title: Where the River Divides
ev.ev_unique_tiju.body: At Tiju, sacks of salt arrive from the country between the city and the sea. A salt measurer needs help with a long day of lifting and checking weights. A coastal boatman sells his sailing notes.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day at the scales and earn 190 silver. Your strength falls, but the measurers come to know you.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.choice_b_result: You pay 180 silver. His notes mark the way toward Sinju and sharpen your judgement of a salt cargo.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.title: Salt from the Coast
ev.ev_yarcan_entry.choice_1_result: Nasir names the wells used on the road out of Yarcan. The cobbler returns his boot before you leave, and you mark the town on your map.
ev.ev_yarcan_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day following Nasir’s sister through the cloth stalls and the cobbler’s lane. Her aunt comes for the flowered border at dusk and thanks everyone who kept it aside. You record what you saw of Yarcan.
ev.ev_yarcan_site_gap.choice_1_result: The neighbour names the stopping places toward Cascar and points out where the next water lies. Farida’s son helps you mark the route, then runs back to hold the young tree.
ev.ev_yarcan_site_gap.choice_2_result: Farida lines up the bark and asks you to hold the cloth while her son ties it. The neighbour fills the watering jug. You leave knowing what the family will check when the bud begins to grow.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You stay the night. Hamid’s daughter finds a clean place for your bedding, and in the morning you help her put out bread for the next travellers. Hamid thanks you and speaks warmly of you to his neighbours.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You join the prayers and remain afterward as the travellers share bread. One of them asks where you have come from; soon the room is full of directions and names of old friends. By the time you leave, people here know you well enough to greet you again.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend the day listening as the travellers trace their journey from Isfahan to Yazd. Hamid’s daughter brings out a scrap of paper so you can note the turns and stopping places they remember. You add that stretch of road to your map before you leave.
ev.ev_yasdi_entry.choice_1_result: Roya’s brother points you toward the next street. You mark Yazd on your map and continue.
ev.ev_yasdi_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the weaving rooms and water courtyards. You mark Yazd on your map and write down what you saw in your travel book before leaving.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You take your dinars and dirhems to the changers, for no one in China will deal with you until your coin is changed into the king's notes. Each note is a palm-sized sheet stamped with the king's stamp; twenty-five make a nashhat, a dinar of the place. When the paper grows torn or worn you may carry it to the mint, and receive new notes in its place without interest.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You sit for the painters, and a day passes under their brushes — none in the world come near to them in painting, and your likeness and the likenesses of your companions go up on the walls and on papers stuck about the streets. It is the custom with every stranger who passes through their towns: should any such a one make flight necessary, his picture is sent out to the other provinces, and wherever he is, he is taken.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day watching the clerks of the harbour take down the names and forms of the men aboard each junk before it sails, and when a vessel returns, the servants of the magistrates board her and compare the men with the descriptions; a missing man costs the commander his ship, and goods not entered in the register forfeit ship and cargo to the king — an oppression seen nowhere else. You learn of the river road, twenty-seven days from Sin Kilan, where earthenware is made as here at Zayton, and that the same river runs on toward Kinsay; here the river called the water of life enters the sea, and the place is called the meeting of two seas.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_1_result: You declare your goods to the Kaan's clerks, and their brushes move without pause, recording your cargo in the sea-trade register. A hundred shiploads wait ahead of yours, and the tally runs two full days before the register closes. When it is struck, one clerk draws a second sheet and asks where your road goes next.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_2_result: You call to the fishermen in their own tongue and slip ashore by their steps, and no brush records your coming. But the tithe clerks will remember the merchant who came ashore undeclared, and the quayside murmurs your name with less welcome. A lamp burns in the watch-house above the quay, and the night watch keeps its own account of every shadow.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_3_result: You ask a boatman what all these ships are, and he answers as only a man who reads the sea can. He can name a hundred ships and a hundred roads, and he offers you the two that matter.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_4_result: A traveller from the West asks leave to handle the king's paper money, and tells of the registry of ships and the painters who draw every stranger's face; he would tell you more of it, if you will listen.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_1_result: You ask the Persian traders about the sea road, and they answer in a tongue you are learning to follow. One of them, an old merchant, calls for tea and offers you the bargain that the quarter keeps for strangers of good faith.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_2_result: You pay a lad of the foreign quarter to interpret for a season, and spend twenty days in his company. The Arabic tongue now sits in your mouth, and your purse is lighter by three thousand pieces.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_3_result: You pay twelve thousand pieces for a bolt of silk from a Manzi weaver and roll it into your cargo. The finest silk of the south now rides with you.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.body: In the foreign quarter, the merchant who heard you bargain sends word to your lodging: a bolt of silk has come from the weaver's own loom, and it is offered first to you. He sets it out beside the well where the merchants of three tongues meet. The price is the weaver's price, he says, and the bargain is yours to close — or you may ask instead what the sea-merchants know of the road they do not speak of at the quay.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_1: Buy the bolt at the weaver's price
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_1_r: The bolt is fine Manzi silk, heavier in the hand than it looks, and you carry it out of the quarter wrapped in oiled cloth. At the weaver's price it is a bargain worth the telling; the quarter watches you go, and its judgment is recorded.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_2: Ask the sea-merchants of the lane to Chamba
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_2_r: A merchant of the Indian sea draws the lane in the dust with his finger, mark by mark — the monsoon's turning, the days of open water, the haven at the end. Chamba is now named on your map, and the road that serves it.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_3: Let the quarter learn your name
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_3_r: You bargain plainly and speak plainly, and the quarter marks you for an honest man. Among the merchants of the sea-lands your name will be repeated before you are seen again.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_4: Copy the wonder-leaves and road chronicles
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_4_r: The scholars lend you their stack of papers. By lamplight you copy Prester John beside Wang Dayuan, paradise beside Zhenla, and the mountain crossings of the two pilgrims — a richer book of the road than you carried out.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.title: Zayton: The Quarter's Bargain
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_1_result: You buy a sack of pepper at the quayside price, and the merchant slaps the sack as it is weighed. But the price he names is not the whole bargain; he keeps you a moment to speak of the freight ledger.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_2_result: You stand the pilots a drink and ask about the winds. A day passes in good talk, and the monsoon's law — and the sea-road to Chamba — are now on your map.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_3_result: You spend the day watching the ships come in — a hundred at a time, they say, when the season is full. The haven of Zayton is now marked in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.body: The warehouseman who weighed your pepper at the quay finds you again by the customs shed. He has seen how you counted the shipping, and he does what his kind do for a man they trust: he lays open his own reckoning. Freight, he says, is the harbour's second tongue. Small wares pay thirty in the hundred, bulky goods forty, and pepper four and forty — and then the Kaan's tamghā on top. He offers to let you take a sack at the price the merchants pay among themselves. He will not hold it past the turning of the tide.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_1: Buy the sack at the merchants' own price
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_1_r: The warehouseman weighs out a sack and lets you have it at the price merchants pay among themselves, the tamghā already reckoned in. Pepper in hand, you know the freight reckoning as the merchants know it — and you know the rate that will follow you to every quay of the Indian sea.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_2: Ask which season the wind turns toward Chamba
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_2_r: The warehouseman points south across the water, where the ships lie waiting. When the monsoon turns, he says, the lane to Chamba opens; a ship that misses it waits a season. The lane is now on your map, and the season that serves it.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_3: Stand another day among the masts
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_3_r: You spend another day on the quay, among masts that stand like a burnt forest, watching the ships of India come in. The day is gone before the last one is moored; after you leave, whenever you look at the sea, this haven is what you see.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.title: Zayton: The Freight Reckoning
ev.ev_zayton_jiaobei_ask.choice_1_result: You cast the two cups before the shrine and wait while they settle their answer. The reading is given, and the shrine keeps your name.
ev.ev_zayton_jiaobei_ask.choice_2_result: You pass the temple-shrine without casting the cups. The goddess's answer stays unasked, and the slip stays in the cylinder.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence.choice_1: You keep the clerk's fair copy of the duty ledger, and your hand rests on the margin where Kinsay and the coastal road are noted. The ledger has given you a road to think about.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence.choice_2: You let the cargo alone be entered and take no copy. The clerk dips his brush once more and closes the book; a coldness settles on the table that has nothing to do with the ink.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence_resoluti: By carrying the sealed copy of the duty ledger, you carry Zayton's own mark upon your cargo. It will not decide the whole journey, but wherever the Kaan's clerks keep their tables, the seal will speak before you do.
Present the copy to the harbour-master before nightfall
The harbour-master reads the seal by lamplight and marks your name cleared in his own book. The copy has done its work; Zayton's harbour will not hold you back again.
Keep the copy safe in your travel book
You spend a day setting the copy down fair in your travel book. The seal's work is preserved for the road, though the writing costs you a day.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_1_result: You make your offering before the sea goddess, and the smoke of the paper rises straight in the still air. The temple keeper watches the reading of your slip, and does not turn away as you rise to leave.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_2_result: You shake the cylinder and draw a slip before the shrine of the sea-goddess. The answer is read aloud, and the sailors watch to see how you take it.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_3_result: You stand at the back and watch the sailors at their prayers before the sea-goddess. The way of the sea-folk is now written in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.body: The slip-reader at the temple door calls you back from the stair. The goddess does not count an offering once, she says; she asks again before every sailing, and a fleet is making ready below. The sailors are already on the hill, burning paper and setting out rice and wine. There is still room at the door for one more who means to ask.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_1: Make an offering before the fleet sails
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_1_resu: You burn paper at the goddess's feet and set out a dish of rice and a cup of wine, as the shipmasters do. She looks south over the water and does not refuse you; the sea road is kinder to you for the asking.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_2: Draw a slip for the sailing
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_2_resu: You shake the cylinder until a slip falls, and the reader reads it against the book of verses. It names a day when the wind will serve you — and the lane to Chamba is named with it. You mark the day and go down to the water.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_3: Stay and watch the sailors ask
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_3_resu: You stay a day on the temple hill while the sailors come and go, each one asking in his own way. The smoke of the sea-temple goes with you when you leave, and you carry the memory of what asking is.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.title: Zayton: The Temple Asks Again
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_1_result: You sit with the old woman at the temple door and give what you can to the temple. She watches your hands as you take up the cylinder, and she begins to teach you as she has taught forty years of readers.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_2_result: You sit with the old woman and ask to learn the cups. She looks at you a long moment, then sets the two cups on the threshold and begins, for the three answers have their own order.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_3_result: The reader of the slips shows how the slips are read by their order and their marks. The art of the lots is now in your book, though the shaking stays with her.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.body: The old woman who reads the slips will not let you leave with only what you have learned. She reaches for the cylinder and draws one slip for your voyage, but she does not read it aloud. The slips tell a man what he has not considered, she says; you have sat with her long enough to read your own. She holds it out and lets you choose how to carry it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take the slip she draws for your voyage
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: She reads the slip once, then presses it into your hand: a day to sail, and counsel you now know how to read for yourself. The reading is yours, and the day with it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask her which road the slips favour
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: She shakes the cylinder until it answers, and reads what falls: the slips counsel the monsoon lane to Chamba, and the sea-goddess's favour with it. The road is drawn on your map, and the counsel carried in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_3: Leave silver for the temple lamps
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You leave silver for the lamps that burn at the goddess's feet and take your leave of the reader. The blessing of the temple goes with you down the hill, and the smoke of it after you to the water.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.title: Zayton: The Reader's Parting Counsel
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.bod: The temple attendant who taught you the throwing of the cups waylays you at the gate. He sets a pair of half-moons of wood before you and bids you throw for the voyage you are about to make. The cups fall, and he does not smile or frown: a throw is a throw, he says, and a verdict is a verdict. Choose how to carry it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.cho: Keep the verdict as a ward for the journey
He wraps the two cups in a cloth and presses them into your hand. Whatever the throw promised, the carry itself is a protection, and you will know how to read it at any campfire.
Ask the cups which road to take from the port
He throws again and reads the falling cups: the sea road to Java is favoured, the goddess's lane open. The course is drawn on your map and the verdict kept in your book.
Wait a day and let the cups settle in your own hand
You sit with the two cups through an afternoon, learning their weight, and leave them with the temple at dusk. The attendant remembers your patience, and the quarter speaks well of you.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.tit: Zayton: The Three Cups at Parting
ev.ev_zayton_pilot_consequence.choice_1_: You ask after the monsoon lane, and the pilot draws the southern line again, deeper. He names the days of the season when it runs, and Chamba settles on your map like a ship coming to anchor.
ev.ev_zayton_pilot_consequence.choice_2_: You ask after the inland road, and the pilot sets down his cup and speaks of it as a man speaks of a road he knows in the dark. The way north to Fuju is now written in your book, and your name in his.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence.choice_1_: You pay the late-declaration fee on the watch-table, and the tally is marked paid. The watch leaves your cargo in your keeping, but they have written your name down twice.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence.choice_2_: You leave the cargo for two days' inspection. The watch goes through the bales without haste and marks each one in their book; in the waiting you come to know the rounds of the quay by heart.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence_resolutio: By carrying the watch's tally, you carry the receipt of a debt settled in the dark. It will not decide the whole journey, but at the next quay the tally says you have already paid your reckoning at Zayton.
Enter the tally at the quay office before nightfall
The quay clerk strikes the tally through and writes your name in the paid column. The night's mischance is closed, and the ledger holds no shadow against you.
Keep the tally in your travel book
You spend a day copying the tally and its reason into your travel book. The reckoning is recorded for the road ahead, though it costs you a day.
ev.fuju.entry.body: Now this city of Fuju is the key of the kingdom which is called CHONKA, and which is one of the nine great divisions of Manzi. The city is a seat of great trade and great manufactures. The people are Idolaters and subject to the Great Kaan. And a large garrison is maintained there by that prince to keep the kingdom in peace and subjection. For the city is one which is apt to revolt on very slight provocation. There flows through the middle of this city a great river, which is about a mile in width, and many ships are built at the city which are launched upon this river.
ev.fuju.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.fuju.entry.title: Concerning the Greatness of the City of Fuju
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.body:
The ferryman reaches into the water with a long hook and fishes out a wooden ladle. Three short lines are cut into its handle. He wipes it on his sleeve and shows it to a child on the bank. "Look, the river brought my ladle back."

The child knocks a heel against the stone step. "You used that to serve me bean soup this morning." The ferryman clears his throat and puts away the hook. A driver on the bridge calls for space to turn his cart, so the ferryman takes the child's hand and moves her away from the wheels. She points at the marks again. "Did you carve them?"

A woman carrying soup pots comes down the steps. She asks the ferryman whether the ladle is clean enough for the noon meal and sends the child to fetch a cloth. The child comes back with one that smells of mint and rubs the handle carefully. The woman says the ladle has served soup here for years. Each time the child asks about the marks, the ferryman tells a different story and then goes back to work. She gives the clean ladle to the child and asks her to get the whole story this time. The covered cart is still easing across the bridge, and the child also wants to know where it is going.
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.choice.route: "Is the cart for Berrhoea waiting on the bridge too?"
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.result.route:
The ferryman nods towards the far end of the bridge. "The cart with the blue cover is going to Berrhoea. Wait until it gets across, then ask the driver whether he'll take someone along."

The child returns the ladle. "Did you drop it in again?" The ferryman winks at you. "I pulled it out myself this time. The river hasn't learned to do my work yet."
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.result.talk:
The ferryman gives the ladle to the child. "Your father made them. One mark for each bowl of soup. He says I serve too much, so he keeps count." The child traces the marks and asks why he threw it in the river today.

"Slipped out of my hand." The child laughs and runs up the steps with it. The ferryman calls after him, "Tell your father he still owes me those three bowls!"
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.title: A Ladle Caught at the Bridge
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.body:
At a bread stall by the canal, a young woman who carries grain holds two loaves and hesitates. Amin, the baker, looks at his board. "I only took payment for one, didn't I?"

She tells him the other is the loaf he promised her little brother this morning. Amin remembers. "He came early. He said you had to cross the river and might miss lunch." She asks whether the second loaf can wait in the oven until the boy returns from school.
